- When the key is missing, `set_unrestricted` appends `key=value` after the last line. If that line ends with a dangling `\` and no newline, Ephervex adds a newline and the appended entry becomes a continuation of the previous value for Java.

`merge_network` (called by core at create, install, network change, and every start) rewrites only the entry this parser considers effective. Java can then read a different value.

## Reproduction

Merge the default network settings (offline mode, `127.0.0.1`, port 25565) and load the result with OpenJDK 25 `Properties.load`:

| Input | Ephervex `get("server-ip")` | Java `server-ip` |
|---|---|---|
| `server-ip=10.0.0.1\n# note \\\nserver-ip=\n` | `127.0.0.1` | empty |
| `online-mode=false\nmotd=hello\\` (no final newline) | `127.0.0.1` | unset (`motd=helloserver-ip=127.0.0.1`) |

An empty or unset `server-ip` makes Minecraft bind all interfaces.

## Expected

The typed network settings stay authoritative over what Minecraft actually reads. Logical-line handling follows the `java.util.Properties` format.

## Impact

An offline-mode server binds all interfaces while Ephervex believes it is localhost-only, and the `OfflineModeExposed` warning is not emitted. Any host that can reach it can join under any name, including the operator name Ephervex writes to `ops.json`. `online-mode` and `server-port` can be overridden the same way.

Preconditions: a malformed or crafted `server.properties`, for example one preserved from an imported server pack. Minecraft rewrites the file on its first save, so the exposure mainly affects the first run.

## Locations

- `crates/server/src/properties.rs` `PropertiesDocument::logical_entries`, lines 164-176
- `crates/server/src/properties.rs` `is_continued`, lines 243-252
- `crates/server/src/properties.rs` `PropertiesDocument::set_unrestricted`, lines 143-162

## Test gap

The properties tests round-trip well-formed input only. Nothing compares the result against Java's reading of the same bytes.
issues.title: server.properties continuation handling lets file content override the typed network settings

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-server`

**Commit:** `0145a4a7da8b701dc49f277adc07291fa0c11096`

## Behavior

Console writes are wrapped in a 5-second timeout, but the Stop and Restart arms write `stop\n` with a plain `.await` inside the `select!`. If the child is not reading stdin and the pipe is full, that await blocks the whole supervision loop: exit polling stops and later requests, including Kill, are never handled.

## Reproduction

1. Supervise `exec sleep 1000` (never reads stdin).
2. Send a 65,533-byte Console command. It is accepted because it fits in the pipe buffer.
3. Send Stop, then Kill.

Kill gets no answer within 3 s and the child keeps running. After a manual SIGKILL of the child, the blocked write fails and supervision ends as `Err(BrokenPipe)`.

## Expected

ADR 0014: Kill is available through the live owner channel. Stop and Restart writes are bounded like Console writes, and a write that does not complete does not block Kill or exit detection.

## Impact

Preconditions: about 64 KiB of unread input, or less when the per-user pipe buffer limit is reached. This needs a server whose console reader is stalled, for example during early loading.

## Locations

- `crates/server/src/process.rs` `supervise_child`, lines 396-397 and 412-413 (compare lines 370-374)
issues.title: Stop and Restart stdin writes have no timeout, so a full input pipe blocks Kill

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-server`

**Commit:** `0145a4a7da8b701dc49f277adc07291fa0c11096`

## Behavior

`serve_control` uses `let Ok((stream, _)) = listener.accept().await else { return; }`, so any accept error ends the control service and closes the listener. Transient errors such as EMFILE or ECONNABORTED are enough.

Once the remaining connection tasks drop their senders, `requests.recv()` in `supervise_child` returns `None` on every call. The `None` arm does `continue`, so the `select!` loop spins without waiting.

## Reproduction

With the supervisor process at its file descriptor limit when a control connection arrives (accept fails with EMFILE), then descriptors released:

- Stop returns `ControlUnavailable` (connection refused);
- classification becomes `UnknownRunning` while the child is alive;
- the idle supervisor uses a full CPU core until the child exits.

## Expected

Transient accept errors are retried. A closed request channel does not cause a hot loop.

## Impact

The live server can no longer be stopped, killed, or sent console commands from Ephervex, and it is shown as unknown-running for the rest of the run, while the launcher burns a core.

## Locations

- `crates/server/src/process.rs` `serve_control`, lines 521-531
- `crates/server/src/process.rs` `supervise_child`, lines 345-348

## Limitations

Triggering it needs descriptor exhaustion or another accept error. The behavior after the error follows directly from the code.
issues.title: One failed control-socket accept loses the control channel and busy-spins the supervisor

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-server`

**Commit:** `0145a4a7da8b701dc49f277adc07291fa0c11096`

## Behavior

`PropertiesDocument` decodes and encodes values differently from `java.util.Properties`:

- `unescape` has no `\uXXXX` support, so `\u00A7` becomes `u00A7`.
- `escape_value` does not escape leading whitespace, which Java strips when reading.
- `parse_entry` skips every `=`/`:` after the key, while Java skips at most one, so `motd==x` reads as `x` instead of `=x`.

The desktop Save Server Properties action sends `motd` and six other displayed keys every time, using the values read through `get`, so saving any field rewrites them with the misread value.

## Reproduction

`get` then `set` the same key, then load with OpenJDK 25 `Properties.load`:

| Original line | Written back | Java reads |
|---|---|---|
| `motd=\u00A7aHello` | `motd=u00A7aHello` | `u00A7aHello` (color code lost) |
| `motd=\ \ centered` | `motd=  centered` | `centered` (leading spaces lost) |
| `motd==x` | `motd=x` | `x` (was `=x`) |

## Expected

`get` returns the value Java reads, and `set` writes a value Java reads back unchanged, following the `java.util.Properties` format.

## Impact

Saving server properties in the desktop app corrupts escaped or space-padded MOTDs. Older Minecraft versions write non-ASCII characters as `\uXXXX`, so this affects any MOTD with a color code or other non-ASCII text written by them.

## Locations

- `crates/server/src/properties.rs` `unescape`, lines 306-324
- `crates/server/src/properties.rs` `escape_value`, lines 336-344
- `crates/server/src/properties.rs` `parse_entry`, lines 290-299
issues.title: server.properties value escaping differs from Java, so saving properties corrupts the MOTD

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-server`

**Commit:** `0145a4a7da8b701dc49f277adc07291fa0c11096`

## Behavior

The runtime lock is a file whose existence is the lock (`create_new`). If `.launcher/server-runtime.lock` exists without `server-runtime.json`:

- `classify_runtime` returns `Stopped`, so the server is shown as stopped;
- `RuntimeGuard::acquire` fails `create_new`, classifies again (`Stopped`, not `ProvenStale`) and returns `AlreadyRunning`;
- `clear_stale_runtime` returns `Ok` on `Stopped` without touching the lock, so Repair does nothing.

The state arises when the launcher dies between creating the lock and writing evidence, or between removing the evidence and dropping the guard.

Because the lock is not an OS lock, stale clearing is also check-then-delete. Two starts that both classify the same stale evidence can, with an unlucky interleaving, delete each other's freshly created lock.

## Reproduction

1. Create only `.launcher/server-runtime.lock` in a server root.
2. `classify_runtime` returns `Stopped`, `clear_stale_runtime` returns `Ok`, and `ServerSupervisor::run` returns `AlreadyRunning`.

## Expected

A lock that no live process holds does not block starts, and recovery clears it.

## Impact

The server cannot be started from Ephervex until the user deletes the lock file by hand.

## Locations

- `crates/server/src/process.rs` `RuntimeGuard::acquire`, lines 659-707
- `crates/server/src/runtime.rs` `clear_stale_runtime`, lines 144-168

## Limitations

The windows that leave the file behind are short. The concurrent-start interleaving follows from the code and was not reproduced.

comments.author: MelanX
comments.bodyMarkdown:
Partly addressed by 7b1d50b.

The runtime lock now records the supervisor that holds it, written whole so it is never read empty. `classify_runtime` reads it when there is no runtime file:

- a live holder reports `UnknownRunning`, so a server that is starting or stopping no longer shows as stopped;
- a holder proven dead reports `ProvenStale`, so `RuntimeGuard::acquire` and Repair clear the lock.

Still open:

- A lock written by an earlier version names no holder and behaves as described here.
- Stale clearing is still check-then-delete, so the race between two starts remains.

issues.title: A leftover runtime lock with no runtime file blocks every start and recovery ignores it

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-server`

**Commit:** `0145a4a7da8b701dc49f277adc07291fa0c11096`

## Behavior

`supervise_commands` spawns the child, then captures its identity, then writes and fsyncs the runtime evidence. Until that write completes, the evidence records no child (first start) or the previous, already exited child (restart). There is no parent-death signal, so the child survives if the launcher dies.

If the launcher dies in that window, the evidence shows a dead supervisor and no live recorded child. `classify_runtime` returns `ProvenStale`, so the next start clears it and starts a second server on the same root while the first JVM keeps running unreported.

## Expected

Classification stays conservative while a spawn is in flight: either the child is recorded before it can outlive the supervisor, or a pending spawn prevents the evidence from being proven stale.

## Impact

A launcher crash or kill during the window leaves an untracked server JVM and allows a duplicate start. On modern Minecraft the world session lock and the port bind usually make the duplicate fail.

## Locations

- `crates/server/src/process.rs` `supervise_commands`, lines 226-247
- `crates/server/src/runtime.rs` `classify_runtime` (`ProvenDead` with no or dead child gives `ProvenStale`)

## Limitations

Established from the order of operations. The window is a few milliseconds (spawn, `/proc` capture, fsync), and it was not reproduced with a real crash.
issues.title: A spawned server child is unrecorded until its runtime evidence is written

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-server`

**Commit:** `0145a4a7da8b701dc49f277adc07291fa0c11096`

## Behavior

`OperatorsDocument::parse` deserializes each entry as `OperatorEntry`, which requires `bypassesPlayerLimit` and a `level` that `OperatorPermissionLevel` accepts (1 to 4). Minecraft's operator list entry treats both fields as optional (missing level reads as 0, missing bypass as false) and accepts level 0.

Core `materialize_operator_setup` parses the existing `ops.json` on every start that has an operator setup, and maps a parse failure to an I/O error, so the start fails.

## Reproduction

Parse `ops.json` content with an entry that has `"level": 0`, or that has no `bypassesPlayerLimit` or no `level`. All return `OperatorsDocumentError::Invalid`.

## Expected

`ops.json` files that Minecraft reads are accepted. Fields this document does not change are preserved as they are, while the desired operator is still written with a valid level.

## Impact

A hand-edited or older `ops.json` blocks every start of that server until the user fixes the file by hand. The module itself notes that operators routinely edit this file.

## Locations

- `crates/server/src/operators.rs` `OperatorEntry`, lines 12-21
- `crates/server/src/operators.rs` `OperatorsDocument::parse`, lines 52-55
- `crates/core/src/server.rs` `materialize_operator_setup` (caller)

## Limitations

Minecraft's tolerant defaults are based on knowledge of its operator list entry reader and were not rechecked against a specific Minecraft release here.
issues.title: ops.json parsing rejects operator entries that Minecraft accepts and blocks server starts

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-server`

**Commit:** `0145a4a7da8b701dc49f277adc07291fa0c11096`

## Behavior

Control sockets live in `/tmp/evx-<uid>`, a predictable name in a world-writable directory. `prepare_control_socket_path` only fixes permissions when the existing entry is a directory owned by the current user, and `validate_control_socket_directory` then rejects anything else. That fail-closed check prevents hijacking, but another local user can pre-create `/tmp/evx-<victim uid>` as their own directory or as a symlink.

## Reproduction

As another local user, create `/tmp/evx-<uid of the Ephervex user>`. Every `ServerSupervisor::run` then fails with `RuntimeState` (permission denied), `send_control` fails, and no server can be classified as `Controlled`.

## Expected

The control socket directory is in a per-user location that other users cannot claim, such as `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, or Ephervex falls back to a safe alternative when the predictable path is taken.

## Impact

A local denial of service of every server start on multi-user systems. There is no control hijack.

## Locations

- `crates/server/src/runtime.rs` `control_socket_directory`, `prepare_control_socket_path`, `validate_control_socket_directory`

## Limitations

Established from the code. Not reproduced, because it needs a second local account.
issues.title: Another local user can block all server starts by creating the predictable control directory

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-server`

**Commit:** `0145a4a7da8b701dc49f277adc07291fa0c11096`

## Behavior

When a Restart stops the old child but the replacement fails to spawn, `supervise_commands` answers the restart waiters with `StartFailed` and returns `Ok(last_exit)`. `last_exit` is the old child's exit, recorded with `stop_requested = stopping && !restart`, which is `false` for a restart.

The run's terminal result therefore describes the intended restart stop as an unrequested exit, and does not mention the start failure that actually ended the run:

- with code 0 after startup finished, the run looks like a normal completion;
- with a restart requested during startup, it looks like "stopped before ready";
- with a nonzero stop code, it looks like "exited with error".

## Expected

A logical run has one coherent terminal outcome. A run that ends because its restart replacement could not start reports that failure, not the old child's exit as if nobody had asked it to stop.

## Impact

The desktop app compensates in the common case, because the restart caller receives `StartFailed` and marks the server failed. The core `Finished` exit, the CLI, and the follow-up failure text for a restart during startup still describe the wrong cause.

## Locations

- `crates/server/src/process.rs` `supervise_commands`, lines 232-243 and 258-264
issues.title: A failed restart replacement ends the run with the old child's exit as an unrequested stop

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-server`

**Commit:** `0145a4a7da8b701dc49f277adc07291fa0c11096`

## Behavior

Once the final child's exit has been handled, `supervise_commands` returns without serving requests still queued in the control channel, and `ServerSupervisor::run` drops the receiver. Requests that arrived while output was being drained, or just before the run returned, lose their response sender, so `send_control` returns `InvalidControlResponse`.

## Reproduction

Supervise a child that leaves a short-lived descendant holding its stdout, Stop it, and send Kill while supervision is still draining output. The run ends with `Ok(ServerExit { code: Some(0), stop_requested: true })`, but the Kill gets `Err(InvalidControlResponse)`. The same happens without a descendant when a Stop races a natural exit.

## Expected

Every accepted control request gets an answer. Requests that arrive after the child exited receive the final exit (or a clear refusal) instead of a broken channel.

## Impact

The desktop app reports a failed stop, with an error, for a server that has already stopped.

## Locations

- `crates/server/src/process.rs` `supervise_commands`, lines 253-269
- `crates/server/src/process.rs` `ServerSupervisor::run`, lines 195-210
issues.title: Control requests that arrive as a server run ends are dropped without an answer

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `0145a4a7da8b701dc49f277adc07291fa0c11096`

## Behavior

Launch and Connect waits for readiness with `wait_for_server_readiness`, which succeeds on any successful TCP connection to the server's target. When another process is already listening on that port, core only emits the `PortUnavailable` advisory and starts the server anyway. The foreign listener accepts immediately, typically long before the new JVM tries to bind. Core sees a `Controlled` runtime, reports the server ready, and launches the client with a direct connection to the foreign server. The managed server then fails to bind and exits.

## Scenario

1. Run any server on the managed server's configured port (for example another local server on 25565).
2. Use Launch and Connect for the linked pair.
3. The client connects to the other server.

## Expected

The client is sent to the server Ephervex started. A port that is already bound before the spawn cannot prove readiness, for example by refusing the start when the port is taken, or by tying readiness to the owned child.

## Impact

The client joins the wrong server. New servers get a free port automatically, so this needs a later port collision, which is plausible in a developer tool on the default port.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/connection.rs` `launch_and_connect`, `wait_for_managed_server`
- `crates/core/src/server.rs` network advisories (`PortUnavailable`)
- `crates/server/src/connection.rs` `wait_for_server_readiness` (readiness primitive, behaves as ADR 0015 defines)

## Notes

ADR 0015 defines readiness as a successful TCP connection and states that process-start failure or exit wins over readiness. A foreign listener answers before the managed process exits, so a correction may need to revisit how that ADR treats an occupied port.

## Limitations

Established from the code path. Not reproduced end to end with a real client.

comments.author: MelanX
comments.bodyMarkdown:
Fixed in 04d8a0f.

Readiness now counts a connection only while the server's recorded Java process itself holds every listening socket a connection to the target can reach. The check reads the launcher's own `/proc/self/net/tcp` and `tcp6` and matches their inodes against the child's descriptors, so it covers both a started and a reused server, and a co-listener on the same port (for example `SO_REUSEPORT`) also keeps the server from being reported ready. ADR 0015 and `docs/architecture.md` describe the new rule.

Follow-up: #322 (a distinct, actionable error instead of the generic readiness timeout when another program shares the port).

issues.title: Launch and Connect treats any listener on the server port as the managed server being ready

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-gui`

**Commit:** `0145a4a7da8b701dc49f277adc07291fa0c11096`

## Behavior

Server runs started from the desktop app execute on detached threads. Closing the main window ends `ui.run()` in `main`, and the process exits without stopping running servers. Other threads are not unwound, so the supervisor's `Child` is never dropped and `kill_on_drop` never fires. The server JVM keeps running with its stdin at EOF and its output pipes broken. On the next launch it shows as orphaned, and Ephervex will not stop it.

The only `on_close_requested` handler belongs to the window-size picker.

## Scenario

1. Start a server in the desktop app.
2. Close the main window.
3. The server JVM is still running. After reopening Ephervex, the server is reported as orphaned.

## Expected

A normal quit either stops servers the app supervises (gracefully, then with the best-effort cleanup ADR 0014 describes), or asks the user before leaving them running unsupervised.

## Impact

Every normal quit with a running server leaves an unsupervised JVM holding the world and port. Recovering requires killing it by hand, using the PID Ephervex reports.

## Locations

- `crates/gui/src/main.rs` `main` (`ui.run()`, line 173)
- `crates/gui/src/backend.rs` `spawn_detached_with_setup_failure`
- `crates/gui/src/controller.rs` close handling (the only `on_close_requested`, around line 5848)

## Notes

ADR 0014 accepts that abrupt supervisor termination can leave an orphan "despite best-effort child cleanup", and ADR 0015 says ending the owning process ends supervision. Whether a normal quit should count as that case needs a maintainer decision. Currently no cleanup runs at all on a normal quit.

## Limitations

Established from the code. The desktop app was not run to observe it.
issues.title: Quitting the desktop app leaves running servers orphaned without a stop

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-minecraft`

**Commit:** `0145a4a7da8b701dc49f277adc07291fa0c11096`

## Behavior

A version document that declares `"logging": {}` is parsed as having no logging configuration: `RawVersion` keeps only `logging.client`, which is absent in an empty object, so the result is `None`. `VersionMetadata::inherit` then fills a `None` from the parent with `child.logging.clone().or_else(|| parent.logging.clone())`.

An explicit empty `logging` object and a missing `logging` key are therefore treated the same, and the child's choice to drop the vanilla client logging configuration is lost. Forge version documents declare `"logging": {}`. The merged Forge launch plan carries vanilla's `client-1.12.xml` and the launch adds `-Dlog4j.configurationFile=...`, which replaces Forge's own log4j configuration.

## Reproduction

Parse the `fixtures/minecraft/1.20.1.json` parent and a child version with `"inheritsFrom": "1.20.1"` and `"logging": {}`, then call `VersionMetadata::inherit`:

- parent logging: present;
- child logging after parse: `None`;
- merged logging: `Some(("client-1.12.xml", "-Dlog4j.configurationFile=${path}"))`.

## Expected

An explicit empty `logging` object in the child overrides the parent and leaves the launch without a vanilla logging configuration. Only a missing key inherits the parent's value.

## Impact

Forge clients run with vanilla's log4j configuration instead of Forge's. Forge's `debug.log`, which the Diagnostics view relies on (ADR 0016), is not produced the way Forge intends, and Forge log output follows vanilla's layout and levels.

## Locations

- `crates/minecraft/src/version.rs` `RawVersion` conversion, line 461 (`self.logging.and_then(|logging| logging.client)`)
- `crates/minecraft/src/version.rs` `VersionMetadata::inherit`, line 317
- `crates/minecraft/src/launch.rs`, lines 434-437 (logging argument added to the command)

## Limitations

The parse and merge behavior was reproduced with a synthetic child document. That Forge 1.12.2, 1.18.2, and 1.20.1 installers ship `"logging": {}` (and NeoForge omits the key) comes from inspecting those upstream documents, not from repository fixtures. Whether the official launcher treats `{}` as an override was not verified.
issues.title: Forge's explicit empty logging section is replaced by vanilla's log4j configuration

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-minecraft`

**Commit:** `0145a4a7da8b701dc49f277adc07291fa0c11096`

## Behavior

`LaunchError::is_cancellation` matches only `LaunchError::Canceled`. The vanilla installer wraps every batch download failure with `LaunchError::download(...)`, which produces `LaunchError::DownloadFailed`, including when the download error is `DownloadError::Canceled`. A user cancel during the library or asset download is therefore classified as a failure.

`CoreError::is_cancellation` delegates to this method for `CoreError::Launch`, so core logs "launch failed", emits `LaunchEvent::Failed`, and the desktop app shows an error for a launch the user canceled.

## Reproduction

```rust
let canceled = DownloadError::Canceled { url: "https://example.invalid/x".into() };
assert!(canceled.is_cancellation());
let wrapped = LaunchError::download("libraries", canceled);
// wrapped.is_cancellation() == false, message: "could not obtain `libraries`"
```

## Expected

A cancellation carried inside `DownloadFailed` is classified as cancellation. `DownloadError::is_cancellation` already exists for the wrapped case.

## Impact

Canceling a launch while it downloads libraries or assets is reported as a failed launch with a download error, instead of a canceled operation.

## Locations

- `crates/minecraft/src/error.rs` `LaunchError::is_cancellation`, line 307
- `crates/minecraft/src/error.rs` `LaunchError::download`, line 313
- `crates/minecraft/src/install.rs`, lines 432 and 485 (wrapping sites)
- `crates/core/src/error.rs` `CoreError::is_cancellation` (delegates)
- `crates/core/src/launch.rs` `launch_operation` (logs and emits `Failed`)

## Related

#113 has the same gap in `ephervex-loaders` and names this method as a dependency for its `Minecraft(...)` case. #144 has the same pattern in `ephervex-mod-platform`. `ephervex-pack` maps download cancellation to `PackError::Canceled` before wrapping, so it is not affected.

comments.author: MelanX
comments.bodyMarkdown:
Fixed in fd08626.

Both wrapping sites in `crates/minecraft/src/install.rs` now map a canceled library or asset batch to `LaunchError::Canceled` before wrapping, so a user cancel during those downloads is classified as cancellation. Regression test: `canceling_an_install_is_reported_as_cancellation_rather_than_a_failed_file` in `crates/minecraft/tests/vanilla_install.rs`.

`LaunchError::is_cancellation` itself is unchanged; no production path builds `DownloadFailed` from a cancellation anymore.

issues.title: Launch errors that wrap a canceled download are not classified as cancellation

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `0145a4a7da8b701dc49f277adc07291fa0c11096`

## Behavior

When no suitable Java is found and the request allows installing one, `plan_java` installs a managed runtime through `install_java_holding_the_cache`. That function creates its own `CancellationToken::new()` and an `OperationReporter::silent("managed-java")`. `plan_java` takes no cancellation token or reporter, so the caller's token and progress reporter never reach the managed Java download:

- `crates/core/src/launch.rs` calls `plan_java` with `install_if_missing` from the launch options;
- `crates/core/src/server.rs` calls it during server install and start;
- `crates/core/src/loader.rs` and `crates/core/src/diagnosis.rs` call it too.

The `ManagedJavaProvider` already accepts a token and a reporter.

## Scenario

1. Launch an instance on a machine without a matching Java, with managed downloads enabled.
2. Cancel the launch while the runtime (roughly 200 MB) downloads.

The cancel has no effect until the download and install finish, and the operation shows no download progress for that phase.

## Expected

The managed Java install is part of the launch or server operation: it observes that operation's cancellation token and reports progress through its reporter.

## Impact

A first launch or server start that needs a managed runtime cannot be canceled during the longest download it performs, and appears stalled while it runs.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/app.rs` `install_java_holding_the_cache`, lines 1132-1133
- `crates/core/src/app.rs` `plan_java`, line 949, and the managed-install branch around lines 1058-1069
- `crates/core/src/launch.rs`, lines 247-256
- `crates/core/src/server.rs`, lines 339 and 709

## Related

#98 covers cancellation inside the java crate's install (extraction, probe, publication) and notes that core currently never cancels. This issue is the core plumbing that #98 assumes. Fixing either one alone does not make a managed install cancelable.

## Limitations

Established from the code path. Not reproduced with a real runtime download.
issues.title: Automatic managed Java installs during launch or server start ignore cancellation and report no progress

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-download`

**Commit:** `0145a4a7da8b701dc49f277adc07291fa0c11096`

## Behavior

`DownloadManager::download` and `DownloadManager::download_all` take a borrowed `OperationReporter`, call `begin` on it, and always call `finish` with `Completed`, `Canceled`, or `Failed` when they return. Most callers pass the reporter of a longer operation they are part of:

- `crates/minecraft/src/install.rs`, lines 430 and 483 (libraries and assets during a launch);
- `crates/loaders/src/install.rs` (installer, libraries, mappings);
- `crates/java/src/managed.rs`, `crates/options/src/feed.rs`, `crates/core/src/pack_url.rs`, `crates/minecraft/src/catalog.rs`, `crates/minecraft/src/language.rs`.

`OperationReporter` has no terminal-state guard: `begin` sets `Running` again after `finish`.

During one desktop launch the operation therefore moves Running, then Completed after the library batch, then Running again when the asset batch begins, then Completed, while later stages (native extraction, loader installation) keep running. Only the frontend's own final `finish` is meant to end it.

`download_all_within` exists for exactly this case ("the same batch as one stage of a longer operation"), and `ephervex-pack` uses it, but the other callers use the finishing variants.

## Expected

A finished operation stays finished, and a download that is one stage of a longer operation does not end that operation. Either the stage variants are used wherever the reporter belongs to the caller, or the reporter refuses to leave a terminal state.

## Impact

While a launch or install is still working, its activity row shows it as completed. The GUI hides Cancel for terminal operations (`cancellable: operation.cancellable && !operation.status.is_terminal()` in `crates/gui/src/presentation.rs`), so the user cannot cancel during the stages that follow a finished batch. A batch failure briefly marks the operation failed with an unlocalized message before the frontend's own failure.

## Locations

- `crates/download/src/manager.rs` `DownloadManager::download`, lines 521-539
- `crates/download/src/manager.rs` `DownloadManager::download_all`, lines 548-562
- `crates/download/src/progress.rs` `OperationReporter::begin` and `finish`, lines 130-192

## Limitations

Established from the code paths. The intermediate states were not observed in a running desktop app.

comments.author: MelanX
comments.bodyMarkdown:
Fixed in 9feb8e4.

- `DownloadManager::download` and `download_all` are now stages: they report progress, the current file and counts, but never begin or finish the caller's operation. `download_all_within` is merged into `download_all`.
- `OperationReporter` ignores every change once the operation is terminal, publishes in order, and `flush` sends an update the throttle held back, so a stage's final count is not lost.
- The launch begins its own operation in a "Preparing exact environment" stage, and the desktop app keeps the launch's cancel button while it downloads.

Follow-ups: #323 (stale file counts between download stages) and #324 (trailing-edge publishing for other throttled stages).

issues.title: Download calls finish the caller's operation reporter, so a running operation shows as completed partway through

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-java`
**Commit:** `0145a4a7da8b701dc49f277adc07291fa0c11096`

## Behavior

`extract_file` checks the header's declared size against both limits, then writes the entry through a reader bounded only by `max_entry_bytes`, and checks the running total afterwards. An entry whose header understates its size can therefore write up to the per-entry ceiling past the remaining total budget. When that late check fails, the written file is not removed.

The declared size comes from `entry.header().size()`, the ustar field. tar 0.4.46 lets a PAX `size` record override the data length (`tar/src/archive.rs`, `pax_size`), so a header can claim fewer bytes than the stream delivers.

`write_file` has a related gap: `io::copy` failures from the archive side, such as a corrupt gzip stream, are reported as `Unwritable` with the destination path, and the partial file stays on disk.

## Code path

- `crates/java/src/archive.rs` `extract_file` and `write_file`.

## Expected behavior

The bounded reader respects the tighter of the per-entry ceiling and the remaining total, so no write passes either limit. A refused or broken entry is removed rather than left looking complete, and a read failure is reported against the archive, not the destination. `ephervex-pack`'s ZIP reader follows this shape (#125).

## Impact and limitations

Not reproduced; derived from the extractor and the pinned tar source. The only caller extracts Adoptium archives pinned by SHA-256, and extraction goes to a staging directory, so this adds no attacker capability today. It is a defect in an extractor documented as safe against hostile archives. Overshoot is bounded by `max_entry_bytes` (1 GiB by default).
issues.title: Java archive extraction can write past the remaining total budget and leaves refused files behind

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-pack`
**Commit:** `0145a4a7da8b701dc49f277adc07291fa0c11096`

## Behavior

An import reads the pack manifest out of the archive twice through the same `PackArchive`. `parse_with` gets the manifest bytes from `modrinth::read` or `curseforge::read` and discards them (`manifest: _`), then `retain_source` calls `PackArchive::read_manifest` (named `read_entry` at the commit above) again to retain it.

Each read decompresses the entry and charges its bytes and one entry to the archive's shared extraction budget, so the manifest counts twice against `max_total_bytes` and `max_entries`.

## Code path

- `crates/pack/src/import.rs` `parse_with` and `retain_source`.
- `crates/pack/src/modrinth.rs` `read`, `crates/pack/src/curseforge.rs` `read`.

## Expected behavior

The manifest is read and charged once per import. The bytes parsed are the bytes retained, for example by carrying them from the analysis to retention.

## Impact and limitations

Low. The manifest ceiling bounds each read, and both reads come from the same open file, so the retained bytes match what was parsed. The cost is a second decompression and a budget double-count of at most one manifest.
issues.title: Pack imports read and charge the manifest twice

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-i18n`

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior and locations

`gui-mod-clash-progress` in `crates/i18n/locales/en-US/main.ftl:2341` requires `value` and `other`. The modal in `crates/gui/ui/app.slint:2427` calls it through `GuiI18n.values`, whose `register_i18n` bridge in `crates/gui/src/controller.rs:2414-2422` always supplies `first` and `second`.

## Reproduction

Add multiple JARs whose filenames already exist in the selected host. The clash dialog displays `{$value} of {$other}` instead of a counter such as `1 of 3`.

A temporary probe using the exact bridge arguments reproduced that output. Supplying `value = "1"` and `other = "3"` produced `1 of 3`.

## Expected behavior and impact

The resource must use the argument names supplied by its caller. Every multi-item clash prompt currently loses its progress indication; skip and overwrite decisions remain functional. The resource can be corrected without changing the generic GUI bridge.

## Validation and limitations

The resource, Slint call, and Rust bridge were inspected, and formatting was reproduced deterministically. The desktop dialog itself was not launched. Existing resource checks do not verify this callback's argument names. `cargo test -p ephervex-i18n --locked --offline` passed all 28 tests.
issues.title: Mod-clash progress uses argument names the GUI never supplies

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crates:** `ephervex-core`, `ephervex-cli`, `ephervex-gui`

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior and locations

`CoreError::message_args` converts `LoaderChangeBlockedByMods.incompatible` to a string (`crates/core/src/error.rs:514-516`). The CLI formatter (`crates/cli/src/main.rs:7465-7468`) and GUI formatter (`crates/gui/src/backend.rs:8142-8145`) then convert that string into `Arg::Text`.

The Fluent resource `error-loader-change-blocked-by-mods` (`crates/i18n/locales/en-US/main.ftl:832-835`) selects a plural branch using numeric `count`. The i18n API already distinguishes `Arg::Count` from `Arg::Text`; the error boundary discards that distinction.

## Reproduction

Select a loader build incompatible with exactly one installed mod without accepting incompatible mods. `change_loader_version_holding_the_cache` (`crates/core/src/loader.rs:207`) returns the error with `incompatible = 1`.

Its message arguments are `[("count", "1")]`. Formatting them as the frontends do produces:

`1 installed mods do not fit the selected loader build.`

Passing the same count as a number produces the expected singular branch:

`1 installed mod does not fit the selected loader build.`

## Expected behavior and impact

Preserve numeric argument types through the core error boundary and both frontend adapters so Fluent can select the correct plural branch. The loader-change refusal remains correct; the proven defect is its singular-count message.

## Validation and limitations

Core argument production and both adapters were inspected; text-versus-number formatting was reproduced with the current resource. The finding is limited to this proven error variant, not every delegated error. Existing i18n tests pass numeric arguments directly and do not exercise the string-only error boundary. All 28 focused i18n tests passed.
issues.title: Loader-change errors stringify counts before Fluent plural selection

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior and locations

`PreferenceValueError` carries the rejected setting ID (`crates/options/src/preference.rs:318-330`), and its Fluent message requires `preference` (`crates/i18n/locales/en-US/main.ftl:296`). `CoreError` delegates the message ID but has no `PreferenceValue` arm in `message_args` (`crates/core/src/error.rs:503-542`), so the ID never reaches the frontend formatter.

## Reproduction

In an isolated application root, call `App::save_global_minecraft_preferences` with an edit setting `fov` to the decimal value `500.0`. Descriptor validation rejects it at `crates/core/src/minecraft_preferences.rs:387`.

The returned error has message ID `error-options-preference-value-unusable` and an empty argument list. Formatting it produces:

`The configured value for {$preference} cannot be used for this setting.`

The GUI's `SaveMinecraftPreferences` handler (`crates/gui/src/backend.rs:4395-4412`) forwards a save failure to the standard localized error path. Neither the GUI nor CLI formatter supplies this missing argument independently.

## Expected behavior and impact

The summary should identify `fov`, preserving the setting ID already present in the typed error. Invalid preference edits currently produce incomplete diagnostics, particularly confusing in a batch. Validation still refuses the edit safely.

## Validation and limitations

The save failure was reproduced using a temporary application root, and the missing argument and resulting text were verified. The existing invalid-batch test in `crates/core/src/minecraft_preferences.rs:590-619` checks the message ID and unchanged configuration, but not formatted arguments. All 28 focused i18n tests passed.

The core probe used an existing compiled artifact; the exercised source files were verified unchanged across the two commits preceding the reviewed commit. Localization was probed using the freshly tested i18n artifact. No real user configuration or credentials were used.

Related to #88, not covered by it: that issue concerns mapping domain failures to `TypeMismatch` in preference planning. Correcting that mapping does not supply `preference` in `CoreError::message_args`.
issues.title: Preference validation errors omit the rejected setting identity

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-i18n`

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior and locations

The `.action` at `crates/i18n/locales/en-US/main.ftl:863` is attached to `error-mod-file-not-toggled` instead of `error-mod-identity-incomplete` at line 840.

`App::set_mod_enabled` converts a failed filesystem rename into `CoreError::ModFileNotToggled` (`crates/core/src/mods.rs:1253`). Both frontend error formatters append its action.

## Reproduction

Enable or disable an installed mod when renaming its JAR fails, for example because the mods directory is not writable. The rename error receives this unrelated recovery advice:

`Mods with no identity have to be managed by hand.`

Meanwhile, `lookup_attribute("error-mod-identity-incomplete", "action")` returns `None`.

## Expected behavior and impact

Recovery attributes must remain attached to the errors they describe. A filesystem rename failure does not imply missing provider identity and can affect a fully identified managed mod. The current binding gives misleading advice for rename failures and removes the intended next step from the identity error.

## Validation and limitations

Runtime attribute lookup reproduced both the incorrect action and the missing identity action. The production rename-to-error path and frontend formatting paths were inspected; no destructive filesystem failure was induced. Existing lookup tests do not check these message/action associations. `cargo test -p ephervex-i18n --locked --offline` passed all 28 tests.
issues.title: Mod rename failures display recovery advice for missing provider identity

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-i18n`

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior and locations

In `crates/i18n/locales/en-US/main.ftl:1438-1441`, `error-mod-managed-identity-missing` has no action. Its explanation is instead a second `.action` on the neighboring `error-mod-hand-placed-not-mutable` message. Fluent returns that neighbor's first action, leaving the second explanation inaccessible through either lookup.

`PackError::ManagedIdentityMissing` provides the correct message ID and its `path` argument (`crates/pack/src/error.rs:391,515`). A production refusal is present in `crates/pack/src/mutate.rs:324`, where removal names a project absent from the managed recipe.

## Reproduction

Format `error-mod-managed-identity-missing` with `path = "mods/example.jar"` and request its action. The result is `None`.

Requesting the neighboring hand-placed error's action returns only:

`Delete it from the mods list if you no longer want it.`

The explanation beginning `Ephervex only records mods it can look up again by project and version` is not returned.

## Expected behavior and impact

Attach the explanation and its path placeholder to `error-mod-managed-identity-missing`. The managed-identity refusal currently loses the detail explaining its identity requirement. Its summary and refusal behavior remain intact.

## Validation and limitations

Runtime lookup reproduced the missing and shadowed attributes. Production error mapping and an existing managed-removal refusal test were inspected. The duplicate-message test checks message IDs rather than duplicate attributes; managed-removal tests check the error variant rather than localization. All 28 focused i18n tests passed. No real instance was mutated.
issues.title: A misplaced duplicate action hides managed-identity recovery guidance

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior

`App::delete_client` deletes every linked server and then calls `Registry::delete_client`, which runs `remove_tree(root)` for `FileDisposition::Remove`. Nothing on this path checks `launch_state` or the instance's `LaunchLock`. The GUI's "Delete instance" menu item has no enabled condition, unlike "Make persistent" next to it, and the CLI's `instance delete` calls the same method.

## Reproduction

1. Create a client instance in a temporary root.
2. Hold `LaunchLock::acquire(&client.root)`, so `launch_state()` returns `Some`.
3. Call `app.delete_client(id, FileDisposition::Remove)`.

It returns `Ok(())` and the instance root is gone, including `.launcher/launch.lock`. With `FileDisposition::Keep` the index row is dropped while the launch is still alive.

## Expected behavior

Deleting a client is refused while it is launching or running, the same way `delete_server`, promotion, snapshot restore, repair and `set_client_runtime_settings` refuse.

## Impact

A running game's directory (saves, logs, crash evidence) is removed underneath the live process, and the lock that tracked the process is deleted with it, so Ephervex no longer knows the game is running. The only precondition is a running instance and an ordinary delete from the GUI or the CLI.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/app.rs` `App::delete_client` (579-599)
- `crates/storage/src/registry.rs` `Registry::delete_client` (610-641)
- `crates/gui/ui/home/host-cards.slint` delete menu item (177)
- `crates/cli/src/main.rs` `InstanceCommand::Delete` (1998-2004)

## Validation and limitations

Reproduced with a probe binary against a temporary root with isolated `HOME`/XDG variables and no network. No test deletes a running client.
issues.title: Deleting a client instance does not refuse while its game is running

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crates:** `ephervex-core`, `ephervex-gui`

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior

`App::mutate_config` clones the `Config` loaded when that `App` was opened, applies the change and saves the whole file. It never reloads or merges what is on disk. The GUI worker keeps one `App` for the life of the process and never reloads its configuration, while GUI sign-in runs `App::login` on a separate, detached `App` (`spawn_login` via `spawn_detached`). That login writes the account into `config.toml` and the refresh token into the keyring, but the worker's in-memory copy still has no account.

## Reproduction

With two `App`s opened on one temporary root (`worker` and `detached`):

1. `detached.add_offline_account("Alice")`.
2. `worker.set_default_account("Alice")` fails with `AccountUnknown`.
3. `worker.set_show_linked_servers(true)`.
4. A freshly opened `App` lists no accounts.

In the desktop app: sign in with Microsoft, then change any setting (theme, Java settings, EULA acceptance, favorite versions, and so on). The account disappears from `config.toml`.

## Expected behavior

A configuration write from one `App` never reverts a change written by another, for example by locking and reloading before applying the change, or with a version check. ADR 0004 and the `remove_account` documentation require that a stored secret always has a configuration record that lets it be removed.

## Impact

The ordinary first-run flow of signing in and then changing a setting loses the account and leaves its refresh token in Secret Service with nothing naming it. This repeats for every GUI sign-in until the application restarts. The same lost update affects the GUI and the CLI running at the same time, for accounts, trusted pack hosts, Java preferences, watched folders and other settings.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/app.rs` `App::mutate_config` (1422-1428), `App::open` (266-284)
- `crates/core/src/account.rs` `App::adopt` (740-766)
- `crates/gui/src/backend.rs` worker `App::open()` (2037), `spawn_login` (7020), `spawn_detached` (7643-7687)

## Validation and limitations

The lost update was reproduced with a probe using two `App`s on a temporary root, with no network and no real keyring. The GUI wiring was confirmed by reading the code. Every existing account and configuration test uses a single `App`.
issues.title: A configuration change made through one App is reverted by another, erasing a GUI sign-in

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior

`App::delete_client` documents that a running linked server "refuses the whole deletion" and that "Nothing is removed in that case". The implementation calls `delete_server` for each linked server in turn (ordered by name) and only then deletes the client. Each `delete_server` checks only its own server, so earlier servers are already deleted when a later one refuses.

## Scenario

1. Client C has linked servers S1 (stopped) and S2 (running).
2. `delete_client(C, FileDisposition::Remove)`.

S1 and its files are deleted, then the call fails on S2 with `AlreadyRunning`. C remains. A failure deleting the client itself after its servers succeeded likewise leaves the servers gone.

## Expected behavior

Every refusal (the client, and each linked server) is checked before anything is deleted, as the documentation promises.

## Impact

A server world is irreversibly deleted by an operation that reported a refusal, and a user who decides not to retry has already lost it.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/app.rs` `App::delete_client` (579-599)
- `crates/core/src/server.rs` `delete_server` (542-547)
- `crates/storage/src/registry.rs` `linked_server_ids` (647-660)

## Validation and limitations

Established from the code path. No test covers a mix of running and stopped linked servers.
issues.title: Client deletion removes linked servers one at a time, so a running one refuses after others are already deleted

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior

`required_projects` builds the set of still-required projects only from roots with origin `UserSelected` or `SelectedOptionalDependency`. Its documentation assumes that no `RequiredDependency` entry can belong to a pack mod. Since ADR 0032 (and for identified pack override jars), a pack-owned mod can change version, and a dependency that its new release needs is recorded as `RequiredDependency` while the pack mod keeps its pack origin. Nothing keeps that dependency alive.

## Scenario

1. An instance from a pack, with pack mod version changes allowed.
2. Change pack mod P to a release that newly requires library L. L is installed as `RequiredDependency`.
3. Install, remove or change any user mod from the same catalog.

The plan for step 3 lists L under `collected_dependencies`, and applying it retires L's jar. P can no longer load. Linked servers use the same helper.

## Expected behavior

A dependency required by any mod that remains installed is never collected, whatever that mod's origin.

## Impact

An ordinary mod change leaves an instance that does not start, and the confirmation presents the removal as harmless orphan cleanup. Recoverable by reinstalling L.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/mutation.rs` `required_projects` (932-999), `orphaned_dependencies` (878-922), `upserts_for` (1008-1035)
- `crates/core/src/linked_mods.rs` (985-1003, 1083-1095)

## Validation and limitations

Established from the code path. Not executed, because driving it needs the test-only loopback catalog. Existing orphan tests use only user roots.
issues.title: Dependencies installed for a moved pack mod are removed as orphans by the next unrelated mod change

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crates:** `ephervex-core`, `ephervex-mod-platform`

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior

A version change or update resolves the target with `InstalledPolicy::Replace`. For a dependency without a pin, the resolver picks `newest_compatible` and ignores the version already installed. `already_installed` then turns every installed dependency whose version differs into a replacement, and `upserts_for` writes every resolved mod. The mutation therefore retires and replaces those dependencies too. The pack-owned restriction (`MutationRestriction::PackOwned`) is applied only to the mod being acted on.

## Scenario

1. An imported pack declares library L at release A (`PackDeclared`), with pack mod version changes off.
2. The user adds mod X, which requires L without a pin.
3. Later the user updates X.

L is resolved to its newest compatible release B, and the mutation retires L@A and installs L@B. The preview lists L only as an install row. A selected optional dependency, or a dependency another mod needs at the older release, moves the same way.

## Expected behavior

Dependencies that are already installed at a release satisfying the new root stay where they are, or the operation asks or refuses. Pack-owned entries are never moved as a side effect.

## Impact

A pack reproduction silently diverges from what the pack shipped, and linked server rebuilds then follow the changed recipe. The precondition is a changed mod whose dependency is installed at an older release.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/mutation.rs` `upserts_for` (1008-1035), `version_change_plan` (707-797), `planned_files` (1168-1183)
- `crates/mod-platform/src/resolve.rs` `select_version` (543-583), `already_installed` (874-915)

## Validation and limitations

Established from the code path. Not executed, because driving it needs the test-only loopback catalog. No mutation test starts from an older installed dependency.
issues.title: Changing or updating one mod moves its already-installed dependencies to their newest releases, including pack-owned ones

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior

When catalogs are asked (`ask_catalogs`, the default for a full diagnosis), `confirm_unmet_requirements` hashes every jar not identified in the requirement's catalog and asks that catalog. A jar the catalog does not recognize is simply absent from the answer, and a requirement with no match is then marked `proven: true`.

## Scenario

1. Addon A, installed from Modrinth, records that it requires project X.
2. The instance also has a hand-placed local development build of X, whose bytes no catalog knows.
3. Offline diagnosis correctly leaves the requirement unconfirmed.
4. A full diagnosis reports `DependencyMissing` with `proven: true`.

## Expected behavior

A catalog failing to recognize a jar says nothing about what that jar is. Absence is proven only when every candidate jar has been positively identified as another project. Otherwise the requirement stays unconfirmed, keeping evidence and uncertainty apart (ADR 0037).

## Impact

Diagnostics shows a false problem in the local-build workflow the launcher exists for, and its missing-mod offer can propose installing a second copy of a mod that is already present.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/dependencies.rs` `confirm_unmet_requirements` (508-565, `None => *proven = true`), `recognize_in` (569-637)

## Validation and limitations

Established from the code path. The existing mixed-catalog test covers only a recognized jar and a genuinely absent project.
issues.title: Diagnostics reports a required mod as proven missing when a catalog does not recognize a local jar

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior

`identify_hand_placed` reads the host layout, including the recipe, before hashing jars and calling Modrinth and CurseForge. `record_identified` then clones that stale recipe, adds the identified entries and writes it. Any recipe change made while the lookups were in flight is overwritten. `record_declared_relations` re-reads the recipe after its network calls to avoid exactly this.

## Scenario

1. Open the workspace of a pack instance that has override or hand-placed jars without an identity. The GUI runs enrichment on its own thread with its own `App`.
2. While recognition is in flight, install a mod, remove a mod, change a mod's version, or restore a snapshot.
3. The enrichment write lands last.

The new install's record disappears (its jar now shows as hand-placed), a removed mod's record returns, or a restored `recipe.json` is replaced by the pre-restore one.

## Expected behavior

The recipe is re-read immediately before writing and only the identity additions are merged, as `record_declared_relations` already does.

## Impact

Silent corruption of the recorded desired state that server reconstruction, verification, repair and orphan collection rely on. The window spans network round trips.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/mods.rs` `identify_hand_placed` (1487-1578), `record_identified` (225-284)
- `crates/core/src/dependencies.rs` `record_declared_relations` (re-read for comparison)
- `crates/gui/src/backend.rs` `refresh_enriched_host_mods` (8530)

## Validation and limitations

Established from the code path. Timing dependent; no concurrent-write test exists.
issues.title: Mod list identification writes back a recipe read before its network calls, reverting concurrent changes

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior

`delete_snapshot` deletes any snapshot, including the safety snapshot an active isolation session depends on. Afterwards `finish_isolation` applies the outcome and then fails renaming the missing snapshot, and `cancel_isolation` fails restoring it. Both fail before `isolation.json` is removed.

## Reproduction

1. Start mod isolation on a host.
2. Delete the "Before mod isolation" snapshot from the Snapshots surface or with `ephervex snapshot delete`.
3. Finish or cancel the session.

Both fail with `SnapshotError::NotFound`, every time.

## Expected behavior

A snapshot that an active session references cannot be deleted, or finishing and canceling handle a missing snapshot instead of failing permanently.

## Impact

`isolation.json` stays, so repairs and mod-touching diagnostic fixes are refused (`IsolationActive`) and a new session is refused as already active. No API removes the session; the only way out is deleting `.launcher/isolation.json` by hand. The pre-isolation state the session promised to restore is gone.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/snapshot.rs` `delete_snapshot` (365-379)
- `crates/core/src/isolation.rs` `finish_isolation` (819-836), `cancel_isolation` (839-857)

## Validation and limitations

Established from the code path. No test deletes the safety snapshot during a session.
issues.title: Deleting an active isolation session's safety snapshot leaves a session that cannot finish or cancel

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior

`set_persistent_instance_root` writes the new path to `config.toml` first, then calls `ensure_base_directories` and `Registry::open` for it. If either fails, the method returns an error, but the configuration already names the new root while the running process still uses the old registry.

## Scenario

1. Set the persistent instance root to a path that cannot be created or written.
2. The call returns an error.
3. Restart Ephervex.

`ephervex_storage::open` applies the configured root and fails in `ensure_base_directories`, so neither the GUI nor the CLI starts until `config.toml` is edited by hand.

## Expected behavior

The new root is created and opened first, and the configuration and registry are switched together only after that succeeds, or the configuration is rolled back on failure.

## Impact

A rejected setting persists and blocks the next startup of both frontends.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/app.rs` `set_persistent_instance_root` (1337-1367)
- `crates/storage/src/lib.rs` `open` (137-142)

## Validation and limitations

Established from the code path.
issues.title: Changing the persistent instance root saves the setting before the new root is created or opened

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crates:** `ephervex-core`, `ephervex-storage`

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior

Operations that require a stopped host check the launch or runtime state once and then do their work without holding anything that excludes a new launch. The clearest case is promotion: core checks `launch_state`, then `Registry::relocate_client` deletes the launch lock file, copies the tree (often from tmpfs to disk, which can take a long time) and removes the old root. The same check-then-act pattern applies to snapshot creation and restore, server deletion and settings, and server start preparation, which writes files before the server crate takes its `RuntimeGuard`. Launch reads the instance record before it takes the launch lock.

## Scenario

1. Promote a temporary instance from the desktop app.
2. While the tree is being copied, launch the same instance from the CLI.

The launch takes a fresh lock on the old root and starts the game there. Promotion then removes the old root underneath it.

## Expected behavior

One lifecycle guard, mutually exclusive with launches and server starts, is taken before the stopped-state decision and held for the whole operation. Storage does not delete a launch lock based on an earlier observation.

## Impact

Files are moved or deleted underneath a running game. Within the desktop app these operations are serialized (promotion runs on the worker's command loop, and snapshot, isolation and repair use an in-flight marker), so the demonstrated risk needs a second process such as the CLI.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/promotion.rs` `promote_instance`, `refuse_promoting` (148-246)
- `crates/storage/src/registry.rs` `relocate_client` (296-345), `discard_launch_lock` (1245-1261)
- `crates/core/src/snapshot.rs` (230-270, 382-415)
- `crates/core/src/server.rs` (542-595, 664-706); `crates/server/src/process.rs` (161-193)
- `crates/core/src/launch.rs` (230-238)

## Validation and limitations

Established from the code paths. Not reproduced with a timed cross-process run.

Related to #33 and #36, which concern the storage launch lock itself.

comments.author: MelanX
comments.bodyMarkdown:
7b1d50b and 3da146d added more operations with the same check-then-act shape, which the fix here should cover:

- `App::delete_client` checks `launch_state` (through `refuse_while_running`) and each linked server's runtime, then removes the trees.
- `App::delete_client_stopping_linked_servers` stops the linked servers, then deletes through `delete_client`.

Nothing is held between the check and the removal, so a launch or server start in between can still have its directory removed.

issues.title: Stopped-state checks are not held for the operation, so a concurrent launch can race promotion and other changes

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior

Import passes the pack's own name (`original_name`) straight to `NewClient::new`. The Modrinth parser takes `index.name` verbatim and the CurseForge parser only trims it. `validated_entity_name`, which refuses empty names, control characters and overlong names, is applied only on rename.

## Reproduction

Import an mrpack whose `name` is `"Evil\u001b[2J\u001b[31mPWNED\nsecond line"`.

- The instance record stores the name exactly as given.
- `rename_client(id, &record.name)` then refuses that same name with `error-name-control-characters`.

## Expected behavior

Names coming from an archive go through the same rules as renames (or are sanitized and truncated) before the record is created.

## Impact

An untrusted archive, or an `ephervex://` link that imports one, can put terminal escape sequences and newlines into CLI listings and log lines. Names can also be empty or extremely long, and the user cannot resubmit the name the instance holds.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/import.rs` (207-220)
- `crates/pack/src/modrinth.rs` (156); `crates/pack/src/curseforge.rs` (158)
- `crates/core/src/instance.rs` `validated_entity_name` (446-464)

## Validation and limitations

Reproduced with a probe binary against a temporary root, no network.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crates:** `ephervex-storage`, `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior

`Registry::duplicate_client` copies the instance tree excluding only `launch.lock` and `snapshots`. An active isolation session lives in `.launcher/isolation.json` and names the original host, so the copy carries it. `App::duplicate_client` does not refuse or clean up.

## Reproduction

1. `begin_isolation` on instance A.
2. `duplicate_client(A, ..)`.
3. On the copy:
   - `isolation_state` fails with `error-isolation-host-mismatch`.
   - `begin_isolation` fails with `error-isolation-already-active`.
   - `repair_host` fails with the host mismatch, and diagnostic fixes fail the same way.

## Expected behavior

A duplicate carries no launcher transaction state: no isolation session, retired files or staging, just as snapshots exclude them. Alternatively, duplication is refused during an active session.

## Impact

The copy cannot repair, isolate or apply fixes until `.launcher/isolation.json` is deleted by hand. Duplicating mid-bisect is an anticipated workflow (the absent-mod policy documents copies made to carry on bisecting).

## Locations

- `crates/storage/src/registry.rs` `duplicate_client` (439-467)
- `crates/core/src/instance.rs` `App::duplicate_client` (514-529)
- `crates/core/src/isolation.rs` `isolation_path` (867-872)

## Validation and limitations

Reproduced with a probe binary against a temporary root, no network.

Related to #34, which covers the copied additional launch locks but not the isolation session.

## Behavior

The copy can contain files from different points in time, including partially written region files, so the duplicated world may be inconsistent or damaged without any warning. The original is unaffected.

## Behavior

`record_identified` records every identified hand-placed jar as `client: Required, server: Unknown, selected: None`, whatever the host is. On a server, `recorded_mods_for(Server)` filters such an entry out, so the jar still appears as an unidentified hand-placed file.

- The jar is still listed as hand-placed, so identification and the recipe rewrite repeat on every refresh.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior

`authenticated_session` returns the cached session whenever it is usable, without checking that it belongs to the default account. `session_for_account` and `login` of a second account both replace the cached session.

## Reproduction

On one `App`, with Alice as the default account:

1. `session_for_account("Bob")` for a launch as Bob.
2. A later launch with no account named.

The second launch runs as Bob. The same happens after signing in a second account while another stays default.

## Expected behavior

The cached session is reused only when it belongs to the default account. `session_for_account` documents that it does not change what the next launch uses.

## Impact

Today's frontends open a fresh `App` per launch and the CLI is one command per process, so this is latent there. Any long-lived `App` launches as the wrong account.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/account.rs` `authenticated_session` (457-477), `session_for_account` (486-510)

## Validation and limitations

Reproduced with a probe binary using offline accounts in a temporary root.
issues.title: A cached session is reused for a default launch even when it belongs to another account

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior

`resume_account` and `session_for_account` build the account provider with session-only storage allowed. When Secret Service cannot be opened, `build_account_provider` falls back to a new, empty `MemoryStore`, and `resume` then finds no refresh token and fails with `NotSignedIn`.

## Scenario

1. Sign in a Microsoft account with a working keyring.
2. Later, with Secret Service temporarily unavailable, launch or resume.

## Behavior

`register_url_handler` writes `Exec=<path> %u` using the executable path verbatim. ## Expected behavior

The `Exec` value is quoted and escaped per the specification, and the status check parses it the same way.

## Impact

Links silently fail for installations under paths with spaces, quotes, backslashes, `$` or `%`, while settings say the handler is registered.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/url_handler.rs` `register_url_handler` (263-297), `read_exec` (127-132)

Established from the code path and the Desktop Entry Specification.

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior

When binding the launcher socket fails because the path exists and connecting to it fails, `start` removes the path and binds again. If two processes both see the stale socket, process A can remove and bind first, and process B then removes A's live socket path and binds its own. Both return `Startup::Primary`. The comment claims the second process "loses the bind and connects instead", which is not true once it has removed the path. A's `Drop` later removes B's path. Any connect error, not only a refused connection, is taken as proof of staleness.

## Scenario

1. A crash leaves a stale socket at `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/ephervex-<uid>.sock`.
2. Two links are opened at nearly the same time.

Two launchers run against the same instances.

## Expected behavior

Taking over a stale name is atomic, for example under a lock file held across remove and bind, or verified after binding, and only a connection refusal counts as stale.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/single_instance.rs` `start` (137-170), `Drop for PrimaryInstance` (103-110)

## Validation and limitations

A small model of the remove-and-bind sequence on AF_UNIX sockets ended with both listeners bound and only the second one reachable. The race window is narrow.
issues.title: Two launchers taking over a stale single-instance socket can both become primary

## Behavior

`resolve_files` puts every distribution-restricted file into `blocked_reasons` before `resolve_duplicate_projects` runs, and that function only sees unrestricted files. A restricted duplicate therefore never takes part in choosing one file per project. If its bytes are cached, `recipe_from_cache` adds it to the recipe next to the chosen file.

A CurseForge manifest declares project P twice (the export defect ADR 0031 handles), and one or both files are restricted.

## Actual behavior

- With a cached restricted copy, both files become `PackDeclared` entries and both jars are installed, so the game refuses the duplicate mod id.
- Otherwise the user is asked to fetch by hand a file the rule would have discarded.

## Expected behavior

Restricted candidates take part in the same one-file-per-project choice (ADR 0031).

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/curseforge_pack.rs` `resolve_files` (651-735), `resolve_duplicate_projects` (802-850), `resolve_curseforge_pack` (183-207), `recipe_from_cache` (229-259)

Established from the code path. Requires a restricted project declared twice.

**Commit:** `a86373528d8017ac36d10a769d7f0ab1d45be08d`

## Behavior

`adopt_into_cache` returns success as soon as a file exists at the target's content-addressed path, without checking it. Acquisition (`cached_artifact_bytes`, and pack's `probe_cache_without_url`) treats a file there that fails verification as not cached and leaves it in place.

## Scenario

1. A corrupt or truncated file sits at a restricted artifact's content path.
2. The operation asks the user to download the file by hand.
3. The user places the correct file in a watched folder. The watcher reports it adopted, but the bad bytes stay.
4. Retrying asks for the manual download again.

## Expected behavior

An existing destination is verified, and replaced atomically when it fails.

## Impact

The user is stuck in a manual-download loop until the cache is cleared.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/download_watch.rs` `check_candidate` (131-157), `adopt_into_cache` (168-199)
- `crates/core/src/acquisition.rs` `cached_artifact_bytes` (47-91)

## Validation and limitations

Established from the code path. Requires a damaged cache entry.

comments.author: MelanX
comments.bodyMarkdown:
The adoption path itself also publishes unsafely (still the case at `ecbee9d`):

- `adopt_into_cache` copies to `.part-adopt-<uuid>` and calls plain `tokio::fs::rename`, with no `sync_all` first. `ephervex_download::publish_staged` does sync, so a crash right after adoption can leave an empty or truncated file at the cache path, which then triggers the loop described above.
- The rename does not take the directory publication lock that the download manager's revalidation discard relies on, so adoption can race a discard of the same path.

Expected in addition: verify an existing destination with `stored_file_matches` (treat a mismatch as absent), and publish through `ephervex_download::staging_path` and `publish_staged` rather than a hand-rolled temp file and rename.

issues.title: The download watcher treats any file already at the cache path as an adopted match

## Behavior

`set_mods_enabled` and `delete_mod_files` apply each change in order and return on the first error, leaving earlier changes in place. `docs/architecture.md` says of dependency-aware enable, disable and delete: "Failure rolls back the batch". The ordering key of `set_mods_enabled` counts only dependents that are currently enabled, so when a disabled mod and its disabled dependency are enabled together both score zero and the input order decides. The function's documentation promises that enables go dependencies first and that any prefix leaves a set the loader can start.

## Scenario

Enable a mod and its library together, with the library later in the input, and let the second rename fail.

## Actual behavior

The mod is enabled without its library. A failed delete batch leaves some files already deleted.

## Expected behavior

The batch is ordered topologically over required edges, including disabled members of the batch, and a failure rolls back what was applied, as documented.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/dependencies.rs` `set_mods_enabled` (734-757), `delete_mod_files` (703-722)
- `docs/architecture.md` (182)

## Validation and limitations

Established from the code path. Isolation resume reapplies the whole configuration, which limits the impact there.
issues.title: Batch enable, disable and delete neither roll back nor reliably enable dependencies first

## Behavior

`mutation_blocker`, which refuses with `IsolationActive`, is consulted only by repair and diagnostic fixes. Installing, updating, changing, removing, adding or deleting mod files, toggling mods, changing the loader build and linked mod operations all proceed during a session.

## Scenario

- During a session, install a new mod that causes the crash. It is not in the session's candidates, so it stays enabled in every round and is never a suspect, and the result can blame an innocent mod.

## Expected behavior

Changes to the mod set are refused while a session owns which mods are enabled, as repair already is, or the session accounts for them.

- `crates/core/src/isolation.rs` `isolation_configuration_applied` (887-903), `apply_isolation_configuration` (905-918)

2. Later `mods/foo.jar` is corrupt and repaired.

Every request uses the current effective User-Agent, or the setting is documented and shown as applying after restart.

## Behavior

`StoredApiKey::api_key` opens the keyring first. When Secret Service is not available, `credential_store()` fails and the error is returned as `CredentialUnreadable` before `curseforge_api_key` can fall back to `DEFAULT_CURSEFORGE_API_KEY`.

## Scenario

## Actual behavior

CurseForge features fail, and the user cannot store a key either.

## Expected behavior

With no secret storage at all there is no user key to prefer, so the built-in key applies (ADR 0030). Refusing on a locked keyring, where a user key may exist, remains reasonable.

## Behavior

`remove_account` documents that the keyring entry goes first and a failure there aborts, so a secret is never left without a record. But when `credential_store()` fails, the error is logged as "no keyring" and the account metadata is deleted anyway. `KeyringStore::open` reports any failed probe as `SecretStorageUnavailable`, which includes a temporarily unavailable or locked Secret Service.

## Scenario

1. Sign in a Microsoft account with a working keyring.
2. Sign out or remove the account while Secret Service is temporarily unavailable.

The removal reports success, and the refresh token stays in the keyring with no account record pointing at it.

## Expected behavior

Deletion is skipped only when no persistent store can exist for the account. Otherwise the removal is refused, or the pending cleanup is recorded (ADR 0004).

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/account.rs` `remove_account` (615-668)
- `crates/auth/src/store.rs` `KeyringStore::open` (170-178)

## Validation and limitations

Established from the code path, without manipulating a real Secret Service.

## Behavior

A persistent Microsoft login stores the refresh token in the keyring inside the provider, before `App::adopt` records the account in `config.toml`. If that configuration write fails, login returns an error, but the token stays in the keyring with no account record naming it.

## Scenario

Sign in while `config.toml` cannot be written, for example on a read-only or full filesystem.

## Expected behavior

A login that fails to record the account removes the token it just stored (or records it in a way that can be cleaned up), so a secret is never left without a record (ADR 0004).

## Impact

The orphaned token cannot be removed from the application. It is only overwritten if the same account later signs in successfully.
