issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crates:** `ephervex-server`, `ephervex-gui`

**Commit:** `aa0355c`

## Behavior

`RuntimeEvidence.child_pending` makes a dead supervisor with no recorded child classify as `UnknownRunning` (`crates/server/src/runtime.rs`), so a JVM spawned just before the supervisor died is not missed. Within the same boot that state never resolves.

If the launcher is killed after the pending mark but before the child is recorded (including before the spawn itself, or after the child has since exited):

- every start returns `AlreadyRunning`;
- `clear_stale_runtime` returns `RuntimeMayBeAlive`;
- the GUI shows the state as unknown with no recovery action, because `needs_recovery` is only set for proven-stale state (`crates/gui/src/presentation.rs`);
- the running list keeps showing the dead supervisor's pid.

The only way out is deleting `.launcher/server-runtime.json` by hand.

## Expected behavior

The state can be resolved without editing files. Options include identifying the pending child by its own process group (it is spawned with `process_group(0)`), working directory and start time after the pending mark, or offering a user-confirmed recovery for this state.

## Locations

- `crates/server/src/runtime.rs` classification of `child_pending`, `clear_stale_runtime`
- `crates/server/src/process.rs` pending mark around the spawn
- `crates/gui/src/presentation.rs` `needs_recovery`
issues.title: A server stays blocked with no recovery after its supervisor dies while a child start is pending

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-pack`

**Commit:** `7bba579`

## Behavior

The public doc on `ManagedMutationReport::repaired` says: "Repair, not a change: the recipe entry is unchanged."

`mutate_managed` applies `recording_side` for `Action::Repair` as well as `Action::Record`. A record that did not take the mutated side is brought in line, so a jar is never written while the recipe says that side lacks it. A repair can therefore rewrite the entry's side requirement and optional selection.

## Expected behavior

The doc says a repair keeps the recorded entry except for taking the side the jar was written on.

## Locations

- `crates/pack/src/mutate.rs` `ManagedMutationReport::repaired`
- `crates/pack/src/mutate.rs` `Action::Repair | Action::Record` arm applying `recording_side`

## Related

#412 added `recording_side` on repair.
issues.title: `ManagedMutationReport::repaired` doc says a repair never changes the recipe entry

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crates:** `ephervex-core`, `ephervex-pack`

**Commit:** `7bba579`

## Behavior

`validate_server_archive` (`crates/core/src/server.rs`) runs before Java probing and loader installation so an unusable archive is refused in milliseconds. It only opens the archive with `PackArchive::open`.

`install_server_pack` then extracts through `extract_prefix_filtered`, and `extract_under` passes every entry in the archive through `entry_under`, including entries outside the extracted prefix. An entry name with a backslash, a colon, a parent or absolute component, or a reserved top-level name anywhere in the archive fails with `EntryPathUnsafe` or `EntryReserved`.

## Impact

Such an archive passes validation and fails only after Java probing and the loader installation have run, which the pre-flight exists to avoid.

## Expected behavior

The pre-flight refuses every entry name extraction would refuse, before any expensive work. Pack import already does this with `PackArchive::require_extractable_entry_names`; the server path should reuse that check rather than duplicate it.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/server.rs` `validate_server_archive`
- `crates/pack/src/archive.rs` `require_extractable_entry_names` (`pub(crate)`), `entry_under`, `extract_under`
- `crates/pack/src/server_pack.rs` `install_server_pack`
issues.title: Server archive validation accepts entry names that extraction later refuses

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-pack`

**Commit:** `7bba579`

## Behavior

`PackArchive::extract_under` calls `ZipArchive::by_index` on every entry in the archive, including entries outside the requested layer, before it checks the name. `by_index` fails for an encrypted entry or an unsupported compression method, which becomes `PackError::ArchiveInvalid`.

`ephervex_pack::analyze` reads the manifest and checks names with `require_extractable_entry_names`, which uses `by_index_raw` and so never looks at encryption or compression.

## Reproduction

An mrpack or CurseForge export with one encrypted entry anywhere, for example a password-protected readme next to `overrides/`.

## Actual behavior

Analysis and preview succeed. Import creates the instance and downloads provider files, then fails when it starts extracting overrides.

## Expected behavior

Analysis and extraction agree. Either the analysis pre-flight checks encryption and compression method on every raw entry, or extraction skips entries outside the requested layer before opening them. A regression test covers an encrypted entry outside any layer.

## Locations

- `crates/pack/src/archive.rs` `extract_under`, `require_extractable_entry_names`
- `crates/pack/src/import.rs` `analyze`

## Related

#425 is the same pre-flight gap for server archives, for entry names.
issues.title: Pack analysis accepts archives with encrypted or unsupported-compression entries that override extraction refuses

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-cli`

**Commit:** `7bba579`

## Behavior

When a pack import fails on an archive-supplied path (`PackError::EntryPathUnsafe`, `EntryReserved`, `FileHashesMissing`, `FileDownloadsMissing`, `DownloadUrlRejected` and similar), the human-readable CLI error prints that path exactly as the archive wrote it. `terminal_safe` is applied to the import preview and summary but not to error output.

## Reproduction

A `modrinth.index.json` file entry with path `"../\u001b[2Jx.jar"`, then `ephervex import pack.mrpack --inspect`.

## Actual behavior

The error reads "the archive entry `../<ESC>[2Jx.jar` escapes the extraction directory" with a raw ESC byte, so a crafted pack can clear the screen or recolor the terminal through the error message.

## Expected behavior

Archive-supplied text in human-readable errors is escaped the same way as the import preview: control and bidirectional formatting characters are shown as visible escapes. JSON error output is already unaffected.

## Locations

- `crates/cli/src/main.rs` `terminal_safe` and the top-level error rendering

## Related

#408 escaped archive text in the import preview and summary.
issues.title: CLI import errors print archive entry paths with raw control characters

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-java`

**Commit:** `7bba579`

## Behavior

`forbidden_entry_type` (`crates/java/src/archive.rs`) lets `EntryType::XGlobalHeader` through, with a comment saying the `tar` crate applies GNU/PAX metadata entries to the entries that follow.

In `tar` 0.4.46, `EntriesFields::next_entry` consumes only GNU long name, GNU long link and PAX local extension (`x`) entries. A pax global header (`g`, such as the `pax_global_header` entry `git archive` emits) is returned as an ordinary entry.

It is neither a directory nor a symlink, so `extract_tar_gz_until_canceled` passes it to `extract_file`, which writes its metadata payload as a file and counts it in `report.files`, whenever `strip_components` does not consume its path.

## Expected behavior

Global headers are skipped explicitly (or refused), and the comment describes what the `tar` crate actually does.

## Locations

- `crates/java/src/archive.rs` `forbidden_entry_type`, `extract_tar_gz_until_canceled`
issues.title: Java archive extraction writes pax global header entries as regular files

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-server`

**Commit:** `7bba579`

## Behavior

The test starts a console write task, sleeps a fixed 200 ms, then sends Stop and expects the console request to be answered `Accepted`. Under CPU load the console request can reach the supervisor after the stop has begun.

## Actual behavior

```text
left: Refused("the server is stopping or restarting")
right: Accepted
```

Reproduced once in 20 runs of the `ephervex-server` lib test binary with 4 copies running at once.

## Expected behavior

The test waits until the console write is observably in progress instead of relying on a fixed sleep.

## Locations

- `crates/server/src/process.rs` test `a_stop_sent_during_a_console_write_is_carried_out_after_it`

## Related

#414 is a different server test with the same kind of load sensitivity.
issues.title: Server test `a_stop_sent_during_a_console_write_is_carried_out_after_it` fails intermittently under load

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-gui`

**Commit:** `7bba579`

## Behavior

`send_server_workspace` (`crates/gui/src/backend.rs`) fills absent keys with values of its own:

- `motd`: the localized `gui-default-motd` text;
- `max-players`: `20`;
- `difficulty`: `normal`;
- `gamemode`: `survival`;
- `allow-flight`, `pvp`, `white-list`: fixed booleans.

`server_property_values` (`crates/gui/src/controller.rs`) then writes all seven keys on every save.

## Reproduction

Use a server whose `server.properties` lacks some of these keys, for example a fresh server or a hand-trimmed file. Change only the port and press Save.

## Actual behavior

Every absent key is written. The MOTD becomes the user's locale text. Difficulty becomes `normal`, although vanilla's default is `easy`, so the server changes difficulty without the user choosing it. A pre-1.14 server reads difficulty and game mode only as integers and cannot parse the written text values.

## Expected behavior

What the form shows is what it saves. An absent key stays absent on save unless the user sets a value, or the form shows that the value is unset.

## Locations

- `crates/gui/src/backend.rs` `send_server_workspace`
- `crates/gui/src/controller.rs` `on_save_server_properties`, `server_property_values`

## Related

#250 fixed the same show-what-you-save problem for difficulty and game mode values that are present.
issues.title: The server Properties form writes values for keys server.properties never had

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-storage`

**Commit:** `7bba579`

## Behavior

`ClientRecord` and `ServerRecord` (`crates/storage/src/records.rs`) carry `root: PathBuf`, and `write_json` (`crates/storage/src/metadata.rs`) serializes them with `serde_json`. Serializing a path that is not valid UTF-8 fails, and `write_json` maps that failure to `MetadataError::Unwritable`.

## Reproduction

`XDG_DATA_HOME=$'/tmp/x/d\xff' ephervex instance create --persistent ...`

## Actual behavior

Exit 1 with `error-registry-metadata-unwritable` ("The instance metadata file could not be written.") and the detail "path contains invalid UTF-8 characters". The message points at writability instead of the real cause.

## Expected behavior

Decide whether such data roots are supported. Either support them, or refuse them early, when the data root is resolved, with a message that names the encoding.

## Locations

- `crates/storage/src/records.rs` `ClientRecord::root`, `ServerRecord::root`
- `crates/storage/src/metadata.rs` `write_json`
- `crates/storage/src/paths.rs` data root resolution

## Related

#295 (CLI `--json` panics on such paths), #260, #59.
issues.title: Instance creation fails under a data root whose path is not valid UTF-8, reported as unwritable metadata

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-pack`

## Behavior

`analyze` (`crates/pack/src/import.rs`) calls `PackArchive::require_extractable_entries("")`. With an empty prefix, `entry_under` (`crates/pack/src/archive.rs`) checks `is_reserved` against the full entry name only, so an entry such as `overrides/.launcher/x` passes: its first component is `overrides`.

`extract_layer_filtered` later calls `entry_under` with the layer prefix, strips it, and checks `is_reserved` on the relative name. `.launcher/x` is reserved, so extraction fails with `EntryReserved`.

## Impact

The archive passes analysis and preview, and import creates the instance and downloads the provider files before failing at override extraction, which the analysis check exists to prevent.

## Expected behavior

Analysis refuses every name that extraction of any layer it will extract would refuse, for example by also running the check with each override layer prefix (including any wrapper directory).

## Locations

- `crates/pack/src/import.rs` `analyze`
- `crates/pack/src/archive.rs` `require_extractable_entries`, `entry_under`, `extract_layer_filtered`

Related to #409, which added the analysis check for names outside any layer.
issues.title: Pack analysis does not refuse reserved names that appear only beneath an override layer

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-gui`

## Behavior

Opening Change Loader sets `loader-change-loading` and sends `Command::LoadLoaderVersions`. `loader_change_loading` is cleared only by `apply_loader_versions` on success. On failure, the backend reports the error through `send_modal_error`, which uses `ModalScope::Anywhere`.

## Actual behavior

- The dialog keeps showing the loading text, with no build list and no way to choose a build, until it is closed.
- Because the scope is `Anywhere`, if the user closed the dialog and opened another one before the failure arrived, the error is written into that unrelated dialog instead of appearing as a toast.

## Expected behavior

A failed build-list request ends the loading state of the dialog it was made for and shows the error there, or as a toast once that dialog is gone.

## Locations

- `crates/gui/src/backend.rs` `Command::LoadLoaderVersions`
- `crates/gui/src/controller.rs` `on_open_loader_change`, `apply_loader_versions`, `apply_modal_error`

Established from the code path.
issues.title: The Change Loader dialog shows loading forever when the build list cannot be fetched

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-gui`

## Behavior

`Command::ChangeLoaderVersion` reports its outcome with `ModalScope::LOADER_CHANGE`, which names the dialog but not the instance it was opened for. Cancel stays enabled while a change runs.

## Reproduction

1. Open Change Loader for instance A, choose a build, and press Change.
2. Press Cancel while the change runs, then open Change Loader for instance B.
3. A's change finishes.

## Actual behavior

- On failure, A's error is written into B's dialog and clears B's `loader-change-pending`.
- On success, `CloseModal(LOADER_CHANGE)` closes B's dialog.

## Expected behavior

Loader-change outcome events carry the instance (or a request id) and act on the dialog only while it is open for that instance. Otherwise the outcome is shown as a toast.

The same name-only scoping applies to other per-host dialogs that use `ModalScope`.

## Locations

- `crates/gui/src/backend.rs` `Command::ChangeLoaderVersion`
- `crates/gui/src/controller.rs` `apply_modal_error`, `close_modal_for`

Established from the code path. Related to #229 and #235, which scoped completions and loader lists to the dialog name.
issues.title: A finished loader change for one instance acts on the Change Loader dialog opened for another

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crates:** `ephervex-core`, `ephervex-storage`

## Behavior

`clone_into` (`crates/storage/src/clone.rs`) gives each snapshot directory the source directory's permissions, so a host directory with a read-only mode such as `0o555` stays read-only inside the snapshot.

Removal then uses plain `std::fs::remove_dir_all`, which fails with `EACCES` when unlinking entries inside a read-only directory:

- `delete_snapshot` and the cleanup of a failed snapshot's staging directory (`crates/core/src/snapshot.rs`) return `SnapshotError::Unwritable` and leave a partly deleted snapshot behind.
- `remove_path_if_present` (`crates/storage/src/restore.rs`) removes the live tree during a restore the same way, so a restore over a host with a read-only directory fails partway.

## Expected behavior

Removal restores owner access to directories (without following links) and retries, through one shared helper in `ephervex-storage`. `relocate::remove_tree_if_present` already does this.

## Tests

Delete and restore snapshots of trees containing a `0o555` directory.
issues.title: Deleting or restoring a snapshot fails when the host contains a read-only directory

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-mod-platform`

## Behavior

`CurseForgeProvider::compatible_files` (`crates/mod-platform/src/curseforge/browser.rs`) maps every file document with `mapping::version`, collecting into `ModPlatformResult`, and only afterwards keeps the files owned by the requested project.

`mapping::version` returns hard errors such as `FileUnavailable` (`isAvailable: false`) and `HashesMissing`.

## Actual behavior

If the `/v1/mods/{id}/files` response includes a file owned by another project that is unavailable or has no supported hash, the whole listing for the requested project fails, even though that file would have been dropped. Search skips the row, and the version callers return an error.

## Expected behavior

Files owned by other projects are dropped before mapping (compare the document's `modId` with the requested `CurseForgeProjectId`), so a foreign entry cannot fail a correct listing.

Related to #141.
issues.title: A CurseForge file listing fails as a whole when another project's file in it cannot be mapped

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crates:** `ephervex-gui`, `ephervex-core`, `ephervex-server`

## Behavior

On server Start, Launch & Connect, or a paired client Launch, the GUI resets every viewer on `LiveLogSource::Server` and sends `Command::OpenLiveLog`. `open_live_log` (`crates/gui/src/backend.rs`) answers with a `reset: true` snapshot from `App::server_output` -> `read_capture_snapshot` (`crates/core/src/server.rs`), which reads every `capture-*.jsonl` segment in the capture directory.

`CaptureWriter::open` (`crates/server/src/capture.rs`) keeps the existing segments across runs and only opens a new one. The start itself runs on a spawned thread, so `OpenLiveLog` is handled before the new run writes anything.

## Actual behavior

The reset Console is refilled with up to 2000 lines from earlier runs, and the new run's lines are then appended as `reset: false` updates with no run boundary.

## Expected behavior

A Console reset by a start shows only the current run, for example by scoping the snapshot to a run marker or segment boundary written at start, or by skipping earlier capture on the start path.

Related to #246, which made all start paths reset the Console.
issues.title: Starting a server refills its Console with earlier runs' output from retained capture

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-gui`

## Behavior

The GUI reopens viewers on `LiveLogSource::Server` (`Workspace::reopen_server_console` -> `LogViews::reopen`, `crates/gui/src/controller.rs`) only on the start paths: server Start, Launch & Connect, and a paired client Launch that starts its server.

A server Restart (`Command::RestartHost`, sent from `register_restart_actions`) also begins a new server run, but nothing reopens the Console on that path.

## Actual behavior

An open Console keeps the previous run's text, and the restarted run's lines are appended under it with no boundary.

## Expected behavior

Restart starts the server's Console and Logs viewers over the same way the start paths do.

Related to #246, which covered the start paths.
issues.title: Restarting a server does not start its Console over with the new run

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-mod-platform`

## Behavior

`a_refused_connection_is_an_outage_rather_than_an_unknown_project` (`crates/mod-platform/tests/modrinth_catalog.rs`) binds a loopback listener to pick a port and drops it before connecting. While the suite runs in parallel, another test's loopback server can take that port.

## Actual behavior

The lookup gets an answer and the test fails with `ProjectUnknown { provider: Modrinth, reference: "jei" }`. Observed once during a full `cargo test --workspace`; the immediate rerun of the unchanged tree passed.

## Expected behavior

The test uses an address no other test can take, for example by keeping the listener bound without accepting.
issues.title: A refused-connection test can reach another test's server and fail intermittently

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-auth`

## Behavior

`expiry` (`crates/auth/src/microsoft.rs`) computes `Utc::now() + TimeDelta::try_seconds(seconds).unwrap_or_default()`. `try_seconds` returns `None` only above about `i64::MAX / 1000` seconds. For values between about 8.3e12 and 9.2e15 seconds it returns `Some`, and `DateTime<Utc> + TimeDelta` overflows chrono's maximum date and panics.

`expires_in` comes from the service response. It feeds the device-code prompt's `expires_at` in `begin_device_code` and `TokenBody::into_tokens`.

## Actual behavior

A malformed response such as `"expires_in": 9000000000000` crashes sign-in instead of producing an error.

## Expected behavior

Use `Utc::now().checked_add_signed(delta)` and treat overflow as a malformed response (or clamp it), with a regression test for an `expires_in` in that range.
issues.title: A large service-supplied expires_in panics the sign-in expiry computation

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crates:** `ephervex-pack`, `ephervex-core`

## Behavior

The async `materialize_server_recipe` (`crates/pack/src/install.rs`) calls `apply_retained_overrides` (a `copy_retained_tree` of every retained override layer into the server game directory), `remove_retained_eula`, `copy_server_source` (another `copy_retained_tree` into the server source store), and `server_store.write_recipe` synchronously on the async worker, with no `spawn_blocking` and no cancellation checks. The token in `ServerMaterializeRequest.fetch.cancel` is checked only by `install_selected_files`.

The caller, `App::materialize_linked_server_recipe` (`crates/core/src/server.rs`), does not check the token after `materialize_server_recipe` returns.

## Actual behavior

- A large retained layer occupies a Tokio worker for the whole copy.
- A cancel that arrives after file installation is ignored: the copies run to completion and the server recipe is written.

## Expected behavior

Run the copy and recipe-write phases on a blocking thread, check the token between retained entries and again before writing the recipe, and return `PackError::Canceled`. Client pack import already follows this contract (#129).
issues.title: Server recipe materialization copies retained layers on async workers and ignores cancellation

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-download`

## Behavior

In a full `cargo test --workspace` run under heavy machine load, the `http_downloads` test binary stopped making progress after `a_batch_of_cached_artifacts_bounds_the_files_it_opens` reported running for over 60 seconds. The process stayed blocked on a futex with 18 threads and no CPU use for about 2.5 hours until it was killed. Run alone, the test passes in about 3 seconds.

The test (`crates/download/tests/http_downloads.rs`) runs on a current-thread Tokio runtime, seeds 300 cache files, and samples `/proc/self/fd` with a blocking `read_dir` every millisecond from a spawned task beside the hashing work. The cause was not isolated; starvation between the sampler and the batch is a likely candidate.

## Expected behavior

The test finishes or fails within a bounded time under load, without weakening the open-file bound it checks.
issues.title: Download test a_batch_of_cached_artifacts_bounds_the_files_it_opens hangs in a full workspace run

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-gui`

## Behavior

The Java, storage root, API identifier and artifact cache limit Save buttons (`crates/gui/ui/app.slint`) stay enabled after a click, so each further click queues another identical command. The artifact cache limit command waits in `cache_lane` behind any running cache measurement or eviction, so duplicate saves can pile up there.

## Expected behavior

These Save buttons are disabled while their save runs and show that a save is in progress, as the Minecraft defaults page already does with `MinecraftDefaultsModel::begin_save` and `is_saving`.
issues.title: Settings Save buttons stay usable while their save is in flight

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-server`

## Behavior

During a full `cargo test --workspace` run with other builds active on the machine, `runtime::tests::a_child_started_before_its_supervisor_died_is_found_by_the_run_tag` panicked at `crates/server/src/runtime.rs:1552` ("a tagged child is an orphan"): `classify_runtime` did not report the freshly spawned tagged child as an orphan. The test passed when rerun alone and in the following full workspace run.

The test classifies immediately after `spawn_tagged`, so it may observe the child before its run tag is visible. It should wait on observable child state rather than timing.

Like #414 and #429, this looks like a load-sensitive process test.
issues.title: Server test a_child_started_before_its_supervisor_died_is_found_by_the_run_tag fails intermittently under load

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-pack`

## Behavior

`normalize_file` (`crates/pack/src/modrinth.rs`) keeps every allowlisted address in a file's `downloads` array, with no limit on how many there are. `fetch_one_by_one` (`crates/pack/src/install.rs`), the fallback after a failed batch download, walks every address of every file in order, one request each.

## Impact

A compact hostile `.mrpack` index can declare a single file with hundreds of thousands of allowlisted but nonexistent addresses (for example `https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/x/versions/N/a.jar`), bounded only by the 64 MiB manifest-size limit. Once the batch fails, the importer makes that many sequential requests to the provider CDN.

`max_declared_files` does not cover this: it limits how many artifacts are declared, not how many addresses each one has.

## Expected behavior

An index whose per-file address count, or total address count across all files, exceeds an explicit `ExtractionLimits` ceiling is refused with `PackError::LimitExceeded` during normalization, with offline regression tests.
issues.title: Modrinth pack file download lists have no per-file or total address ceiling

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `608ed91b241bef9bbe395a35eb10540b3e2932ef`

## Behavior

The unit test `readiness_propagates_start_failure_exit_and_timeout_before_client_launch` (`crates/core/src/connection.rs`) binds a `std::net::TcpListener` on `127.0.0.1:0`, reads its port, and drops it. It then expects `ServerError::ReadinessTimeout` from `wait_for_managed_server` against that port.

The runtime evidence in the test records the test process itself as the server child, and `wait_for_server_readiness` treats the target as ready once that child listens on the port. Any loopback listener another test in the same test binary binds is owned by the same process.

## Actual behavior

While the suite runs in parallel, another test can bind the freed port. The readiness wait then succeeds instead of timing out and the test fails.

## Expected behavior

The test uses an address no other test can take, for example by keeping a bound, never-listening socket alive for the whole test.

Related to #439, the same flaw in an `ephervex-mod-platform` test.
issues.title: A readiness test in ephervex-core can take a port another test's listener reuses, and fail intermittently

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `608ed91b241bef9bbe395a35eb10540b3e2932ef`

## Behavior

`read_capture_snapshot` (`crates/core/src/server.rs`) lists the `capture-*.jsonl` segments in a server's capture directory and then reads each one with `std::fs::read`. Any read error, including `NotFound`, fails the whole snapshot with `ServerError::Io`.

While a server runs at its capture budget, the supervisor's `CaptureWriter::enforce_budget` (`crates/server/src/capture.rs`) removes the oldest segments. It can remove one after the listing and before the read.

## Actual behavior

`App::server_output` and `App::server_latest_run_output` fail. The GUI Console and the CLI server output show an error instead of the lines that are still retained.

## Expected behavior

A segment that disappears with `NotFound` between listing and reading is skipped, and the snapshot is reported as truncated, rather than failing the read.
issues.title: A server output snapshot fails as a whole when retention removes a segment while it is read

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-server`

**Commit:** `608ed91b241bef9bbe395a35eb10540b3e2932ef`

## Behavior

`CaptureWriter::open` (`crates/server/src/capture.rs`) names a run's first segment from `Utc::now()` without looking at the newest retained segment. Rotations within one writer stay monotonic (`rotate` uses the later of now and the current segment's instant plus 1 ms), but a new writer does not.

Segment name order is relied on by retention pruning (`existing_segments` sorts by path), by the order of the retained snapshot, and by latest-run detection in `read_capture_snapshot` (`crates/core/src/server.rs`), where `CaptureScope::LatestRun` picks the newest segment that does not continue a run.

## Actual behavior

If the system clock steps backwards between two supervised runs (NTP correction, manual change), the new run's first segment sorts before the previous run's segments. The GUI Console then shows the earlier run instead of the current one, and pruning can delete the current run's segments first.

## Expected behavior

A new run's first segment always sorts after every retained segment, for example by seeding its instant with the later of `Utc::now()` and the newest retained segment's instant plus 1 ms.
issues.title: Server capture segments sort out of creation order when the clock steps backwards between runs

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crates:** `ephervex-gui`, `ephervex-server`

**Commit:** `608ed91b241bef9bbe395a35eb10540b3e2932ef`

## Behavior

The server Console loads only the latest run's capture (`App::server_latest_run_output`), and `read_capture_snapshot` reports no retention loss when the latest run's first segment is still retained.

The live path does not make that distinction. `forward_server_event` (`crates/gui/src/backend.rs`) turns every `ServerEvent::CapturePruned` into a `LiveLogUpdate` with `source_truncated: true`.

## Actual behavior

When the capture budget prunes segments that belong only to earlier runs, an open Console is marked truncated although none of the run it shows was lost. Reopening the same Console shows it as not truncated.

## Expected behavior

The live Console is marked truncated only when a prune removed part of the run it shows, for example by having `CaptureWriter::enforce_budget` report whether the pruned segments reached the current run's start segment.
issues.title: An open server Console is marked truncated when only earlier runs' capture was pruned

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crates:** `ephervex-gui`, `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `608ed91b241bef9bbe395a35eb10540b3e2932ef`

## Behavior

Live server lines reach the GUI only through the in-process forwarders in `crates/gui/src/backend.rs` (`spawn_server` and the Launch & Connect server forward task). Those exist only when this GUI process started the supervisor.

A server started elsewhere, for example with `ephervex server start` from the CLI, is still controlled, and the GUI offers Restart and Stop for it.

## Actual behavior

The Console of such a server only receives the one-time snapshot from `open_live_log`. No live lines arrive. The GUI never sees `ServerEvent::Restarting` for it either, so a restart sent from the GUI neither starts the Console over nor refreshes it.

## Expected behavior

The Console follows the server's capture whichever process supervises it, for example by following the capture directory through `ephervex-core`, or it makes clear that it shows a static snapshot and refreshes after a Restart.

Related to #341, which covers adopting a server after the process that supervised it exits.
issues.title: The GUI Console of a server supervised by another process never shows new output

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `608ed91b241bef9bbe395a35eb10540b3e2932ef`

## Behavior

`App::install_server_archive` (`crates/core/src/server_pack.rs`) checks the cancellation token once, right after the blocking extraction. Two slow async steps follow:

- `measure_installed_mods` hashes every installed jar;
- `identify_installed_mods` runs CurseForge fingerprinting and Modrinth requests.

Neither turns a cancel into a failure. `identify_installed_mods` only skips catalog lookups once canceled and still returns an outcome, and `PackError::Canceled` from `recognize_with_curseforge` is reported as CurseForge being unavailable. `install_server_archive` then writes the server recipe and returns `Ok`.

Its callers, `create_server_holding_the_cache` and `install_server_holding_the_cache` (`crates/core/src/server.rs`), go on to `publish_staged_server` / `update_server_committed` without checking the token.

## Actual behavior

Pressing Cancel while a large archive's mods are measured or identified publishes the server and reports it as created.

## Expected behavior

The token is checked after identification and before the recipe write, and the install returns `PackError::Canceled`. A canceled create or install publishes nothing and discards the staging root, as the linked-recipe path does.
issues.title: Canceling a server created from a server-pack archive while its mods are measured or identified still publishes the server

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-server`

**Commit:** `608ed91b241bef9bbe395a35eb10540b3e2932ef`

## Behavior

In a full `cargo test --workspace` run, with other Cargo builds running on the machine, `runtime::tests::a_pending_start_that_left_no_process_behind_can_be_cleared_without_editing_files` (`crates/server/src/runtime.rs`) failed: `classify_runtime` did not return `RuntimeClassification::ProvenStale`.

The test passed 3 of 3 times when run alone with `cargo test -p ephervex-server --lib a_pending_start_that_left_no_process`.

The fixture `write_dead_pending_start` writes a pending start for the current supervisor (the test process) with `start_ticks = 0`. Other tests in the same binary spawn child processes of that same process (for example through `spawn_tagged`), so the classification likely depends on process-table state those tests change.

## Expected behavior

The test is isolated from processes other tests spawn concurrently, or the classification is shown not to depend on them.
issues.title: Server test a_pending_start_that_left_no_process_behind_can_be_cleared_without_editing_files fails intermittently in a full workspace run

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-mod-platform`

**Commit:** `608ed91b241bef9bbe395a35eb10540b3e2932ef`

## Behavior

`ModrinthProvider::versions` (`crates/mod-platform/src/modrinth.rs`) maps every raw version with `mapping::version`, which can fail with `HashesMissing` or `AmbiguousPrimaryFile`. Only afterwards does `ModProvider::project_versions` (`crates/mod-platform/src/provider.rs`) drop entries whose `project_id` is another project's.

## Actual behavior

An entry owned by another project can fail the whole listing, although it would have been dropped from the result.

## Expected behavior

## Behavior

`Resolver::normalize_all` (`crates/mod-platform/src/resolve.rs`) looks up every relation that names a version but no project in one `versions_by_id` batch, whatever the relation's kind, including `ModRelationKind::Optional`. The batch result is propagated with `?`.

A version the provider does not know is now reported as `OptionalStatus::Unverified(UnverifiedOptional::UnknownIdentity)`. A failed batch is not: a transport or credential failure, or a content refusal such as `HashesMissing` or `AmbiguousPrimaryFile` for the pinned release, fails the plan.

An unselected optional extra that pins only a version can fail the install the user asked for, while the same optional dependency naming a project degrades to an unverified offer. Embedded and incompatible relations that name both a project and a version already go through `lookup_owners`, which tolerates content refusals.

## Expected behavior

A failed lookup for an unselected optional relation that pins only a version is reported as an unverified offer rather than failing the plan. Cancellation still stops the plan, and a selected optional still goes through strict resolution.

Related to #151, which separated optional lookup failures from incompatibility for relations that name a project.

## Behavior

The doc comment promises that a refused value leaves the file and the stored network settings as they were, but that only holds for validation failures.

**Commit:** `beee756`

## Behavior

`crates/download/tests/http_downloads.rs::the_file_named_beside_a_batch_count_advances_with_it` failed once during a full `cargo test --workspace` run:

```
the name beside `7 of 8` is not the file that count refers to
  left: Some("file-4.jar")
 right: Some("file-1.jar")
```

The snapshot had count 7 but already named `file-4.jar`, the file whose gate is released last. It passed when the whole workspace was rerun and in about 270 isolated and parallel runs of the test binary.

## Analysis

`DownloadManager::download_all` publishes the count and the name together from the same completion (`set_batch_items_at`), so the two can only disagree like this if `file-4.jar` completed seventh, before the test released its gate. That points at the test harness rather than the reporter, for example how `GatedServer` arrivals map to gates (a repeated arrival for a route would replace and drop the earlier gate in the test's `HashMap`). This is not confirmed.

## Expected behavior

The test passes deterministically, or the product race it exposes is identified and fixed.

## Behavior

`Resolver::normalize_all` (`crates/mod-platform/src/resolve.rs`) sends every non-optional relation that pins a version and names no project, including `Embedded` and `Incompatible`, through one strict `versions_by_id` batch whose result is propagated with `?`. A transport failure or a content refusal (`HashesMissing`, `AmbiguousPrimaryFile`, `FileUnavailable`) for the pinned release fails the plan.

The same embedded or incompatible relation naming both a project and a version goes through `lookup_owners`, which tolerates content refusals.

## Actual behavior

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-server`

**Commit:** `beee756`

## Behavior

After #414 replaced the fixed sleep with a gate, `process::tests::a_stop_that_meets_a_child_already_exiting_reports_the_real_exit` failed once in a `cargo test -p ephervex-server` run with a different panic, at `crates/server/src/process.rs` `result.as_ref().expect_err("a closed input")` (`a closed input: ()`). The pending stop write succeeded instead of returning `BrokenPipe`. It passed in three isolated reruns.

## Analysis

The test assumes that once the child prints `input-closed` after `exec 0<&-`, no process holds the read end of its stdin pipe, so a write must fail with `BrokenPipe`. A successful write means some process still had the read end open at that moment. Under parallel load that assumption does not hold reliably, for example if a child spawned concurrently by another test in the same process briefly inherits the descriptor before its `exec`.

## Expected behavior

The test passes deterministically: either it does not depend on the write failing, or it guarantees no other process can hold the pipe's read end.

Follow-up to #414.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-gui`

**Commit:** `beee756`

## Behavior

When a server Console is opened (or reopened through a tail restart) while this GUI process supervises the server, two paths deliver lines with no common ordering point:

- `follow_server_capture` (`crates/gui/src/backend.rs`) always sends its first poll as a reset snapshot; the read and the send are separate steps;
- the in-process forwarder (`spawn_server` / `spawn_connect` through `forward_output_batch` and `send_server_lines`) sends the same lines as incremental updates. The supervisor writes a line to the capture before emitting `ServerEvent::Output`.

## Actual behavior

The outcome depends on which side queues first for a line written around the follower's first read:

- **Duplicate:** the line is in the capture read, the reset is queued, and then the forwarder's update for the same line arrives. The Console shows it twice.
- **Lost:** the line is written right after the read, the forwarder queues its update first, and the reset then replaces the history with a snapshot that lacks it. The follower sends nothing more while the forwarding mark is held, so the line never appears.

The window is small but applies to every Console opened while this process supervises the server.

## Expected behavior

Every captured line appears exactly once. The snapshot and the forwarder need one ordering point, for example taking the snapshot from the supervisor's own ring under the capture lock, having the follower record its capture position so the forwarder skips lines at or before it, tagging forwarded lines with capture positions, or routing the in-process run through the follower as well.

Related to #450 and #16.
issues.title: A server Console opened during an in-process run can show a line twice or lose it

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crates:** `ephervex-storage`, `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `79561f5`

## Behavior

`ephervex_storage::atomic::write_atomic` (`crates/storage/src/atomic.rs`) renames the temporary file over the destination and then calls `sync_parent(path)`. If that directory fsync fails (for example with `EIO`), the function returns `Err` even though the rename succeeded and the new contents are already visible.

`metadata::write_server_metadata` passes this error up, so `Registry::update_server_committed` (`crates/storage/src/registry.rs`) returns `Err` and skips the index `UPDATE`. Callers then treat the mutation as not committed. For example, `App::commit_or_restore_properties` (`crates/core/src/server.rs`) restores the previous `server.properties`, while `.launcher/server.json` already holds the new network settings and the index still holds the old ones.

## Actual behavior

After a save whose directory sync fails, canonical metadata, the index and `server.properties` can disagree.

## Expected behavior

Callers can tell "not published" apart from "published but not durably synced". For example, report a post-rename sync failure as a separate durability warning, or as a distinct error that callers handle as committed.
issues.title: A failed directory sync after the rename reports a metadata write as failed although the new file is already published

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-gui`

**Commit:** `79561f5`

## Behavior

`follow_server_capture` (`crates/gui/src/backend.rs`) restarts a server's tail by setting the previous thread's stop flag and spawning a new follower thread. The old thread checks the stop flag only at the top of its loop, before it takes the per-server `ConsoleDelivery` lock and polls.

## Scenario

1. The old follower passes its stop check and waits for the delivery lock.
2. The Console is reopened. The new follower takes the lock first and sends its reset snapshot.
3. The old follower gets the lock, polls from its stale position, and sends a non-reset update (and records it with `note_sent`).

The lines in that update are already in the new snapshot, so the Console shows them twice. This applies whenever the run is not being forwarded by this process, for example a server started by another process.

## Expected behavior

A stopped follower never sends after its replacement started. For example, re-check the stop flag after taking the delivery lock and before polling or sending.

Related to #465.
issues.title: Reopening a server Console can append a stale update from the previous capture follower after the new snapshot

## Behavior

`processor_values` (`crates/loaders/src/install.rs`) builds `ROOT`, `LIBRARY_DIR`, `INSTALLER` and `MINECRAFT_JAR` with `Path::to_string_lossy()`. `resolve_coordinate` and `resolve_data_value` (installer data entries under the data directory) do the same.

These strings are substituted into Forge and NeoForge installer processor command lines. On Linux a non-UTF-8 component in the cache root or workspace becomes U+FFFD, so the processor JVM receives a different pathname than the one Ephervex prepared.

## Expected behavior

The processor command path refuses a non-UTF-8 path with a typed loader error, as the launch command does with `LaunchError::PathNotUtf8` since #59, instead of passing an altered path. A regression test should use a path component containing byte `0xff`.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `79561f5`

## Behavior

`crates/core/src/app.rs` writes user-chosen paths into the configuration with `to_string_lossy()`:

- `java.preferred_path` in `set_java_settings`;
- the persistent instance root setting;
- `watched_download_folders`.

On Linux a path containing a non-UTF-8 byte is saved as a different path containing U+FFFD. The current session uses the real path, but the next start reads back a different, nonexistent one. For the instance root this can point the next start at the wrong storage location.

## Expected behavior

These setters refuse a non-UTF-8 path with a typed, actionable error before anything is saved, or store it losslessly. Regression tests should use a path component containing byte `0xff`.

Related to #431.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-download`

**Commit:** `79561f5`

## Behavior

`DownloadError::Transport` (`crates/download/src/error.rs`) stores a redacted `url` label, but its `#[source] reqwest::Error` still holds the full request URL. reqwest appends ` for url (<full url>)` to its `Display`, including the query string, and after a redirect it may show the final URL. The construction sites in `crates/download/src/manager.rs` (the request send and the body chunk read) never call `reqwest::Error::without_url()`.

`ErrorChain` (`crates/core/src/error.rs`) walks `source()` and appends every cause's `Display`. Its doc comment says every URL a download error names is already redacted, which is not true for this cause. `ErrorChain` is used in GUI logs such as `modpack link download failed` and `GUI operation failed` (`crates/gui/src/backend.rs`) and in `crates/core/src/launch.rs`.

## Impact

A connection, TLS, timeout or truncated-body failure on a signed or token-bearing download URL writes the secret query to the log.

## Expected behavior

The URL is stripped from reqwest errors (`without_url()`) or redacted wherever `DownloadError::Transport` is built. A regression test should show that the `ErrorChain` of a transport failure on a `?token=` URL does not contain the token.
issues.title: Download transport errors keep the unredacted URL in their reqwest source, which ErrorChain logs

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-download`

**Commit:** `79561f5`

## Behavior

`DomainAllowlist::validate(raw)` (`crates/download/src/allowlist.rs`) returns `UrlPolicyError::Malformed { url: raw.trim().to_owned() }` when the URL fails to parse. `DownloadRequest::parse` (`crates/download/src/manager.rs`) does the same. Every other `UrlPolicyError` variant, built from a parsed URL, goes through `redacted`.

This puts an untrusted, possibly query-bearing string unredacted into an error that callers display or log. Callers include the options feed's Gist `raw_url` fallback (`gist_body` in `crates/options/src/feed.rs`) and other user- or remote-supplied URLs.

## Expected behavior

`Malformed` reports a fixed placeholder or a safely truncated form instead of the raw input. A test should assert that the error text omits a `?token=` value.
issues.title: A URL that fails to parse is echoed unredacted in UrlPolicyError::Malformed

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crates:** `ephervex-options`, `ephervex-download`

**Commit:** `79561f5`

## Behavior

`OptionsFeed::cached` and `OptionsFeed::is_fresh` (`crates/options/src/feed.rs`) peek the metadata envelope and, if `OptionsDataset::parse` fails, call `MetadataCache::invalidate` (`crates/download/src/metadata.rs`). That removes whatever file is at the envelope path, unconditionally and without the entry's `<key>.lock`.

## Scenario

1. Process B peeks an unusable entry.
2. Process A publishes a valid newer revision through `MetadataCache::store_if`.
3. B's `invalidate` deletes A's valid publication.

The next refresh then sees no cached revision, so the rollback check has nothing to compare against and an older revision served by the source can be stored.

`discard_unless_replaced` in `crates/download/src/publication.rs` guards against the same stale-verdict discard for artifacts.

## Expected behavior

The discard runs under the entry lock and re-checks the entry, or removes the file only if it is still the one that was inspected (by file identity).

Related to #359.
issues.title: The options feed can delete another process's newer cache entry when it discards one it could not parse

issues.bodyMarkdown:

## Behavior

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-storage`

**Commit:** `57f5739`

## Behavior

`Registry::update_client` (`crates/storage/src/registry.rs`) calls `metadata::write_client_metadata`, which writes `.launcher/instance.json` through the strict `write_json` path (`crates/storage/src/metadata.rs`). If the directory fsync after the rename fails (for example with `EIO`), `write_json` returns `Err` although the new `instance.json` is already visible.

`update_client` then returns `Err` and skips `update_client_row`. Canonical client metadata holds the new values, the SQLite index holds the old ones, and callers (including `modify_client`) treat the mutation as not committed.

Servers already handle this case: `update_server_committed` uses `publish_server_metadata`, still updates the index and reports `ServerCommitWarning::MetadataNotDurable`. The client path did not get the same handling.

## Expected behavior

A client update whose `instance.json` was published but not durably synced is treated as committed: the index is updated and the durability failure is reported as a warning, as for servers. Reconciliation eventually repairs the index from canonical metadata, but until then the result callers see is wrong.

Follow-up to #466, which was fixed for the server path only.
issues.title: A failed directory sync after the rename still reports a client metadata update as failed and skips the index

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-download`

**Commit:** `57f5739`

## Behavior

`discard_unless_replaced` (`crates/download/src/publication.rs`) runs its compare-and-remove on a `spawn_blocking` task. Its callers keep the inspected file open so its inode number cannot be reused while the identity is compared:

- the stored artifact handle in `DownloadManager` (`crates/download/src/manager.rs`, the comment "`stored` stays open across the discard, which keeps the inode unique");
- `InspectedMetadata` in `MetadataCache::discard` (`crates/download/src/metadata.rs`).

The blocking closure captures only the path and the `FileIdentity`, not that handle. If the awaiting future is dropped (for example by a timeout or `select!`), the handle closes while the detached blocking task may still be waiting for the directory lock.

## Scenario

1. A discard is awaited for an inspected file; its blocking task waits on the directory lock.
2. The awaiting future is dropped, closing the inspected handle.
3. A concurrent publication had already replaced the inspected file, so its inode is freed.
4. A later publication reuses the same inode number and is renamed into place before the blocking task takes the lock.
5. The blocking task sees a matching identity and removes the new, valid file.

The window is small and needs cancellation, inode reuse and a contended lock together.

## Expected behavior

The inspected handle lives as long as the blocking comparison: move it into the blocking closure, or otherwise tie its lifetime to the blocking task rather than to the awaiting future.

Related: #472, #47.
issues.title: Canceling an identity-checked cache discard can close the inode guard before the comparison runs

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-gui`

**Commit:** `57f5739`

## Behavior

In `snapshot()` (`crates/gui/src/backend.rs`), `connection_states` is filled only while iterating the listed clients, for servers whose `linked_client_id` matches one of them. A server whose `linked_client_id` points to a client that is no longer listed gets no entry, so its row keeps `can_connect = false` and an empty `connect_reason`.

`app.slint` shows the Launch Client and Connect button whenever `linked-client-id != ""` (Servers page and the server overview pane), so the button is shown disabled with no explanation.

## Expected behavior

When the linked client cannot be found, the button either carries a reason saying so or is not shown.

Remaining case of #261.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-storage`

**Commit:** `57f5739`

## Behavior

`path_to_sql` (`crates/storage/src/registry.rs`) stores `record.root` with `to_string_lossy()`.

### Orphaned client

When reconciliation reindexes an orphaned client (`crates/storage/src/reconcile.rs`, around line 715), it sets `record.root` to the discovered directory and calls `index_existing_client`, which inserts the row through `path_to_sql`. If the directory name contains a byte that is not valid UTF-8, the index row records a path with U+FFFD in it. The CLI test `reconcile_reports_a_reindexed_root_whose_name_is_not_valid_utf8` (`crates/cli/tests/json_path_encoding_cli.rs`) creates exactly this case and expects success.

That indexed path does not exist, so:

- the next reconciliation sees the indexed root as missing;
- a later `update_client` on the record fails while serializing the root into `instance.json`, reported as `MetadataError::Unwritable`.

### Orphaned server

The orphaned-server reindex path (around line 869) calls `write_server_metadata` with the non-UTF-8 root. Serialization fails, and the whole reconciliation pass aborts with the same mislabeled unwritable-metadata error.

## Expected behavior

Creation, duplication and moves already refuse such roots with `PathError::NotUtf8` in `ensure_free_root`. Reconciliation should refuse and report such a root the same way (`error-paths-not-utf8`) instead of indexing it, or store it losslessly. Mapping a serde path-encoding failure in `publish_json` to `PathError::NotUtf8` would also stop the error being mislabeled as unwritable metadata.

Follow-up to #431, which covered creation only.
issues.title: Reconciliation indexes a host root whose name is not valid UTF-8 under a different path

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-core`

**Commit:** `57f5739`

## Behavior

`App::set_server_runtime_settings` (`crates/core/src/server.rs`) stores `java_override` directly and calls `update_server_committed`. A `JavaOverride` whose path contains a byte that is not valid UTF-8 fails while `server.json` is serialized and is reported as `MetadataError::Unwritable` instead of `PathError::NotUtf8` (`error-paths-not-utf8`).

The client equivalent, `App::set_client_runtime_settings` (`crates/core/src/app.rs`), checks the path with `ephervex_storage::utf8_path` before claiming and writing, and stores a relative path as an absolute one. The server setter does neither.

No CLI or GUI caller passes a Java override to the server setter today, but it is a public core API.

## Expected behavior

The server setter refuses a non-UTF-8 Java path with `PathError::NotUtf8` before writing, and makes a relative path absolute, as the client setter does. Add a regression test with a `0xff` path byte.

Related: #431, #469, #284.
issues.title: Setting a server's Java override does not refuse a non-UTF-8 path or make a relative path absolute

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-gui`

**Commit:** `57f5739`

## Behavior

`ServerPropertiesForm` (`crates/gui/ui/workspace/host-settings.slint`) enables Save only when `host.server.state-kind == "stopped"`.

`ServerTools::stamp` (`crates/gui/src/controller/server_tools.rs`) rewrites a stopped server row's `state_kind` to `"failed"` while its lifecycle phase is `Phase::Failed`, which is set when a server run ends in failure (`apply_server_tool_event` -> `lifecycle.servers.apply`). The runtime is still `RuntimeClassification::Stopped`, so the properties could be saved safely, but Save stays disabled. The hint `gui-hint-save-server-failed` tells the user to start the server again and stop it first.

Right after a failed run is when a user most likely needs to edit `server.properties`, for example after a crash caused by a port conflict. Starting a server that fails to start just to unlock Save does not work as a workaround.

## Expected behavior

Save is available for a stopped server whose previous run failed. Check the enabled condition against the runtime classification, or treat `"failed"` like `"stopped"`, instead of the stamped display state. Update or remove the `gui-hint-save-server-failed` hint to match.
issues.title: Server Properties Save is disabled for a stopped server whose last run failed

issues.bodyMarkdown:
In `crates/i18n/locales/en-US/main.ftl` (around line 768), the translator comment `# $code is the process exit status.` sits directly above `launch-exited-cleanly = Minecraft exited normally.`, which takes no arguments. The message that takes `$code` is the next one, `launch-exited-with-code = Minecraft exited with code { $code }.`.

Evidence at 57f5739: main.ftl:768-770 confirmed. A scan of every `$var` translator comment in main.ftl against the message directly below it found this as the only other mismatch besides #457.

Acceptance criteria: the comment sits directly above `launch-exited-with-code`, and no translator comment in main.ftl describes a variable that the message directly below it does not take.

Related: #457 fixes the same kind of defect for `$value` comments; different messages and lines.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
The credential change order (CredentialChangeLock with a 30 second patience, reached through ConfigDirectoryOrder::hold in crates/core/src/account.rs, and ProcessChangeOrder, a std Mutex, in crates/auth/src/order.rs) is taken synchronously from async code. Callers: App::login (finish_keyring_cleanup, adopt_login which holds the order and then writes config under it), finish_pending_cleanup, and the resume/refresh paths inside the ephervex-auth token chain. A contended order blocks a tokio worker, and every task scheduled on it, for up to 30 seconds.

It cannot simply be moved to spawn_blocking at the call sites: CredentialChangeGuard wraps Box<dyn Any> and is not Send, and adopt_login holds the guard across the sign-in's configuration write. Holding any blocking-wait lock across an await on a current-thread runtime makes a synchronous waiter on the same thread wait for a holder that cannot run.

Acceptance: waiting for the credential order does not stall other tasks on a current-thread runtime, and the order's critical section does not span an await point (or the order is async-safe). Add a regression test that holds the order from another thread or process and shows other tasks keep running.

Related but distinct from #302 (launch lock and configuration write lock). Evidence at 57f5739: crates/auth/src/order.rs (CredentialChangeGuard, ProcessChangeOrder), crates/core/src/account.rs (adopt_login, finish_pending_cleanup, hold_credential_changes), crates/storage/src/config.rs (CredentialChangeLock::take, CREDENTIAL_LOCK_PATIENCE).

<!-- ephervex-followup:9e1774a5-fad8-44c3-ad22-8e6e9d198f52 -->
issues.title: The credential change order waits synchronously on async runtime workers

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
Registry::update_client_committed (crates/storage/src/registry.rs) publishes .launcher/instance.json, which is the commit point under ADR 0002, and then calls update_client_row with `?`. If that UPDATE fails (SQLite busy/IO error, or 0 rows changed, which becomes RegistryError::InstanceUnknown), the function returns Err even though the new canonical metadata is already visible. update_client and modify_client then report the mutation as not committed to callers in core (rename, settings, attention updates, snapshot restore, relocate_client), while the files on disk hold the new values. Startup reconciliation later adopts the canonical metadata, so a change the user was told had failed reappears.

Servers already handle this: update_server_committed and publish_staged_server turn an index failure after the metadata commit into ServerCommitWarning::IndexOutOfSync on a committed result.

Acceptance: after a successful metadata publication, an index-mirror failure on a client update is a commit warning on a committed result (for example ClientCommitWarning::IndexOutOfSync), not an Err. Add a regression test that forces the row update to fail after the metadata is published.

Related: #476 (unsynced directory after rename) adds ClientCommitWarning and Registry::update_client_committed; once it is merged, this extends the same type. Until then the same code path is in crates/storage/src/registry.rs update_client.

<!-- ephervex-followup:527b9c92-d389-49a9-915b-9ff005acb356 -->
issues.title: A client update whose index write fails after instance.json was published is reported as failed

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
Registry::update_client_committed (crates/storage/src/registry.rs) returns Vec<ClientCommitWarning> with ClientCommitWarning::MetadataNotDurable when .launcher/instance.json was published but its directory fsync failed. No production caller uses it: core client mutations (app.rs rename/settings paths, instance.rs, verify.rs, snapshot.rs restore) and Registry::modify_client all go through update_client, which drops the warnings after a tracing::warn.

Servers carry ServerCommitWarning::MetadataNotDurable through ServerCommit<ServerRecord> into core and the CLI's print_server_commit (stderr text and a `metadata_not_durable` JSON entry). Client mutations in core should return their commit warnings in the same way, so the CLI (including --json output) and the GUI can tell the user the change was saved but may not survive a power loss.

Dependency: this builds on the change for #476, which introduces ClientCommitWarning and update_client_committed. That change is reviewed but may not be on main yet; check main before starting and wait for or build on it.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
The light color scheme has many controls that are unreadable or inconsistent with the dark scheme. Dark is the reference look. The findings below come from comparing the dark and light 1920x1080 captures of every screen in the documentation screenshot set (63 screens plus their sub-captures; screenshots live in ephervex-doc-screenshots/tools/auto-screenshot-tool/screenshots, regenerate with the screenshot tool). Several screens show the same defect, so the fix belongs in shared components and palette tokens, not per-screen patches.

## Defects, most severe first

1. **Switch that is on has no visible knob in light (high).** Every `Toggle` that is on renders as a flat teal pill. Likely cause: in the light palette `toggle-on` and `accent` are both #15707a, and the knob of a checked switch is drawn in `accent` over a `toggle-on` track (`components/controls.slint`, `Toggle`). The off state (pale track, dark knob) looks like a different control. Seen on: settings (General, Java, Minecraft defaults), mod manager rows, mod impact, install plan, isolation setup, create server dialogs, diagnostic bundle selection, client settings, snapshot restore dialog, import dialogs, theme screens.
2. **Interface theme popup is unreadable in light (high).** In the open dropdown the entries "Dark", "Midnight Blueprint" and the selected "Light" are near-white on light gray. Other combo boxes on the page lose their chevron and border while the popup is open. The popup covers the "Diagnostics and console text" combo. Capture: theme-selector-open.
3. **Primary button labels have low contrast in light (medium-high, every screen).** The label of `AppButton` with `tone: "primary"` uses `Theme.text` (near-black in light) on the #15707a fill, roughly 3:1. Affects Launch, Install, Search, Save, Create, Sign in, Start, Stop, the selected "All" chip and similar. There is no token for text on a primary fill.
4. **Combo boxes and text inputs do not match (medium).** In light, closed dropdowns are near-white and almost borderless while text inputs next to them are gray-filled with faint borders, and gray inputs look disabled. In dark both share one treatment. Seen in settings (Minecraft defaults, Storage, Java), create instance/server dialogs, client mods filter, accounts offline name.
5. **Destructive buttons are much louder in light (medium).** Kill Instance, Remove..., Forget, Delete, Stop Game, Cancel isolation, Restore snapshot confirm are solid saturated red with white text; dark uses a muted tinted outline. The restore confirm button looks identical to Delete.
6. **Dialog and overlay scrims are too weak in light (medium).** The page behind modal dialogs and the file drop overlay stays fairly legible and looks washed out (light `scrim` is alpha 0x73, dark is 0x99). Selected sidebar item nearly vanishes under the scrim. Scrim strength also differs between light dialogs (Make Persistent vs mod dialogs).
7. **Standard widgets use their own accent (low).** The Field of view slider handle/track (Minecraft defaults) and the busy spinner (diagnostics-working) are blue in light and teal or blue in dark instead of the Ephervex accent.
8. **Other low-severity light-mode issues.**
   - Context menu (instance actions) is near-white on near-white with only a thin border.
   - Log viewer panel (crash reports, live logs, split workspace) is the same gray as the page, while dark has a distinct darker panel.
   - Scrollbar thumbs are heavy in light and nearly invisible in dark; make both consistent.
   - Warning text (amber/olive), "Temporary"/"Persistent"/"Starting" labels and the isolation banner are low contrast or drab on light surfaces.
   - Row/card fills in mod manager, install plan, impact and isolation setup look sunken (darker than the panel) instead of defined by borders.
   - Selected sidebar entry and "CurseForge/Modrinth" segmented selection are weak in light.
   - Toast and card shadows are barely visible in light.
   - Disabled buttons are faint and hard to tell from secondary buttons in both schemes.
   - Log-level filter chips (All, INFO, WARN...) show selected and unselected in the same teal in both schemes (split-workspace, server console).

## Expected behavior

Every control reads clearly in both built-in palettes, and the light palette follows the same visual hierarchy as the dark one: a switch that is on shows a distinct knob, primary and destructive buttons have readable labels and comparable weight, dropdowns (closed and open) and text inputs share one field treatment, scrims dim the page comparably, and std widgets follow the Ephervex accent.

## Constraints (see AGENTS.md, User interface)

- Colors only in `palettes.slint`; components read `Theme` tokens and never branch on the active palette. No literal colors or font sizes in markup.
- A new color token (for example for text on a primary fill, or the knob of a switch) is added to `Theme` with a comment, to `ThemePalette`, to every built-in palette, and documented in `docs/themes.md`. Never rename or remove an existing token.
- The std-widget palette scheme stays driven by the palette's `widget-scheme`. The popup defect (2) needs a root-cause check of how the ComboBox popup picks up its palette, not a color workaround.
- Do not change dark appearance except where a shared fix requires it.

## Acceptance criteria

- Each defect above is fixed or, for a low-severity item judged intentional, explicitly noted in the commit or docs.
- Regenerate the light and dark captures for the affected screens (at least: settings General, theme-selector-open, mod-manager, create-server-standalone, diagnostic-bundle-selection, snapshot-restore-dialog, instances-overview, split-workspace) and compare them against dark.
- Where practical, add a test that every built-in palette keeps required token pairs apart (for example the knob of a checked switch differs from its track) and that primary label contrast meets a minimum ratio.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` pass.


<!-- ephervex-followup:7d206358-ca17-4115-a838-24e6fe41ba35 -->
issues.title: Light color scheme has unreadable or inconsistent controls compared to dark (toggles, dropdown popup, primary buttons, scrims)

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
Registry::modify_client (crates/storage/src/registry.rs) and core mutations that do `let mut record = self.client(id)?; ...; registry.update_client(&mut record)` (rename_client in crates/core/src/instance.rs, app.rs settings updates, verify.rs, and launch.rs/loader.rs/mods.rs/mutation.rs via modify_client) read the record from the SQLite index row. The same applies to servers (self.server(id) + update_server).

Under ADR 0002, instance.json/server.json is canonical and the index row can lag it. An index write that fails after metadata publication is reported as ClientCommitWarning::IndexOutOfSync / ServerCommitWarning::IndexOutOfSync on a committed result. Until the next startup reconciliation, any later read-modify-write in the same session reads the stale row, applies its own change, and republishes the stale fields over the newer canonical metadata.

Example: a rename commits to instance.json, the index UPDATE fails (SQLite busy/IO), and the user is told the rename succeeded. A launch then records last_launched_at through modify_client, which reads name=old from the index and publishes it, so the reported rename is silently lost.

modify_client's doc comment says the record is read immediately before the write so only the fields the change touches differ from what is stored. That does not hold while the index lags. relocate_client/relocate_server already avoid this by reading canonical_*_at from the host files.

Acceptance: a read-modify-write after an index-out-of-sync commit must not revert the committed fields. Possible directions: read the canonical metadata when the root is present (as relocate does), or re-sync the row from canonical metadata after an IndexOutOfSync warning. Add a regression test that makes the index write fail after a first update and verifies a second modify_client keeps the first change. Covers clients and servers.

Related: #485 (turns the client index failure into a commit warning; this is the follow-on staleness).

<!-- ephervex-followup:dd77c5bb-a698-49be-9d92-c9165fd8c745 -->
issues.title: Read-modify-write updates read the index row, which can lag canonical metadata and silently revert a committed change

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
Two production server mutations commit server metadata but discard its ServerCommitWarning (IndexOutOfSync / MetadataNotDurable) instead of reporting it.

1. App::synchronize_restored_host (crates/core/src/snapshot.rs, InstalledHost::Server branch) calls Registry::update_server, which calls update_server_committed and discards the warnings. A server snapshot restore never reports an out-of-sync index or an unsynced metadata directory, and `snapshot restore --json` always prints `warnings: []` for a server host.
2. App::promote_instance (crates/core/src/promotion.rs) matches `Ok(commit) => servers.push(commit.record)` on Registry::relocate_server, dropping commit.warnings for every linked server that moved. The CLI `instance promote` output and the GUI promotion toast only show servers that failed to move.

Other server mutations carry these warnings through ServerCommit<ServerRecord> to print_server_commit (stderr text plus index_out_of_sync / metadata_not_durable JSON entries), so these paths are inconsistent.

Acceptance: both operations return the server commit warnings to core callers (for restore, as a field on SnapshotRestore; for promotion, on PromotionOutcome), and the CLI (text and --json) and the GUI report them, localized.

Relation: the client-side equivalent is #486, which adds the Commit<T, W> / ClientCommit generalization, SnapshotRestore.warnings and PromotionOutcome.instance_warnings; build on that change once it is on local main (check main first and wait for it if not).

<!-- ephervex-followup:a430a255-9c62-4d47-ad55-b94838510eec -->
issues.title: Server snapshot restore and linked-server promotion drop ServerCommit warnings

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
Registry::delete_client (crates/storage/src/registry.rs, the loop over linked_server_ids) reads each linked server's canonical record with metadata::read_server_metadata(&indexed.root) and passes it straight to update_server_committed. Unlike canonical_server_at (storage) and App::canonical_server_for_mutation (core), it does not check that found.id equals the indexed server id and does not reset the record's root to the indexed root.

Reproduction: a linked server's root holds a server.json naming a different server id (for example a copied server directory, the case duplicate_server_roots exists to detect). Delete the client. delete_client rewrites the foreign server's record with linked_client_id = None, publishes it at the root stored in that foreign file (the other server's directory), and updates that foreign server's index row. The server actually linked to the client keeps its stale linked_client_id in its canonical metadata.

Expected: delete_client refuses (or skips with a reported condition) foreign or unreadable server metadata, using canonical_server_at plus the indexed root, so deleting a client can never rewrite another server's metadata.

Acceptance: regression test with a linked server root whose server.json names another id; deleting the client must not change the other server's metadata or index row.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
In crates/core/src/diagnosis.rs, App::apply_fix handles DiagnosticFix::UseAutomaticJava for InstalledHost::Server by calling set_server_runtime_settings(id, None, facts.jvm_override).map(drop). That call returns ServerCommit<ServerRecord>, and .map(drop) discards its ServerCommitWarning list (IndexOutOfSync / MetadataNotDurable). FixOutcome has no field for server commit warnings, so the GUI's apply-fix result reports a clean success even when the server's canonical metadata was published without a directory sync or its index row could not be updated.

Acceptance: the fix outcome carries the server commit warnings and the GUI reports them as localized toasts, the same way other user-requested server changes do (print_server_commit in the CLI). Add a regression test that provokes MetadataNotDurable on a server through apply_fix.

Relation: same family as #489 (server snapshot restore and linked-server promotion drop ServerCommit warnings) but a different entry point; the client-side equivalent is #486, which adds FixOutcome.client_warnings and GUI send_client_commit_warnings. Build on #486 once it is on local main (check main first and wait for it if not).
