issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
Registry::relocate_client (crates/storage/src/registry.rs, the record closure inside move_host) records the move with update_client. update_client_committed reports an index UPDATE failure after instance.json was published as a ClientCommitWarning::IndexOutOfSync warning, and update_client discards warnings, so the move is reported as successful while the SQLite row still names the old root and storage class. In the cross-filesystem copy path move_host then discards the source tree, so the index row points at a directory that no longer exists. For the rest of the session everything that reads the client through the index (App::client, launch planning, mod operations) sees a missing root. Registry::modify_client falls back to the index row for a missing root and updates the index only, so a later rename, setting or attention change is reported as successful but never reaches instance.json at the new root. Reconciliation follows the files automatically only for the temporary-to-persistent direction.

relocate_server already uses update_server_committed and returns the warnings.

Expected: relocate_client surfaces the IndexOutOfSync warning (for example by returning a commit with warnings) or repairs the row, so the session does not keep working against the vacated root.

Acceptance: regression test that fails the index write during a cross-root client move and checks the result reports it and the client stays addressable at its new root.

<!-- ephervex-followup:acb356f1-dadc-401f-9dac-6ffa568a90fd -->
issues.title: Client relocation reports success when the index write fails, leaving the index row on the vacated root

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
After an index write fails behind a committed client update (ClientCommitWarning::IndexOutOfSync, which update_client and modify_client only log), the SQLite row keeps the old fields until the next successful write or reconciliation. Read-only consumers still take their facts from that row. Launch planning (crates/core/src/launch.rs, self.client(instance)?) takes minecraft_version, loader and Java/JVM overrides from it: after a loader-build change commits to instance.json but the index UPDATE fails, the next launch in the same session plans the old loader build, a silent substitution of the user's exact selection. Registry::duplicate_client (crates/storage/src/registry.rs, self.client(source)) builds the copy's record (name, loader, overrides, flags) from the lagging row while copying the newer files and recipe, so the duplicate's record disagrees with its files. Registry::prepare_server reads a linked client's minecraft_version and loader from the row the same way.

Expected: consumers whose result depends on the client's current settings read canonical metadata when the root exists, as read-modify-write updates and server mutations do, or the lagging row is repaired inside the session.

Acceptance: regression tests that fail the index write after a loader or override change and then plan a launch, duplicate the client and prepare a linked server.

<!-- ephervex-followup:cad3f65d-73a5-4c6a-bebf-2613a3818a89 -->
issues.title: Launch planning and client duplication read the index row, which can lag committed client metadata

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
Registry::current_client (crates/storage/src/registry.rs, also used by modify_client) always prefers instance.json when the root is a directory. Reconciliation (crates/storage/src/reconcile.rs, the client branch around the index_is_newer check) instead adopts the index row when the record carries AttentionReason::MissingRoot and row.updated_at > canonical.updated_at, because update_client_committed updates only the index while a persistent root is missing. If a removable or remote root comes back during a session before reconciliation runs, modify_client starts from the older instance.json and writes it over the index-only edits (loader, overrides, name), and launch or Java planning plans from the older settings.

Expected: current_client uses the same precedence as reconciliation (index wins when MissingRoot is set and the row is newer), or the returning root is reconciled before canonical reads.

Acceptance: regression test that sets an override while the root is missing, restores the root, then calls modify_client or current_client and checks the override survives.

Found while reviewing #493 (Registry::current_client was introduced there; the worker must base on it).

<!-- ephervex-followup:0e9a1ed9-2104-42de-a6a7-95128e1c9baf -->

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
After an index write fails behind a committed client update (ClientCommitWarning::IndexOutOfSync, only logged by update_client and modify_client), several core readers still take a client's settings from the lagging SQLite row via App::client instead of the canonical metadata (Registry::current_client / App::current_client). Readers: App::plan_loader_version_change, change_loader_version and loader_versions_for_instance (crates/core/src/loader.rs, report and log the old build as current_version); mod compatibility and search targets (crates/core/src/mods.rs, declared_relations.rs); mutation contexts reading allow_pack_mod_version_changes (mutation.rs, linked_mods.rs); diagnosis host_facts (diagnosis.rs); snapshot capture (snapshot.rs); launch_and_connect_availability (connection.rs). Each can plan from a Minecraft version, loader, or flag the user already replaced until reconciliation or the next successful index write.

Expected: readers whose result depends on current settings use current_client when the root exists, so none substitutes a lagging row for the user's exact selection.

Acceptance: regression tests that fail the index write after a loader or override change and then exercise each reader. Readers that only need the root path may keep App::client; state which and why.

Found while reviewing #493, which covers launch and Java planning, duplicate_client, prepare_server and the linked-server recipe; base on the commit that adds Registry::current_client.

comments.author: MelanX
comments.bodyMarkdown: Two more readers found while reviewing #493: App::verify_shared_artifacts (crates/core/src/verify.rs, reads record.minecraft_version and record.loader.kind from self.client) checks the cached metadata of the old Minecraft version and reports loader coverage for the old loader kind when the index row lags. App::host_target for InstalledHost::Instance (declared_relations.rs) was already listed. issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
Every slider, dropdown and switch edit on the Minecraft defaults screen goes through `edit_minecraft_draft` (crates/gui/src/controller.rs), which ends in `render_minecraft`. That function replaces the whole `minecraft-preference-rows` model with a new `ModelRc` (`ui.set_minecraft_preference_rows(model(state.rows()))`), so the repeater tears down and rebuilds every `MinecraftPreferenceRowCard`, including the control that has keyboard focus.

Actual: after one arrow-key step on a slider, one arrow-key change on a dropdown, or one Space on a switch, the focused control is destroyed and focus is lost, so the user cannot keep adjusting by keyboard.

Evidence: the call sites of `edit_minecraft_draft` are in crates/gui/src/controller.rs (the number, boolean and enumeration handlers). The repo already has `edit_minecraft_row`, whose doc comment explains that rebuilding the list recreates the control the user is still in; it writes back only the edited row via `refresh_minecraft_row` and is used for the window size fields.

Expected: number, boolean and enumeration edits keep the edited row's control alive and focused, for example by updating only the edited row (as `edit_minecraft_row` does) or reusing the model.

Acceptance: a regression test that re-renders through the real controller path and asserts that a second keyboard step on the same slider (and a second change on the same dropdown or switch) is still delivered to the same control. Found by code reading during review; not verified against a live run.

<!-- ephervex-followup:50db8dff-83a0-4f81-8725-cae2cc380683 -->

comments.author: MelanX
comments.bodyMarkdown:
The same rebuild also hits the number and free-text fields on this screen, not only sliders, dropdowns and switches.

- `on_minecraft_commit_number` and `on_minecraft_commit_text` (crates/gui/src/controller.rs) commit through `edit_minecraft_draft` and so through `render_minecraft`. Pressing Tab out of a field commits on focus-lost, and the rebuild destroys the control that just received focus, so keyboard focus lands nowhere. Pressing Enter destroys the field itself.
- The Reset button (`on_minecraft_forget_preference`) rebuilds the list through the same path.

Care for the field case: a `TextField` whose `text` binding was broken by typing does not follow a row-only update, so the committed normalization (for example a trimmed or reformatted number) must still reach the field. Reset may need to keep rebuilding, because Toggle and Slider replace their own bindings after interaction.

Acceptance addition: a regression test through the real controller path showing that Tab-ing out of a committed field leaves the next control focusable. Found by code reading; not verified against a live run.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
canonical_server_at and canonical_client_at (crates/storage/src/registry.rs, near the end of the non-test code) and App::canonical_server_for_mutation (crates/core/src/server.rs, around lines 1047-1065) return RegistryError::ServerUnknown / InstanceUnknown when the server.json or instance.json at an indexed root names a different id. The message is "no server with id {id}" and registry_failing_path (crates/core/src/error.rs, around line 999) maps it to no path. A user who tries to delete, move or edit a server that is plainly listed, but whose directory holds a copied directory's metadata, is told the server does not exist, with no hint that the metadata at its root belongs to another server. There is no in-app recovery: deleting the server or its linked client refuses through the same check. Expected: a dedicated typed error such as "metadata at <root> belongs to another server" carrying the failing path, plus a recovery path such as forgetting the index row without reading metadata.

Acceptance: a listed server or client whose directory holds another record's metadata is refused with an error that says the metadata at that path belongs to another record and names the path, in the CLI and GUI; the user has a way to forget the index row without the metadata being read; delete, move and edit all report the same condition.

Found while reviewing the #490 change (Registry::delete_client now refuses foreign linked-server metadata via canonical_server_at).

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
Several tests in crates/cli/tests run the real `ephervex` binary with only HOME and the XDG variables pointed at a temporary directory (for example account_status_cli.rs and account_removal_cli.rs, whose headers say they need no keyring). The child keeps the session D-Bus address and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, so any code path that opens the credential store can connect to the developer's real Secret Service: KeyringStore::open and open_quietly (they call keyring::Entry::store_status() in crates/auth/src/store.rs) and the installation health report's credential backend probe (crates/core/src/health.rs). Running `cargo test --workspace` then raises the desktop keyring unlock prompt.

Only installation_health_cli.rs blocks the bus (DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS set to a dead socket, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR removed). The fix for in-process tests (#321, credential access behind the App's keyring) cannot cover a spawned binary, because that binary is not a test build.

Which CLI tests actually connect has not been established. It can be measured without touching a real keyring: point DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS at a Unix socket that a small listener logs connection attempts on, and run the workspace suite.

Acceptance: no test in the workspace connects to the session bus or the Secret Service. Every test that spawns the binary shares one helper that sets the dead bus address and removes XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, so a new test gets the isolation by default. A test (or the listener check above) fails if a spawned process connects to the bus.

Found while running the workspace tests for #490.

<!-- ephervex-followup:dca09a3f-e24a-49a3-91e2-9ce0f9c18802 -->

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
Nine unit tests in crates/gui/src/backend.rs (#[cfg(test)] mod tests, from about line 11788) open a real App on a temporary Paths root and then build a snapshot. refresh_snapshot / send_snapshot / snapshot() call app.account_status() (crates/core/src/account.rs, self.keyring()) and app.api_settings(), which call the real KeyringStore::open() (crates/auth/src/store.rs, keyring::Entry::store_status()). Core's TestKeyring guard is #[cfg(test)] only, so it is inactive when core is linked into the gui crate's test build, and the call reaches the developer's Secret Service. Running `cargo test --workspace` can raise the desktop keyring unlock prompt through these tests. Paths::rooted_at(tempdir) isolates files only, not the bus.

Affected tests: a_running_game_refreshes_the_rows_that_said_it_was_starting, a_snapshot_from_an_app_opened_earlier_shows_the_settings_saved_since, work_moved_off_the_command_loop_still_reports_its_result, a_server_start_is_cancelable_while_it_prepares_and_stops_offering_cancel_once_it_runs, linked_server_completion_targets_the_server_without_waiting_for_the_client, a_pair_start_server_row_is_cancelable_while_it_prepares_and_settles_when_the_server_exits, a_pair_start_server_row_records_a_crash_after_start_as_failed, a_pair_start_server_row_fails_when_supervision_ends_after_the_server_started, a_pair_start_server_row_settles_with_the_run_outcome_when_preparation_ends_the_start.

Acceptance: no gui test connects to the session bus or the Secret Service. Verify by pointing DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS at a Unix socket whose listener logs connections and running `cargo test -p ephervex-gui`; zero connections. Prefer an App-level way to supply a non-bus credential store to tests of other crates over redirecting the environment. Related: the spawned-binary equivalent is covered by the CLI test launcher.

The core account tests were fixed by #321 (closed); that fix keeps the test keyring inside core's own test build and does not cover tests in other crates that link core.

issues.bodyMarkdown:
App::cancel_isolation (crates/core/src/isolation.rs, around line 862) calls restore_isolation_snapshot and matches `Ok(_) => {}`, which throws away the returned SnapshotRestore. Its `warnings` (ClientCommitWarning) and `server_warnings` (ServerCommitWarning) are lost. When the host metadata written during the isolation-cancel restore is published but its directory sync fails (MetadataNotDurable), or the index UPDATE fails (IndexOutOfSync), the user is never told: the CLI and GUI isolation-cancel flows report plain success. cancel_isolation returns CoreResult<()>, so callers cannot see these warnings.

Acceptance: return the commit warnings from cancel_isolation and have the CLI (text and --json) and the GUI report them, localized, the same way snapshot restore and instance promotion do. Add a regression test that uses a SQLite trigger to make the clients/servers index UPDATE fail during cancel.

Dependency: SnapshotRestore.server_warnings is added by the change for #489 (server snapshot restore and promotion warnings), which may not be on local main yet; the client warnings field (#486) is already on main. Check main first and wait for it if absent.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
After Registry::relocate_client publishes instance.json at the persistent root but the SQLite UPDATE fails (ClientCommitWarning::IndexOutOfSync), the instances row keeps naming the vacated temporary root until the next reconciliation or modify_client (modify_client follows the moved files since #492). Everything that reads the client through Registry::client / App::client still gets the vacated root during that session: launch (claim_host + HeldLaunch::take on record.root), duplicate_client (RootMissing), mod/verify operations, snapshot operations.

Worst case: Registry::delete_client(id, FileDisposition::Remove) calls remove_tree on the vacated temporary root (a no-op), deletes the row and reports success. The real tree at <data>/instances/<id> stays on disk and startup reconciliation re-indexes it as an orphaned client root, so the instance the user deleted, with its files, comes back.

The IndexOutOfSync message ('lists may show the old value until the next reconciliation') also understates the effect: the instance cannot be launched or duplicated in that session.

Expected: a client whose row still names a vanished temporary root, while a finished root with the same id stands at the persistent path, is addressed at the persistent root by readers and by delete (for example by applying the same check Registry::following_moved_files uses in Registry::client or in the App-level read), or delete_client(Remove) also removes that persistent tree. relocate_client's own retry path must keep repairing the row (it short-circuits when record.storage == storage). The warning text should say the instance is unavailable until the next start if it is not repaired in-session.

Acceptance: regression tests that fail the index write during a promotion and then (a) delete the client with files and check no tree remains and the instance does not return after reconcile, (b) plan a launch / duplicate and check they address the persistent root.

Distinct from #493 (readers use canonical metadata only when the indexed root exists) and #492 (modify_client follows moved files).

<!-- ephervex-followup:b4f4ff01-19b3-42aa-8591-cb8ecc4cb939 -->
issues.title: In-session reads after a client promotion whose index write failed still use the vacated temporary root, and deleting the client with its files leaves the persistent tree behind

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
`Registry::update_client_committed` (crates/storage/src/registry.rs) writes only the index row when `record.root` is not a directory, but does not add `AttentionReason::MissingRoot`. Only reconciliation adds that flag (app or GUI startup, or an explicit reconcile).

If a persistent client's root disappears during a session (for example a removable or network drive unmounts) and the user then changes the loader, Java or JVM override, or name through `modify_client`, the newer settings exist only in the index row, without `MissingRoot`. When the root returns, `Registry::current_client` and `reconcile_present_client` (crates/storage/src/reconcile.rs) both rely on `client_index_is_newer`, which requires `MissingRoot`, so the older `instance.json` wins:

- launches plan from the old settings;
- the next `modify_client` writes the old metadata over the index edits;
- reconciliation replaces the index row with the canonical file (`index_repaired`), losing the edits for good.

The server side has the same gap: `update_server_committed` also writes only the row when the root is missing, and reconciliation's server branch only treats a newer row as current when it carries `MissingRoot`.

Reproduce:
1. Create a persistent client.
2. Remove its root.
3. `modify_client` setting a Java override (no reconcile in between, so no `MissingRoot`).
4. Restore the root with the previous `instance.json`.
5. `current_client` or reconcile returns the old record without the override.

Expected: an update that can only reach the index because the root is missing flags the row `MissingRoot`, so the existing newer-row rule applies on read and in reconciliation.

Acceptance: regression tests for a client and a server that edit while the root is missing without prior reconciliation, restore the root, then check that `current_client` and reconciliation keep the edit.

Related: #494.
issues.title: Client and server edits saved while a root is missing are lost when the root returns, unless reconciliation flagged it missing first

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
After an index write fails behind a committed client update (`ClientCommitWarning::IndexOutOfSync`), the CLI and GUI still read a client's settings from the lagging SQLite row through `App::client` instead of the canonical metadata. The canonical reader (`Registry::current_client`) is exposed only as `pub(crate) App::current_client`, so frontends cannot reach it.

1. CLI runtime edit (`apply_instance_runtime` in crates/cli/src/main.rs): `let record = app.client(id)?;` then `args.java.map(JavaOverride::new).or(record.java_override)` and `record.jvm_override.unwrap_or_default()` with only the flagged JVM fields replaced. The result is written with `set_client_runtime_settings`, so committed Java or JVM override fields the flags did not touch are written back to their stale values.
2. GUI runtime panel (`instance_runtime_data` in crates/gui/src/backend.rs): `app.client(instance)?` then displays `java_override` / `jvm_override`, so it shows overrides the user already replaced.
3. CLI `instance show` (`InstanceCommand::Show` in crates/cli/src/main.rs): `app.client(*id)?` then `print_instance` prints the lagging record, including Minecraft version, loader and overrides.

Expected: ephervex-core exposes a public canonical client reader (`App::current_client` made public, or an equivalent), and these frontends use it for settings they display or derive new values from. Readers that need only the name or root (for example the GUI entity-name lookups and the CLI delete confirmation) may keep `App::client`.

Acceptance: regression tests that fail the index write (or write canonical metadata only) after an override or loader change, then exercise each frontend path.

Related: #495, which moved the remaining ephervex-core readers to the canonical metadata.
issues.title: CLI and GUI show and derive client settings from an index row that can lag committed client metadata

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
`Registry::delete_client` rewrites each linked server's `server.json` and index row through `update_server_committed`. `App::delete_client` takes a host claim on every linked server first, but reconciliation (`forget_stale_client` in crates/storage/src/reconcile.rs, reached at startup for a stale temporary client) calls `Registry::delete_client` directly and holds no claim on those servers.

Another Ephervex process that is editing, moving or starting one of those servers at that moment can have its metadata overwritten by the stale read-modify-write. Found by reading the code; the window has not been reproduced.

Expected: reconciliation claims each linked server before unlinking it, or skips a server whose claim is held and reports it, as other reconciliation steps already do for a host whose claim is not free.
issues.title: Reconciliation unlinks a stale temporary client's servers without holding their host claims

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
`forget_stale_client` in crates/storage/src/reconcile.rs catches `ServerUnknown`, `ServerMetadataForeign` and `Metadata` errors from `Registry::delete_client`, keeps the client, and logs a warning that carries only the instance id. The error is dropped, so the log never says which linked server failed, whether its metadata was foreign or unreadable, or whether the failure came from reading the metadata or from publishing the unlinked record.

The doc comment says the helper handles metadata that is "unreadable or names another server", but `Metadata` errors from `publish_server_metadata` in the write phase are caught as well, so the comment and the message are narrower than the behavior.

Expected: the warning includes the error text and the linked server, and the doc comment describes everything the helper catches.
issues.title: The warning for a stale temporary client kept by reconciliation does not name the linked server or the error

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
In crates/storage/src/registry.rs, `move_host` for a copy (cross-filesystem) promotion publishes `instance.json` at the persistent root with `storage = Persistent`, then updates the index row, and only afterwards discards the source with `relocate::discard_tree(source)`, whose failure is only logged.

If the index UPDATE fails (`ClientCommitWarning::IndexOutOfSync`, a committed move) and `discard_tree(source)` also fails, the row still names the temporary root, and that root still exists with the pre-move metadata (`storage = Temporary`). `Registry::following_moved_files` only redirects when the indexed root is not a directory, so `Registry::client` / `App::client` keep returning the stale temporary copy.

In-session changes (`modify_client`), launches, mod operations and `delete_client(Remove)` then act on the stale copy, while the committed persistent copy at `<data>/instances/<id>` is never touched. Deleting leaves the persistent tree behind, which the next reconciliation re-indexes, and edits diverge between the two copies.

Expected: after a committed copy-mode move, the session addresses the committed persistent copy even if the stale source could not be removed. For example, the redirect could prefer a finished persistent root whose metadata says `Persistent` over a temporary root whose metadata still says `Temporary`, or the stale source could be retried or marked.

Acceptance: a regression test that makes both the instances UPDATE and the source discard fail, then checks that reads, edits and deletion address the persistent copy.

Related: #492 (modify_client follows moved files) and #502 (readers and deletion follow moved files when the temporary root is gone). This is the case where the temporary root still exists.
issues.title: A copy-mode promotion whose index write and source removal both fail leaves the session addressing the stale temporary copy

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
ADR 0002 says an index row flagged `MissingRoot` that is newer than the canonical metadata outranks it once the root returns. `Registry::current_client` and reconciliation follow that rule, but several paths in `crates/storage/src/registry.rs` read `instance.json` / `server.json` directly and ignore it:

- `relocate_client`: both the move's `record` closure (`canonical_client_at(host_files_root(..))`) and the repair-only branch (`canonical_client_at(&record.root, id)`);
- `relocate_server`: the `record` closure (`canonical_server_at(host_files_root(..))`);
- `delete_client`: each linked server is read with `canonical_server_at(&indexed.root, ..)` before it is unlinked.

On the core side, `App::canonical_server_for_mutation` (`crates/core/src/server.rs`) also reads `server.json` directly whenever the root exists, so server edits made after the root returns start from the older file as well. There is no server equivalent of `current_client`.

Scenario: a persistent client or server root disappears, the user edits it (the row is flagged `MissingRoot` and is newer, since #503), the root returns, and before reconciliation runs the user moves the host to the other storage root, edits the server, or deletes a client the server is linked to. The older metadata is published and mirrored into the index, so the edits are lost permanently.

Expected: these paths apply the same newer-row rule as `current_client` (a shared server equivalent is likely needed) and strip `MissingRoot` before publishing.

Acceptance: regression tests that edit while the root is missing, restore the root, then move, edit, or unlink, and check the edit survives.

Related: #494 (client reads), #503 (write side flags the row).

<!-- ephervex-followup:b3723a50-1dc7-408c-8fe1-9ca038c25108 -->
issues.title: Moving a host or unlinking a deleted client's servers drops edits a newer MissingRoot row holds

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
`Registry::delete_client` (`crates/storage/src/registry.rs`) lists the client's linked servers again after its callers have already claimed the servers they listed, so a server linked in between is rewritten without a host claim.

`App::delete_claimed_client` (`crates/core/src/app.rs`) and `forget_stale_client` (`crates/storage/src/reconcile.rs`) each list `Registry::linked_server_ids`, claim every listed server, then call `Registry::delete_client`. `delete_client` calls `linked_server_ids` a second time and rewrites each server through `update_server_committed`. Creating a linked server (`App::create_server` in `crates/core/src/server.rs`: `prepare_server`, then `publish_staged_server`) does not take the client's host claim, so another process can publish a linked server between the caller's listing and `delete_client`'s.

That server is then unlinked without the caller holding its claim. If the other process already claimed the new server and is editing it, the stale read-modify-write can overwrite its edit. With `FileDisposition::Remove` the new server is also left behind unlinked instead of being deleted with the client.

The window is narrow; found by reading the code, not reproduced.

Expected: unlinking only rewrites servers the caller has claimed. For example, `delete_client` takes the set of server ids the caller claimed and refuses when its own listing differs, so every rewritten linked server is claimed by construction.

Acceptance: a test links a server after the caller's listing and before `delete_client`'s listing (or exercises the new check directly) and shows the unclaimed server is neither unlinked nor rewritten.

Related: #505 (reconciliation claims linked servers).

<!-- ephervex-followup:cc0ef16c-e261-41ec-9ab9-b0abd15d6736 -->
issues.title: Deleting a client can unlink a server linked after the caller claimed the client's servers

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
Take a copy-mode promotion whose instances UPDATE and source discard both failed: the row names the still-present temporary root, and the committed copy at the persistent root has newer metadata with `storage = Persistent`. `Registry::client` follows the persistent copy only while its `updated_at` is newer than the temporary copy's (`is_committed_copy_of` in `crates/storage/src/registry.rs`).

Reconciliation (`crates/storage/src/reconcile.rs`) has no equivalent check:

- `reconcile_client` reads the row as indexed and runs `reconcile_present_client` on the stale temporary root. When `report_interrupted_state` flags something there, it calls `registry.update_client` on the temporary record, which stamps `updated_at = now` and republishes `instance.json` in the stale tree. That copy is now newer than the committed persistent copy, so every later read addresses it again, and edits made on the persistent copy since the move become invisible.
- `reindex_orphaned_clients` sees the committed persistent copy, finds `entry.root != directory && entry.root.is_dir()`, and reports a `ClientRootConflict` instead of recognizing the committed move and repairing the row.

Expected: when a committed persistent copy supersedes a still-present temporary root, reconciliation repairs the row to the persistent root, as it already does when the temporary root is gone, and never stamps or adopts the stale temporary copy.

Acceptance: a regression test in which the index write and the source discard both fail, reconciliation runs, and reads and edits still address the persistent copy with the row naming it.

Related: #507 (in-session addressing of the same state).

<!-- ephervex-followup:da32e784-df96-412e-b4a8-b463a5c1e454 -->
issues.title: Reconciliation can flip a client back to a stale temporary copy left by a committed copy-mode promotion

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
When `move_host` (`crates/storage/src/registry.rs`) copies a client to the persistent root and records the move, a failure of `relocate::discard_tree(source)` is only logged, so the old tree stays under the temporary instances root. If the index UPDATE also failed, the row still names the temporary root: `Registry::following_moved_files` addresses the persistent copy (#507), and `delete_client(Remove)` removes both trees.

Once any write repairs the row, nothing names the temporary tree any more:

- `Registry::modify_client` -> `update_client_committed` with the redirected root;
- the repair-only branch of `Registry::relocate_client` (`record.storage == storage` but `record.root != indexed.root`).

Neither discards the stale source. Reconciliation scans only the persistent instances directory for orphans (`reindex_orphaned_clients`), nothing sweeps unindexed temporary roots, and a later `delete_client(Remove)` removes only the persistent root. The full instance tree, possibly gigabytes for a modded instance, stays on the tmpfs-backed temporary root and uses RAM until reboot.

Expected: the row repair retries discarding the superseded temporary tree the way `move_host` does after a successful record, logging on failure, or another owner removes a temporary tree superseded by a committed persistent copy.

Acceptance: a regression test in which the index write and the source discard fail once, the row is then repaired, and the stale temporary tree is gone.

Related: #507 (in-session addressing of the same state), #510 (reconciliation of the same state).

<!-- ephervex-followup:4a6a5f9e-8d4d-4a5f-aa7f-67af3611a5dc -->
issues.title: A stale temporary client copy left by a committed copy-mode promotion is orphaned once the index row is repaired

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
`Registry::relocate_server` shares `move_host` with clients, but `Registry::server(id)` (`crates/storage/src/registry.rs`) returns the row exactly as indexed. There is no server counterpart of the client-side `following_moved_files` (#502, #507), and `App::canonical_server_for_mutation` (`crates/core/src/server.rs`) reads only the indexed root.

If a linked server's promotion publishes `server.json` at the persistent root but the servers UPDATE fails (`ServerCommitWarning::IndexOutOfSync`, a committed move), the row keeps naming the temporary root:

- After a rename move that root is gone. Until reconciliation runs, server reads, starts and edits address a missing root (`canonical_server_for_mutation` returns `RootMissing`). Edits recorded through `update_server_committed` meanwhile reach only the index row, and `reconcile_servers`' moved-files branch then adopts the persistent canonical metadata, discarding them.
- After a copy move whose source discard also failed, the session keeps using the stale temporary server. Retrying `relocate_server` then removes the committed persistent copy (`move_host`: `names_this_host(destination)` -> `remove_tree`) and copies the stale tree over it.

Expected: as for clients (ADR 0025), a server whose promotion committed is addressed at its persistent root by reads and edits, and a retry repairs the row instead of recopying.

Acceptance: regression tests for a rename move and a copy move whose servers UPDATE fails, checking reads, edits, deletion and a retry.

<!-- ephervex-followup:5c2bcc36-9ad7-42e9-ba3e-4678fa445d70 -->
issues.title: Server reads do not follow a committed promotion whose index write failed

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
On the Minecraft defaults screen a pointer press or drag on a slider sets a continuous, unsnapped value in the std Slider (slider-base.slint `set-value` does not snap pointer input to `step`), and `released(value)` sends it to `on_minecraft_set_number`. `MinecraftDefaultsModel::set_number` (crates/gui/src/minecraft_defaults.rs) then rounds it: `number.round()` for percent, decimal and degrees scales, `whole_from_control` for whole numbers. The draft and the readout therefore hold the rounded value while the slider handle stays at the unrounded position, up to half a step away.

Before row-only edits, the full row rebuild after each edit reset the handle to the rounded value. Now the edited row is updated in place (crates/gui/src/controller.rs `edit_minecraft_row` / `refresh_minecraft_row`), and the Slider has replaced its own `value` binding during interaction, so the handle keeps its own unrounded position.

Expected: after a pointer release the handle shows the value the draft holds.

Acceptance: a regression test through the real controller path (the `MinecraftScreen` harness in controller.rs tests) showing the slider value equals the rounded draft after a pointer click at a position that does not land on a step, without recreating the slider element, so keyboard focus is kept (see #496).

Found while fixing #496 (1e3c1b2).

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
Take a copy-mode promotion whose instances UPDATE and source discard both failed: the row still names the temporary root, the stale temporary tree stands, and the committed copy at the persistent root has newer metadata with `storage = Persistent`. `Registry::client` follows the persistent copy (#507), so `restore_snapshot_for` (`crates/core/src/snapshot.rs`) restores files into the persistent root.

`RestoreTransaction::publish` (`crates/storage/src/restore.rs`) marks that root incomplete before `synchronize_restored_host` calls `self.client(id)`. `Registry::following_moved_files` requires `is_finished_client_root(persistent)`, which is false while the incomplete marker exists, so `client()` returns the indexed temporary record. `synchronize_restored_host` then copies `current.root` / `current.storage` (temporary) into the restored record, and `update_client_committed` publishes the restored `instance.json` into the stale temporary tree with `updated_at = now`.

After `finish()` clears the marker, the persistent root holds the snapshot's older metadata while the stale tree holds the newest, so `is_committed_copy_of` no longer holds. Every later read, edit and launch addresses the stale tree, the restored files are no longer visible, and reconciliation reports a `ClientRootConflict`.

Expected: `synchronize_restored_host` records the restored metadata at the root the restore actually wrote to (the layout root it was given), repairs the row to that root, and never writes to the superseded temporary tree.

Acceptance: a regression test with a copy-mode promotion whose index write and source discard fail, followed by a snapshot restore. Afterwards the row and `Registry::client` name the persistent root, the stale temporary tree's metadata is unchanged, and reads return the restored content.

Related: #507 (in-session addressing of the same state), #510 (reconciliation of the same state).
issues.title: Restoring a snapshot of a client whose row names a superseded temporary copy records the restored metadata in the stale temporary tree

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
Take a copy-mode server move (temporary to persistent) that publishes `server.json` at the persistent root, but whose servers UPDATE fails (`ServerCommitWarning::IndexOutOfSync`) and whose temporary source cannot be discarded. With #512, `Registry::server` follows the persistent tree only while `is_committed_server_copy_of` holds, meaning the persistent metadata says `Persistent` and has a later `updated_at` than the stale temporary metadata.

Reconciliation reads the raw row (`crates/storage/src/reconcile.rs`: `reconcile_server` -> `reconcile_present_server` -> `reconcile_server_against_metadata`), which still names the stale temporary root. If that tree carries interrupted state (`has_interrupted_state`, for example a non-empty `.launcher` retired or staging directory carried over by the copy), `report_interrupted_state` adds `InterruptedMutation`. Because `adopted` is true, `registry.update_server` republishes the stale temporary `server.json` with a fresh `updated_at`.

From then on `is_committed_server_copy_of` is false, so `Registry::server` returns the stale temporary record, and reads, starts and edits act on the stale tree. A retried `relocate_server` to persistent then takes the `move_host` branch for replacing a finished copy that an earlier move could not record: it removes the committed persistent tree, which holds later edits, and copies the stale tree over it.

Expected: reconciliation never rewrites the canonical metadata of a temporary server tree that a committed persistent copy supersedes. This is the server equivalent of #510.

Code: `crates/storage/src/registry.rs` (`following_moved_server`, `is_committed_server_copy_of`, `move_host`), `crates/storage/src/reconcile.rs` (`reconcile_server_against_metadata`).

Acceptance: a regression test with a copy-mode server move whose servers UPDATE and source discard fail and whose stale tree carries interrupted state. After reconciliation, reads still follow the persistent copy and a retried move keeps the committed copy.

Related: #512 (server reads follow a committed move), #510 (client equivalent).

comments.author: MelanX
comments.bodyMarkdown:
Another symptom of the same state: while both trees stand, `reindex_orphaned_servers` (`crates/storage/src/reconcile.rs`, the `indexed.root != directory && indexed.root.is_dir()` branch) reports the committed persistent copy as a `ServerRootConflict` on every pass, even though reads, starts, changes and deletion already follow it.

The fix should give server reconciliation the client rules from #510: follow the newer persistent copy and repair the row, never stamp the stale temporary tree, and still report a persistent tree that is not the newer copy as a conflict. ADR 0025 currently documents the conflict report as the server behavior and needs the same update. Removing the superseded temporary tree after the repair is tracked in #516.

issues.title: Reconciliation can restamp a stale temporary server tree that a committed persistent copy supersedes

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
Take a copy-mode server promotion that publishes `server.json` at the persistent root, but whose servers UPDATE fails (`ServerCommitWarning::IndexOutOfSync`) and whose temporary source cannot be discarded. `Registry::server` follows the committed persistent copy (`following_moved_server` / `is_committed_server_copy_of` in `crates/storage/src/registry.rs`), and `delete_server(Remove)` removes both trees while the row still names the temporary root.

Once any write repairs the row to the persistent root, nothing names the temporary tree any more:

- `Registry::relocate_server`'s repair-only branch (`record.storage == storage && record.root != indexed.root`);
- every server change that writes back the followed record through `update_server_committed`, for example `add_server_attention` and the other callers in `crates/core/src/server.rs`, and a snapshot restore.

None of them discards the superseded temporary tree. `delete_server` then sees `indexed.root == record.root` and removes only the persistent tree, and reconciliation's orphan scan only covers the persistent servers directory. The stale tree under `<temp>/ephervex-<uid>/servers/<id>` stays until the OS clears the temporary directory, which may be tmpfs and so uses memory.

ADR 0025 says that tree is removed when the server is deleted with its files, which no longer holds after a repair.

Expected: as for clients (#511, `discard_superseded_client_root`), every repair of such a server row, whether by a change, a repeated promotion, or reconciliation (#515), removes the superseded temporary tree and logs a failure to remove it. Update ADR 0025, which currently describes this lifecycle only for clients.

Acceptance: regression tests with a server whose promotion left its row and temporary tree behind, followed by (a) a server change and (b) a repeated promotion. Afterwards the row names the persistent root and the superseded temporary tree is gone.

Found by reading code at local main 65ce0fa; not reproduced.

Related: #511 (client equivalent), #512, #515.
issues.title: A stale temporary server copy left by a committed copy-mode promotion is orphaned once the server row is repaired

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
When a copy- or rename-mode promotion's index write failed, `Registry::client` (and `Registry::server`) follow the committed copy at the persistent root. `restore_snapshot_for` (`crates/core/src/snapshot.rs`) then publishes the restore there and sets the incomplete marker. If the process dies between `RestoreTransaction::publish` and `finish`, reconciliation does not recover that restore: `reconcile_client` (`crates/storage/src/reconcile.rs`) consults `committed_copy_superseding` / `is_finished_client_root`, which are false while the marker exists.

- **Superseded** (the temporary tree still stands): the row is reconciled as the stale temporary tree. `reindex_orphaned_clients` then reaches `settle_unfinished_client_root` with an indexed entry whose root differs from the persistent directory, reports it as an unfinished instance and leaves it alone. `recover_restore_state` never runs, the half-restored persistent tree keeps its marker, and the client resolves to the stale temporary tree.
- **Vacated** (the temporary root is gone): `is_finished_client_root(persistent)` is false, so `reconcile_client` calls `forget_stale_client`. The record is dropped and its linked servers are unlinked before the orphan scan re-indexes and recovers the persistent tree.

The server arm has the same problem (`following_moved_server` / `is_finished_server_root`).

Expected: reconciliation treats a marked persistent root of an indexed temporary row as that host's interrupted restore, recovers it at that root, then follows and repairs the row, without forgetting the record or unlinking servers.

Acceptance: regression tests for the superseded and vacated variants, for a client and a server, that interrupt a restore after publish and then reconcile. The record and its linked servers survive and the restore is recovered at the persistent root.

Found by reading code at local main 65ce0fa; not reproduced.

Related: #507, #510, #512, #514.
issues.title: An interrupted snapshot restore at a followed persistent root is never recovered while the row names the temporary root

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
Importing a published Modrinth pack fails as a whole with "The pack's description file could not be understood" because a file's `env` value is `unknown` (`unknown variant 'unknown', expected one of 'required', 'optional', 'unsupported'` at line 1973 column 35 of `modrinth.index.json`).

The .mrpack format says a file's `env` uses the Modrinth client/server side types (https://support.modrinth.com/en/articles/8802351-modrinth-modpack-format-mrpack), and the Modrinth API reference allows `required`, `optional`, `unsupported` and `unknown` for those types (https://docs.modrinth.com/api/operations/getproject/). So `unknown` is a value Modrinth itself publishes, and the pack is valid.

`RawRequirement` in `crates/pack/src/modrinth.rs` deliberately accepts only the first three. The normalized `SideRequirement` (`crates/pack/src/recipe.rs`) already has an `Unknown` variant, which is never installed automatically and stays distinct from `Optional`, but the .mrpack parser cannot produce it. The doc comments on both types state that .mrpack has only three environment values, which is no longer accurate.

Reproduce: `ephervex import --inspect --trust once 'https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/t1tOiUHZ/versions/BSg2ZS8u/Create%2B%206.0.0%20Alpha%20f.mrpack'` (Create+ 6.0.0 Alpha f, NeoForge 1.21.1).

Expected: the manifest parses, and a file whose side is `unknown` maps to `SideRequirement::Unknown` and follows that variant's explicit rule instead of the whole import being refused. Keep `unknown` distinct from `unsupported`, check that server reconstruction handles per-side `Unknown` from a pack file, and correct the doc comments.

Acceptance: a regression test that imports an .mrpack fixture with `env` values of `unknown` on each side and checks the resulting side requirements and the client and server install plans.
issues.title: Modrinth pack import refuses a pack whose file env uses "unknown"

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
A NeoForge 1.21.1 server whose mods/ folder holds JustEnoughAdvancements-21.1.1.jar crashes at mod loading ("Mod jea requires jei 19.25.0.322 or above"). The report has no Mod List table but states the culprit jar directly: "-- Mod loading issue for: jea --" followed by "Mod file: <server>/mods/JustEnoughAdvancements-21.1.1.jar".

`ephervex server crash <id>` prints "high  jea  named as the mod that failed" followed by "Not in this server's mods list, so it cannot be switched off here." (crash-not-in-mod-list, crates/cli/src/main.rs near line 5694). The suspect is not actionable, although `ephervex server mods` lists the jar.

Cause: crates/core/src/crash_analysis.rs (review building near lines 670-695) maps a suspect to a file only through suspect.jar, which comes from the Mod List table. Early FML/NeoForge loading failures have no such table, so logical_path stays None.

Expected: use the report's own "Mod file:" line (resolved against the host's mods folder, never trusting a path outside it) so the suspect maps to the installed row and can be disabled. The "not in the mods list" text should only appear when the mod is really absent. Also check the Forge 1.20.1 form ("Mod File:" and "Failure message:" lines, for example a client-side shader mod failing to load on a Forge server).

Acceptance: a regression test with a loading-failure report that has no Mod List table maps the named mod to its installed jar, for both the NeoForge and the Forge report formats.

Reproduction: create a NeoForge 1.21.1 client with JustEnoughAdvancements (which requires JEI) plus a few other mods, build a linked server from it (JEI is client-only, so the server leaves it out), accept the EULA and start the server. It stops during mod loading and writes a crash report. Then run `ephervex server crash <server-id>` and compare with `ephervex server mods <server-id>`.

Verified against the code at the current main: the mapping to a file happens only in the crash review builder in crates/core/src/crash_analysis.rs, so the GUI crash view shares the behavior.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
Evidence (read at local main 41b69a6 plus the in-progress server supersession change): several host writers commit metadata without holding the host claim: App::rename_server (crates/core/src/instance.rs, via canonical_server_for_mutation + Registry::update_server_committed), add_server_attention (crates/core/src/server.rs), and Registry::modify_client_committed for clients. Moves (relocate_server/relocate_client) hold the claim.

For a host whose row names its temporary root while a committed persistent copy supersedes it, the writer decides before publishing that the temporary tree is superseded, publishes, writes the row, then calls discard_superseded_*_root. That function only re-checks that the path is the launcher's temporary root and that the persistent root is finished. Interleaving: (1) writer A decides the temporary tree is superseded; (2) process B, holding the claim, demotes the host: move_host removes the stale temporary tree, copies persistent to temporary and records the row at the temporary root; (3) A publishes at the persistent root, overwrites B's row back to persistent and discards the temporary root, which is now B's freshly demoted host; (4) B discards its source, the persistent tree. Both trees are gone and the row names a missing root. The window is narrow, but the result is unrecoverable data loss.

Separately, is_committed_copy_of / is_committed_server_copy_of compare wall-clock updated_at, so a backwards clock jump between a promotion and a later demotion makes a stale persistent leftover look newer; reads follow it and every write discards the live temporary host.

Expected: a superseded-tree discard must not be able to remove a tree a concurrent claimed move just produced. Possible fixes: make metadata writers take the host claim, or re-verify under the claim at discard time that the stale tree is still older than the persistent copy; consider a monotonic generation instead of wall-clock updated_at for the committed-copy decision.

Acceptance: a regression test that interleaves a claimed demotion between a writer's supersession decision and its discard and shows neither tree is lost.

<!-- ephervex-followup:b13bbfb5-3226-4254-bc8c-52c7cb3e3c01 -->
issues.title: A superseded-tree discard can remove the tree a concurrent claimed move just produced

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
Writers that commit host metadata without holding the host claim (App::rename_server via Registry::update_server_committed, App::add_server_attention, Registry::modify_client_committed when the claim is busy, set_allow_pack_mod_version_changes, and similar) read the current record, then publish metadata and the index row at that record's root. A relocate_client/relocate_server holding the claim can commit in between: move_host copies or renames source S to destination D, the commit closure writes D's metadata and the row at D, then the source is removed. If the writer's update_*_committed runs after the move's commit, it writes the row back to S (publishing metadata into S if it still exists, which the move then deletes). Final state: a row naming a missing root S while the host's files are at D. For a persistent S the row gets MissingRoot attention and nothing follows it to D (client()/server() follow moved files only for rows with vanishing storage; the reconciliation orphan scan covers only persistent directories), so a host demoted to the temporary root becomes unreachable and its files vanish when the temporary root is cleared. The writer's own edit is also lost. Applies to any host, not only one with a superseded temporary tree.
Expected: a claim-less writer cannot publish a row or metadata at a root a claimed move has moved the host away from. Fix direction: claim-less writers take the host claim (bounded wait) or verify under it that the row still names the root they read before writing; callers that already hold the claim must not self-deadlock (the claim is not reentrant).
Acceptance: a regression test that interleaves a claimed move between a writer's read of the record and its write, and shows the row still names the host's files and the host stays reachable. Found while reviewing the superseded-tree discard fix (#520) in crates/storage/src/registry.rs and reconcile.rs.

Related: #520 (superseded-tree discard under the claim) does not cover this; the discard guard there never lets a tree be removed, but a claim-less row write can still name a root a claimed move has vacated.

<!-- ephervex-followup:c8a58ca8-1a31-40ed-927d-7a84edea1df1 -->
issues.title: A host write without the claim can overwrite a concurrent move's row with the source root the move then removes

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
docs/adr/0025-storage-class-is-promoted-in-place.md, around lines 107-109, reads: "For a server that holds for every write of its record, because each goes through the one that commits it." The sentence has no subject or predicate and does not say what holds for a server (presumably that every server write repairs a row left at a superseded temporary root and removes that tree). It predates the claim-guarded removal paragraph added beside it. Expected: rewrite it so the ADR states the server rule explicitly and consistently with the client rule beside it. Acceptance: the paragraph reads as a complete statement of the server rule. Documentation only, no code change.

## Behavior

`process::tests::a_supervisor_that_died_while_starting_is_resolved_through_the_child_it_tagged` failed once in a full `cargo test --workspace` run at a load average of about 26. Right after `spawn_child` returned, `classify_runtime` reported `UnknownRunning { child: None }` instead of `Orphaned { child }`, so the tagged child was not yet observable. The test passed five times in a row when run alone.

The test classifies immediately after spawning `/bin/sh -c "exec sleep 30"`, with no wait for the child to become observable as tagged.

## Expected behavior

The test waits, with a bounded deadline, until the child is observable as tagged before classifying (or the classification tolerates a child that has not finished exec), so the suite does not fail under load.

The same pattern was fixed for a different test in #444.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-core`

## Behavior

`App::plan_for_host` builds a server's installed set with `installed_projects_of`, which reads `PackRecipe::managed_mods` and ignores sides. A reconstructed linked server's recipe copies the client's desired state, so a client-only file can have an entry with no jar on the server. The resolver counts that project as `already_installed` and leaves it out of the install.

Installing a server mod (or changing a server mod's version) that needs such a dependency therefore does not put the dependency on the server, and the server fails to start with a missing dependency.

## Expected behavior

A server host's installed set is built from entries installed on `PackSide::Server` (`recorded_mods_for(PackSide::Server)` or `is_installed_on` already exist). Any side-agnostic installed check on the server install path gets the same treatment.

Regression test: a reconstructed linked-server recipe holding a client-only dependency, then a server install of a mod that requires it.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/mods.rs` `plan_for_host` (2122), `installed_projects_of` (2284-2302), server install/plan paths (1329, 1372)
- `crates/pack/src/recipe.rs` `managed_mods` (1246), `recorded_mods_for` (1235), `is_installed_on` (683)
issues.title: Server catalog installs treat a client-only recipe entry as already installed on the server

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-server`

## Behavior

`runtime::tests::a_live_orphan_whose_executable_was_replaced_is_not_proven_dead` copies `/bin/sleep` into a temp dir and spawns the copy at once. When another test thread forks at the same moment, its child can inherit the still-open write descriptor of the copy, and `execve` fails with ETXTBSY:

```
spawn: Os { code: 26, kind: ExecutableFileBusy, message: "Text file busy" }
```

Seen once in a full `cargo test --workspace` run while six workspace test runs ran in parallel on the machine; it passes on rerun.

Other tests use the same copy-then-spawn pattern and are exposed the same way: `crates/server/src/runtime.rs` around 1643 and 1862-1866, and `crates/server/src/process.rs` around 1791.

## Expected behavior

These tests do not fail on ETXTBSY. Options: retry the spawn on `ExecutableFileBusy` for a bounded time, or produce the executable through a path that is fully closed before any fork (write it in a helper process, or hard-link instead of copy where possible). The replaced-executable invariant the test checks stays intact.

## Locations

- `crates/server/src/runtime.rs` 1825-1835 (the failing test), 1643, 1862-1866
- `crates/server/src/process.rs` 1791
issues.title: Server tests that run a copied executable fail with "Text file busy" under parallel tests

**Crate:** `ephervex-gui`

## Behavior

Several handlers inside a workspace pane run `root.close-workspace(); root.page = 4; root.settings-tab = ...;` in that order. ## Behavior

The Instances page has three body branches (loading spinner, empty state, instance list), with its header and filter bar in the same `VerticalLayout`.

1. **Background service not running:** when `startup-error` is set, none of the three branches is shown, so nothing takes the remaining height. The Servers page has no loading branch and shows "No servers" while loading.

```sh

export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=$D/runtime XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$D/config XDG_DATA_HOME=$D/data XDG_CACHE_HOME=$D/cache XDG_STATE_HOME=$D/state TMPDIR=$D/tmp
```

**Crate:** `ephervex-core`

## Behavior

The single-instance socket is named `ephervex-<uid>.sock` and placed only from `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (or the state/tmp fallbacks), never from the data or configuration directories. A desktop launcher started with a different `XDG_DATA_HOME` / `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (a test sandbox, or a second profile) therefore finds the socket of a launcher that serves other data and hands over to it instead of opening on its own data. Anything it carried, such as an `ephervex://` link or a pack file to open, is acted on by the launcher that owns the other data directory.

## Reproduction

Start Ephervex normally, then start a second one with `XDG_DATA_HOME=/some/other/dir XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/some/other/config ephervex-gui`. The second process exits after "handed over to the launcher that is already running".

## Expected behavior

Either key the socket on the data directory so launchers over different data are independent, or refuse the handover when the running launcher serves a different data directory and say why. Add a test for the chosen behavior.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/single_instance.rs` `socket_path` (383-386), `SocketDirectories::from_environment` (410-416), `host_local_state_directory` (486-490)
- `crates/gui/src/main.rs` 116-136 (handover and exit; needs a change only if the handover is refused with a reason)

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crates:** `ephervex-cli`, `ephervex-i18n`

From a manual pass over the mod and server commands.

## Wording

- `mod verify --server` fails with "this instance does not hold what it recorded", and "this instance still does not hold what it recorded" after repair (`crates/cli/src/main.rs` 5554, 5599).
- `server mods` on an empty server prints "No mods have been installed into this instance through a provider." (`mod-list-empty`, main.ftl 1798, printed for servers at main.rs 6240).
- A `CoreError` prints its localized sentence and then its technical line, which often repeats it, for example "Sodium is declared client-only, so it is not installed on a server." followed by "`Sodium` is declared client-only, so it cannot be installed on a server". `report_failure` (main.rs 9852-9895) only drops technical lines that exactly equal the summary.
- "Mods that need this one: 1. Pass --with-dependents..." and "Required mods that are turned off: 1." read awkwardly (main.rs 5147, 5178).
- "Changing an installed mod's version is not supported yet." reads like roadmap wording (main.ftl 1779).

## Misleading output

- `server mods` prints "3 installed mods" even when some are disabled or missing (`mod-installed-count` uses `snapshot.len()`, main.rs 6252).
- Plan output after an install shows a dependency both as `+` (to install) and `=` (already installed): `already_installed` is never subtracted from `dependencies` (`crates/mod-platform/src/resolve.rs` 1622). `=` lines and optional dependencies show bare ids instead of titles (main.rs 6098-6117).
- `--json server mods` gives `version: null` and uses the jar file name as `name` (`crates/core/src/mods.rs` 720-745).
- With `--json --include-incompatible`, client-only server results report `compatibility.compatible: true` (`crates/mod-platform/src/modrinth.rs` 268-282, main.rs 5885).

## Arguments and help

- `server mods <ID>` and `server delete <ID>` have no help for `<ID>` (main.rs 1510, 1583).
- `mod install` without a host names only `--instance` in its usage (`HostArgs`, main.rs 694-703).
- `--limit 0` is accepted and treated as 1 (`crates/mod-platform/src/model.rs` 442).

## Expected behavior

Server commands use server wording, counts and plan lines describe what is actually there, JSON reports real versions, names and server compatibility, every positional argument has help, and an out-of-range `--limit` is refused.

The GUI Diagnostics card already has server wording (`gui-diagnosis-files-unrestorable-server`); the CLI should likewise say the file has to be put back in the server folder by hand.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crates:** `ephervex-core`, `ephervex-pack`, `ephervex-i18n`

## Behavior

On a server, UtilitiX was installed from Modrinth, which installed LibX (`LibX-26.1.2-7.0.4.jar`) from Modrinth. Installing Skyblock Builder from CurseForge, which requires LibX on CurseForge, then fails with:

> A file Ephervex did not install is already in the way. .../mods/LibX-26.1.2-7.0.4.jar was not installed by Ephervex

The file was installed by Ephervex and is recorded under its Modrinth identity. Install planning only sees the requesting catalog's recorded mods (`installed_projects_of`, per ADR 0022), so the CurseForge LibX is planned as new, and the installer treats any file at the destination that is not the same catalog entry as hand-placed.

Clients are affected the same way. When the two catalogs' file names differ, the install succeeds and leaves two copies of the same mod.

## Expected behavior

A planned file whose published SHA-1 matches a recorded entry from the other catalog counts as already present and is reused: no second download, no second jar, and the dependent installs. Diagnostics already recognizes jars across catalogs by their bytes (`crates/core/src/dependencies.rs`).

If reuse is impossible, the error says what is really there (a mod Ephervex installed from Modrinth), keeping the current wording for genuinely unrecorded files. ADR 0022 is updated to allow byte-identical files to count as present across catalogs.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/mods.rs` `installed_projects_of` (2284-2302)
- `crates/pack/src/managed.rs` `disposition_for` (407-445), `crates/pack/src/mutate.rs` 469, 480
- `crates/pack/src/error.rs` 332, `crates/i18n/locales/en-US/main.ftl` 1756-1757
issues.title: Installing a mod whose dependency came from the other catalog fails with a false "not installed by Ephervex" error

## Behavior

Putting a pack mod aside leaves its recipe entry unchanged and records no put-aside state, so `verify_host` reports the jar `Absent` and `integrity_findings` raises "N recorded files are missing or damaged". On a client it offers Restore. On a server built from server files it says "1 has no recorded source. Import the pack again to restore it.", which is also wrong for a server, which has no pack to import.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crates:** `ephervex-core`, `ephervex-gui`

## Behavior

On a host built from a pack, the Mods bin puts a pack mod's jar aside and leaves a Restore row, and its confirmation says the mod stays in the list so it can be restored. `delete_mod_files_together` moves the jar into the retired directory only as a rollback buffer and removes it once the batch succeeds, so no copy survives.

Restore (`restore_mod_file_holding_the_gate`, then `ephervex_pack::restore_file`) can only download from a recorded address or find a verified copy in the shared Downloads cache by hash (`probe_cache_without_url`). A server built from published server files records every jar with no download address (`server_pack_recipe`), and the archive is not kept, so Restore fails, or turns into a manual-download prompt when a catalog happens to identify the jar. The same happens for any addressless pack file on a client, such as a jar shipped in overrides.

Introduced by the put-aside flow in 2e6fa99 and 3c9f6ca, with the final removal in b81eaf0.

## Expected behavior

The bin never destroys a file it promises can come back. Before dropping the set-aside copy, publish it into the shared Downloads content store under its strongest recorded hash, which restore already reads, or offer a permanent delete with honest wording when no source or cached copy exists. Add a regression test that puts aside and restores an addressless pack file.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/local_mods.rs` `delete_mod_files_together` (492-499)
- `crates/pack/src/server_pack.rs` `server_pack_recipe` (282-304)
- `crates/pack/src/install.rs` `restore_file` (200), `probe_cache_without_url` (738)

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crates:** `ephervex-core`, `ephervex-pack`, `ephervex-gui`

## Behavior

Creating a server from the Servers tab with a server files archive (for example the All the Mods 11 ServerFiles zip) takes Minecraft and the loader only from the New Server dialog, which defaults to Vanilla. Choosing the archive never reads it: `set_server_pack` / `ServerPackPicked` only store the path and name, the backend builds `NewServer::new` with the dialog loader, and core installs a vanilla server jar and extracts the archive over it. `validate_server_archive` checks only entry safety.

The result is a vanilla server with NeoForge jars in `mods/` that never loads them, named after the dialog's version ("26.1.2 Server"). Its Mods surface has no catalog browser and its mod manager says the loader cannot load mods. `server create --server-pack` in the CLI behaves the same. A server created together with a client from Import Modpack is fine, because it copies the client's loader.

Introduced in c7a5f25.

## Expected behavior

Never build a server whose recorded loader cannot load the archive's mods:

- refuse a Vanilla selection for an archive that carries mod jars;
- refuse a selection that contradicts the archive's loader evidence (NeoForge or Forge installer jar names, `libraries/net/neoforged/neoforge/<version>/`, `libraries/net/minecraftforge/forge/<mc>-<version>/`), read as untrusted entry names;
- in the dialog, prefill the Minecraft version, loader and loader version from that evidence when the archive is picked and say where they came from; when the archive has mods but no exact loader can be read, block Create while the loader is Vanilla. Never guess a version.

ADR 0024 is updated to say the standalone selection must agree with the archive.

## Locations

- `crates/gui/src/controller.rs` `set_server_pack` (2817-2838), `ServerPackPicked` (8215)
- `crates/gui/src/backend.rs` 4807, `crates/cli/src/main.rs` 2694
- `crates/core/src/server.rs` `validate_server_archive` (1307-1310)
- `crates/pack/src/server_pack.rs`
issues.title: A standalone server built from published server files is created as a vanilla server

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
In the AppImage build, pressing a mod's name in Manage Mod (the external link that opens its project page) opens no browser.

The GUI handler (`on_open_mod_project_page` in `crates/gui/src/controller.rs`) calls `ephervex_core::open_in_browser`, which hands the address to `open::that_detached` and shows a toast either way. That code path predates the AppImage build, so the AppImage environment is the suspected cause rather than the handler.

Every desktop hand-off goes through the same `open::that_detached` call and is likely affected the same way:

- `ephervex_core::open_in_browser` (project pages, the EULA and CurseForge API key help links, CurseForge restricted-download links, the CLI sign-in address)
- `ephervex_core::open_containing_folder` (diagnostic bundles)
- `open_folder` in `crates/core/src/instance.rs` (Open Folder)

## Still to confirm

- Whether it reproduces with the plain release binary outside the AppImage.
- Which toast appears (`open_in_browser` returns `false` and logs `could not hand the address to a browser` when the hand-off fails).
- What the launcher log says.

`packaging/AppRun` does not set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `PATH` or `XDG_DATA_DIRS`, so the environment the opener inherits differs from a plain launch mainly by what the AppImage runtime exports (`APPDIR`, `APPIMAGE`, `ARGV0`, `OWD`) and by the working directory. That narrows the candidates but does not rule them out.

## Fix direction

Once the cause is confirmed, launch the opener with any AppImage-specific environment removed or restored to the values from before the runtime ran. This must be verified inside the AppImage.

comments.author: MelanX
comments.bodyMarkdown: Not reproducible. Built the AppImage from main 28f10eae in the baseline container and ran it with a logging xdg-open on PATH. Both the CLI (`instance open --folder`) and the GUI (Open Folder) hand the same arguments to xdg-open as the plain binary does, and the opener sees only the expected APPDIR, APPIMAGE, ARGV0 and OWD additions. The maintainer then confirmed that opening works from the AppImage. Redirecting XDG_CONFIG_HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME (as a sandbox launcher does) changes which default browser xdg-open resolves, which is the likely source of the original report. No code change.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crates:** `ephervex-core`

Related: #541, which covers the byte-identical case.

## Behavior

Cross-catalog reuse (`crates/core/src/mods.rs` `reuse_identical_files` / `identical_recorded`) only applies when the release the requesting catalog resolves has the same SHA-1 as a file the host already records from the other catalog.

If the host has LibX 7.0.3 installed from Modrinth and a CurseForge mod that requires LibX resolves CurseForge's newest compatible LibX (7.0.4), nothing matches. The CurseForge LibX is planned as new, gets a different file name, and installs. `mods/` then holds two builds of the same mod, and the loader refuses to start because of the duplicate mod id. The install reports success. The reverse direction behaves the same.

Install planning has no cross-catalog notion of the same project. The only reliable signal is the jar's own mod id (`mods.toml` / `fabric.mod.json`), which diagnostics already reads.

## Reproduction

1. On a client, install mod A from Modrinth, which pulls dependency L at an older release.
2. Install mod B from CurseForge, which requires L on CurseForge, where CurseForge's newest compatible L is a newer release.
3. Both L jars are in `mods/`.

## Expected behavior

An install never silently leaves two copies of one mod. Either refuse (or ask) before installing a dependency whose jar has the same mod id as an installed mod from the other catalog, or prefer the other catalog's installed release when the requesting catalog publishes the same bytes under another release.
issues.title: Installing a cross-catalog dependency at a different release of an installed mod leaves two copies in mods/

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
Installs and version changes refuse a jar whose mod id (fabric.mod.json / quilt.mod.json / META-INF/mods.toml / META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml) matches an enabled jar in the same folder (crates/pack/src/mod_ids.rs require_distinct_mod_ids, called from install_managed and mutate_managed). Disabled jars, put-aside mods and recorded jars missing from disk are deliberately not counted. Other writers never run that check: the enable toggle (App::set_mod_enabled -> toggle_mod_file in crates/core/src/mods.rs, a plain rename), put-aside restore (App::restore_mod_file -> ephervex_pack::restore_file in crates/core/src/local_mods.rs), and host repair (App::repair_host / repair_host_files in crates/core/src/verify.rs, also via restore_file).

Repro: install LibX 7.0.3 from Modrinth on a client; disable it, put it aside, or delete its jar by hand; install a CurseForge mod requiring CurseForge's LibX 7.0.4 (succeeds, since no enabled LibX is present); now re-enable, restore, or run Repair. Both LibX builds are enabled in mods/ and the loader refuses to start, with no warning.

Expected: these paths reuse the pack crate's mod-id check (refuse or warn) before making the second jar visible to the loader.

Acceptance: re-enabling a disabled jar, restoring a put-aside mod, and repairing a host never leave two enabled jars declaring one mod id for the same loader family without the user being told (typed refusal before the rename/copy, reusing the pack crate's mod-id reader rather than duplicating it). Regression tests for each path.

Related: #548 (installs and version changes).

issues.title: Re-enabling, restoring a put-aside mod, or repairing a host can silently leave two jars with one mod id

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
When a planned dependency's jar declares the same mod id as an enabled jar already in mods/ (another catalog's release, the pack's, or a hand-placed local build), install_managed / mutate_managed refuse the whole operation with PackError::DuplicateModId, and ModInstallRequest has no way to skip a dependency. A user testing a hand-placed local build mods/libx-dev.jar cannot install any catalog mod that requires libx without disabling the build, installing, removing the downloaded release, and re-enabling the build. The same applies to another release installed from the other catalog.

Enhancement: when an incoming RequiredDependency is a mod-id duplicate of an installed jar, offer to treat the installed jar as satisfying it (skip writing the dependency and report it), or let the caller confirm skipping the dependency. Never silently substitute a release (AGENTS.md exact-version rules). The refusal text 'Remove or disable that file first if you want this release instead' also fits poorly when the user wants the dependent mod rather than the release.

Acceptance: installing a catalog mod whose required dependency's jar duplicates the mod id of an installed jar can complete without writing the duplicate, only after an explicit choice, with the plan/report saying which installed jar stands in. No silent release substitution.

Related: #548.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
`ephervex mod verify --server <ID> --shared` is accepted by argument parsing even though `shared` is declared `#[arg(long, requires = "instance")]` (crates/cli/src/main.rs, `ModCommand::Verify`). With the host arguments flattened from `HostArgs`, the requirement does not stop a server invocation.

At runtime `run_mod_verify` matches `(shared, host.instance)` and falls through to `None` for a server, so no shared-store check runs and nothing says the flag was ignored. A user may believe the shared libraries and client JAR were verified.

Reproduce: run `ephervex mod verify --server <any-id> --shared`. It goes straight to the server lookup ("No such server.") instead of a usage error. Seen on current local main (3e9c490d).

Expected behavior / acceptance:
- `--shared` together with `--server` is refused at argument parsing with a usage error (for example `conflicts_with = "server"`), or the command states that shared-store checking applies only to client instances. It never silently skips the check.
- A CLI regression test covers `mod verify --server <ID> --shared`.
