issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
App::apply_isolation_configuration (crates/core/src/isolation.rs) applies every round configuration, the kept outcome and the snapshot-missing fallback through apply_mod_toggles without the duplicate mod-id refusal that set_mod_enabled / set_mods_enabled run (ephervex_pack::require_distinct_mod_id, added for #549; isolation passes SecondCopies::Tolerated). Round configurations come from IsolationPlan::enabled_for, which always includes pinned_closure. Planning (isolation.rs, the loop over graph.entries) lets the user pin a mod whose presence is not Installed, i.e. a Disabled jar, and ModGraph::required_closure (crates/core/src/dependencies.rs) adds Disabled required dependencies to a closure.

Repro: a client has libx-7.0.4.jar enabled and libx-7.0.3.jar.disabled, both declaring mod id libx. Start an isolation session that pins the disabled jar, or whose candidate requires a dependency resolving to the disabled jar. Each round renames libx-7.0.3.jar.disabled to libx-7.0.3.jar; the loader refuses to start with two copies of libx and the round's failure is attributed to whatever the round tests. Keeping the outcome can leave both enabled permanently.

Expected: planning or round application refuses or warns (reusing ephervex_pack::require_distinct_mod_id) before a round or kept outcome enables a second copy of a mod. Restoring the session's initially_enabled set and undoing a failed toggle batch can stay unchecked, since they put back a state the host already had.

Acceptance: an isolation session never silently enables two jars declaring one mod id for the same loader family that were not both enabled when it started; regression tests for pinning a disabled duplicate and for a closure reaching one.

Related: #549 (enable toggle, put-aside restore and repair), #548 (installs and version changes).

<!-- ephervex-followup:36b16ed8-b0ff-4ccc-9cf4-b955fcc3cfc6 -->
issues.title: Isolation rounds can turn on a disabled jar that duplicates an enabled mod id without warning

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
ModInstallRequest::letting_installed_stand_in_for (crates/core/src/mods.rs) lets install_mods leave out a confirmed dependency when one enabled jar already declares every mod id its file does, and the CLI exposes it as `ephervex mod install --use-installed <PROJECT>`. Unconfirmed, such a dependency is refused with CoreError::ModDependencyAlreadyProvided.

Gaps:
1. The GUI install flows never set it: crates/gui/src/backend.rs Command::InstallMod (via App::apply_linked_mod_operation / LinkedModRequest::Install in crates/core/src/linked_mods.rs, for the client and each selected linked server) and Command::InstallServerMod. On ModDependencyAlreadyProvided the GUI only shows the refusal and offers no choice, so a developer with a hand-placed mods/libx-dev.jar still cannot install a mod that requires libx from the desktop app.
2. change_managed_mod_version / update_managed_mod (crates/core/src/mutation.rs -> ephervex_pack::mutate_managed, which calls require_distinct_mod_ids with no stand-ins) still refuse with PackError::DuplicateModId when a new release's dependency is provided by a hand-placed build or the other catalog's release, for example updating a mod that was installed with a stood-in dependency.
3. On a server, require_confirmed_server_support still asks for server-support consent for a dependency that ends up stood in.

Expected: the GUI offers an explicit choice to use the installed jar when ModDependencyAlreadyProvided is returned, on the client and each selected linked server, and retries with that dependency confirmed. Version changes accept the same explicit choice. No silent release substitution.

Acceptance: from the desktop app, installing a catalog mod whose required dependency an enabled jar already provides can complete without writing the duplicate after the user explicitly chooses the installed jar, on the client and on each selected linked server, and the result names the jar that stands in. A version change or update whose new release needs such a dependency offers the same explicit choice instead of failing. Without that choice nothing changes and the refusal stays as it is.

Related: #550 (adds the core/pack opt-in and the CLI flag), #548.

Starting a server without Minecraft EULA consent is presented as a failed run, with misleading Diagnostics and console text.

Observed in the desktop app (0.11.0 build of PR #554, fresh sandbox, vanilla 1.21.1 server, EULA never accepted), pressing Start:
- The core refuses the start during preparation (App::prepare_server_start_operation calls EulaStatus::require_valid() before any process exists), but the workspace shows the state pill "Failed" and the red run-failure notice "The server stopped with an error".
- The notice, the "Action Needed" toast and the Diagnostics page show the error's action text "Review the Minecraft EULA, then accept it interactively with the server EULA command." (error-server-eula-not-accepted .action in crates/i18n/locales/en-US/main.ftl). That is CLI wording; the desktop app's way to accept is Properties > Server EULA > Review and accept, which nothing points to.

- Diagnostics either checks EULA consent for servers or never claims "No problems found" when the last start was refused for missing consent.
- Console's unavailable text matches the server's actual state (stopped vs orphaned).

Acceptance criteria: GUI regression tests for a start refused for missing EULA consent (state, notice, message and action wording), and for the Console unavailable text of a stopped server.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-core`, `ephervex-gui`

## Behavior

A seasonal theme is shown only while its season lasts (`THEME_SEASONS` in `crates/core/src/seasonal_theme.rs`, ADR 0049): `shown_theme` takes the local date, so checking the Halloween theme outside October 25 to 31 means changing the system clock or preloading a clock shim. There is no supported way to preview a seasonal theme on any other day.

## Expected behavior

An environment variable, named `SEASONS_THEME` in the request, selects a seasonal theme for debugging regardless of the date. `SEASONS_THEME=halloween` shows the Halloween theme on every day, in place of Dark or Light as it is during its season. The mechanism must be generic: the value names a `SeasonalTheme` (by its `as_str` identifier), so a season added later is selectable without new plumbing.

Requested scope, as stated by the maintainer: the override replaces the date check. Decisions the implementation should settle and document:

- Value matching (case-insensitive is expected) and what an unset, empty or unknown value does; an unknown value must not break startup and should leave the date-based behavior in effect, with a diagnostic naming the accepted values.
- The override only replaces the date. The recorded theme, user themes and the Seasonal themes setting keep their meaning (a user theme is never replaced; turning the setting off shows the chosen theme), unless the maintainer decides otherwise in review. It never writes the theme setting (ADR 0049).
- The running window re-checks the date once a minute; the override must hold across those checks and across a restart for as long as the variable is set.
- The variable name is given as `SEASONS_THEME`; the only other documented variable, `EPHERVEX_LOG`, carries an `EPHERVEX_` prefix. Keep the requested name unless review decides on a prefix.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/seasonal_theme.rs` (`season_on`, `shown_theme`, `THEME_SEASONS`)
- `crates/gui/src/backend.rs` (`application_settings_on`, the date check)
- `docs/themes.md` (Seasonal themes; document the variable and the new extension step under Adding a seasonal theme)

## Acceptance

- Tests cover the override with a date outside the season, an unknown value, an empty value, the setting turned off, and a user theme.
- Production date handling stays the default when the variable is unset.

<!-- ephervex-followup:4df9899e-6138-4c96-bbc6-92f6505b292e -->

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
## Behavior

When a user supplies a distribution-restricted CurseForge file by hand, `adopt_into_cache` (`crates/core/src/download_watch.rs`) copies it into `ContentStore::Downloads` at its content address. `resolve_pack` later resolves the blocked file from that cache entry. Nothing records that this entry cannot be fetched again automatically.

Both ways of reclaiming the download store treat such an entry as regenerable:

- the byte-budget collector: `ContentStore::holds_reusable_artifacts` is true for `Downloads` (`crates/download/src/cache.rs`), and `crates/download/src/artifact_cache.rs` collects from every store it selects;
- the reference-based storage cleanup: `judge` in `crates/core/src/storage_maintenance.rs` marks every `Downloads` entry that no client version plan names as `Unused`.

The cleanup preview explains these entries with `gui-storage-why-downloaded-files` ("It is downloaded again when something asks for it"). That is not true for a manually supplied restricted file.

## Scenario

1. Import a CurseForge pack containing a distribution-restricted file and supply it through the download watcher.
2. Run storage cleanup (or let the byte-budget collector run).
3. Import the same pack again, or create a new disposable environment from it.
4. The file blocks again and the user has to download it by hand again.

If cleanup or collection runs between analysis and materialization of an import that resolved the file from the cache, materialization loses its source.

## Expected behavior

Record the provenance of adopted restricted files and withhold them from both collection and cleanup. At minimum, the cleanup preview must not describe them as re-downloadable.

## Locations

- `crates/core/src/download_watch.rs` `adopt_into_cache`
- `crates/core/src/storage_maintenance.rs` `judge`
- `crates/download/src/cache.rs` `ContentStore::holds_reusable_artifacts`
- `crates/download/src/artifact_cache.rs` byte-budget collection
- `crates/i18n/locales/en-US/main.ftl` `gui-storage-why-downloaded-files`

Related: #10 (storage maintenance), #205 (watcher adoption).
issues.title: Manually supplied CurseForge restricted files in the download store are treated as re-downloadable cache

The supplied-downloads/ directory itself falls into the catch-all (C::Other, R::Regenerable) arm.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
Host output captures are never removed when the host is deleted.

Paths::server_capture_dir (logs/servers/<id>) and Paths::client_capture_dir (logs/clients/<id>/<first|launch-HANDLE>) hold durable stdout/stderr capture segments. Per-directory retention caps each capture, but nothing removes a capture directory when its server or client instance is deleted: delete_client and delete_server in crates/core never touch them (verified: the only users of server_capture_dir are start, read, folder-open and diagnostics paths). Every launched disposable (temporary) instance therefore leaves a capture directory behind permanently.

Expected: deleting a host removes its capture directories, or a sweep removes captures whose host no longer exists.
Acceptance: a regression test that deletes a host with a capture and asserts the directory is gone.


<!-- ephervex-followup:a1d0220b-2035-4ccf-bd81-a53161a86dee -->
issues.title: Host output captures are never removed when the host is deleted

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
CI run 210 (push to main at e45c8969, job fmt, clippy, test) fails: ephervex-core storage_maintenance::tests::a_removal_that_fails_is_reported_and_its_bytes_are_not_claimed panics at crates/core/src/storage_maintenance.rs:2228 with Result::unwrap() on Err(NotFound).

The test makes the store shard directory read-only (0o555) to force a failed removal, and detects a privileged process (root, as in CI) by probing remove_file on the shard so it can return early. But it runs world.apply(&plan) and then unconditionally restores the shard permissions with set_permissions(...).unwrap() BEFORE checking `privileged`. As root the removal succeeds and the store inventory prunes the now-empty shard directory (crates/download/src/store_inventory.rs prune_empty_parents), so set_permissions on the missing shard fails with NotFound and the test panics instead of skipping.

Expected: the test passes (skips its failure assertions) when run as root; restore permissions only if the shard still exists, or check `privileged` before touching the shard.
Acceptance: the test passes when run as root and still asserts failed-removal reporting as a normal user; the CI job fmt, clippy, test is green.

<!-- ephervex-followup:2b9d75d0-ce21-4f7b-bf8e-b821465802a8 -->

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
The `Publish the release` step in `.forgejo/workflows/release.yml` (from line 180 to the end of the file) is a roughly 80-line inline shell script. It checks `RELEASE_TOKEN`, copies the AppImage, deb and rpm out of `dist/` by name, writes a `.sha256` beside each, creates or reuses the release for the tag, and replaces existing assets of the same name.

Move that logic into a script under `packaging/` that the workflow calls, so the workflow step only declares the secret, the environment and the call. The script can then be read, linted and run locally like the other packaging scripts.

Also decide whether `.github/workflows/release.yml` (478 lines, against 264 in the Forgejo workflow) should call the same script or be removed. The two workflows currently duplicate artifact selection and checksum logic.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
The minecraft-options compatibility dataset is published only as a GitHub Gist (`84f4b9229c20bb0fcda74215aabe3e76`), and `tools/minecraft-options/update.py` leaves publication as a manual step. There is no readable view of which Minecraft releases and options are covered, and the app depends on a third-party service for its data.

Serve the dataset from the documentation site instead, make that the feed the application reads, and stop publishing to the Gist.

## Scope

1. **Publish the file.** The site build copies the committed dataset `crates/options/data/minecraft-options.json` to a stable, unversioned URL, for example `https://ephervex.chaotictrials.de/assets/minecraft-options.json`, outside the versioned docs. The committed file stays the single source; no second copy is checked in.
2. **Add a docs page** that renders the dataset: which Minecraft releases and options are covered.
3. **Switch the application's default feed** from the Gist to that URL. `FeedSource::Document { url }` already exists in `crates/options/src/feed.rs` and derives its host allowlist from the URL, so this is a change to `FeedSource::default()` and its tests, not a new source and not a `FEED_HOSTS` entry. It ships with an application release.
4. **Retire the manual Gist step** in `tools/minecraft-options/update.py` and the docs that describe it, so committing the dataset is the only publish step.

## The site must rebuild when the dataset changes

The feed has to update between application releases, as the Gist does, so a release-only rebuild is not enough. `.github/workflows/pages.yml` does not do this today:

- The `push` trigger filters on `web/**`, `tools/auto-screenshot-tool/**`, `assets/**` and the workflow file. A commit that changes only `crates/options/data/minecraft-options.json` does not run it. Add that path.
- The build checks out the latest published release tag and builds the site from that source. The feed file must come from `main`, not from the release tag, or a dataset update would not be served until the next release. The docs pages can keep using the tag.
- Pages does not deploy until the first release is published. The application default must not switch before the feed URL answers.

## Decisions and prerequisites

- **Released applications** read the Gist and nothing else. Decide whether to keep mirroring the dataset to the Gist for supported releases, or accept that they keep their cached data and stop refreshing. This decides whether step 4 can happen at once.
- **Domain.** `ephervex.chaotictrials.de` and GitHub Pages must be live and verified (see `web/TODO.md`) before step 3.
- **Integrity.** The existing dataset validation stays the gate for the downloaded document; nothing in this issue relaxes it.

## Out of scope

- Automatically detecting new Minecraft releases.

## Acceptance

- The feed URL serves the committed dataset after a push to `main` that changes only the dataset.
- A fresh application release reads the feed from the docs site and falls back to its cached document when offline, as it does today.
- The docs page lists the same releases as the file.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
A server archive that carries only a root `forge-1.20.1-47.1.<n>-installer.jar` is read as a Forge server even when it is a NeoForge Minecraft 1.20.1 server.

`installer_loader()` in `crates/pack/src/server_pack.rs` maps a root `forge-<minecraft>-<build>-installer.jar` to `LoaderKind::Forge`. NeoForge's Minecraft 1.20.1 builds are published as `net.neoforged:forge`, so their installer carries the same file name (`forge-1.20.1-47.1.106-installer.jar` verified on maven.neoforged.net), and Forge and NeoForge 47.1.x build numbers overlap.

Actual: the archive evidence reports loader Forge. `ServerArchiveEvidence::conflict` in `crates/core/src/server_pack.rs` then refuses a NeoForge selection with `error-server-archive-loader-differs`, and a frontend that prefills from the evidence suggests Forge. If the archive also carries `libraries/net/neoforged/forge/1.20.1-<build>/`, the two entries disagree and the loader-kind evidence is dropped.

Expected: the installer name alone counts as Minecraft-version evidence only (or as ambiguous between Forge and NeoForge) unless other entries settle the loader kind.

Acceptance: a NeoForge 1.20.1 archive with only the installer jar does not refuse a NeoForge selection and does not suggest Forge; a Forge 1.20.1 archive keeps its current behavior; tests cover both.

Context: NeoForge for Minecraft 1.20.1 became an offered combination when #15 was fixed (the catalog, installer, and server files for that release use the Forge-named `net.neoforged:forge` artifact). That is what makes this installer name ambiguous in practice.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-server`

**Commit:** `cb2b89c3c18c48df303f132e500396ec93c876e4`

## Behavior

In a CI run on that commit (`CI / fmt, clippy, test`, run 218), `runtime::tests::a_process_that_started_before_the_supervisor_is_not_its_pending_child` (`crates/server/src/runtime.rs`) failed: `classify_runtime` did not return `RuntimeClassification::ProvenStale` (assertion at `runtime.rs:1662`). The other 144 tests in the crate and the rest of the workspace passed. The same test passed on the next CI run (run 219, commit `5803ec0ec35e3829d857c6e4f6f1ae636b9ee251`), on which `crates/server` is byte-identical, and in a local full `cargo test --workspace` run.

The test writes a pending start for the current supervisor with `supervisor.start_ticks = u64::MAX` through `write_dead_pending_start`, spawns a tagged `/bin/sleep`, and expects the pending-child scan to skip every process because none can have started after that supervisor. A process's start ticks are always below `u64::MAX`, so the scan can only report anything other than a gone child when it fails to read some process while walking `/proc`, which makes the classification unverifiable. The fixture is the one `a_pending_start_that_left_no_process_behind_can_be_cleared_without_editing_files` used when #452 reported the same kind of failure, where the outcome depended on process-table state that other tests in the same binary change concurrently.

The cause of this failure is not confirmed and it has not been reproduced locally.

## Expected behavior

The test passes regardless of which processes other tests in the binary spawn or reap while it runs, or the process scan is shown not to fail on a process that exits or changes during the walk.
