issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-options`, `ephervex-gui` and `tools/minecraft-options`

**Commit:** `2b2af1e4f8166d02e4732d19e040a53745d97a51`

## Behavior

Client-owned progress markers are handled inconsistently by the preference catalog:

- `tutorialStep`, `joinedFirstServer` and `startedCleanly` are in `EXCLUSIONS`, so a user cannot set them at all.
- `onboardAccessibility` has no exclusion and ships as an ordinary `language_and_accessibility` toggle with no translation key and no help text.

The categories are a closed set (`CATEGORIES` in `preferences.py`, mirrored by `PreferenceCategory` in `crates/options/src/catalog.rs`), so there is no place for markers a user may legitimately want to set. For disposable bug-reproduction instances the useful ones are exactly these: starting with the tutorial hint set to `none` and the accessibility onboarding already dismissed avoids first-launch screens that get in the way of a reproduction.

## Expected behavior

A dedicated category (name to be decided, for example "Onboarding") holds markers that are client-owned state but safe and useful to set. Each carries a durable description saying what it controls. At least `tutorialStep` (enum token, `none` disables the hints), `onboardAccessibility` and `joinedFirstServer` are candidates. `startedCleanly` stays excluded because it is crash-recovery state, not something to set. The category is added in the generator, in `PreferenceCategory`, and in the settings UI, and `docs` and the README describe it.

## Impact

Today `onboardAccessibility` appears among accessibility settings without a label, and the tutorial and first-launch markers cannot be controlled at all, so fresh instances open with first-launch screens.

## Locations

- `tools/minecraft-options/preferences.py` `CATEGORIES`, `EXCLUSIONS`
- `crates/options/src/catalog.rs` `PreferenceCategory`
- `crates/options/data/minecraft-preferences.json`
- the settings screens that list categories in `ephervex-gui`

## Validation and limitations

Read the generator, the committed catalog and the Rust enum. The meaning of `onboardAccessibility` (shown-once marker, default true) and of `tutorialStep` `none` is from knowledge of the game and should be checked against the bytecode before the descriptors are written. Which markers belong in the category, and how the UI should present them, is a product decision.
issues.title: Offer tutorial and onboarding markers in their own preference category

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `tools/minecraft-options`

**Commit:** `f844b107`

## Behavior

`arithmetic_chain` collects adjacent `<const> <arith-op>` pairs and skips every other instruction, including method calls. `analyse_option_window` resolves the persisted `Codec.xmap` through `xmap_transform(dis, window[:idx], members, owner)` with the default `plain=False`, so `lambda_arithmetic` never applies the `is_plain_arithmetic` guard on this path. A pair whose lambdas call `Math.pow`, `Math.log10`, `Math.round` or `Mth` helpers is accepted when `invert_ops(encode) == decode` on the linear remainder, and is reported with `transform_resolved: true`, a `value_to_storage` formula and `transform_ops`, although the real storage transform is non-linear.

The mouse wheel sensitivity slider pair (`logMouse` = `Math.pow(10, i / 100.0)`, `unlogMouse` = `round(log10(d) * 100)`) resolves through `xmap_transform` as `[* 100]` in 1.19, 1.21.4 and 26.2 when `plain` is not set. Today that pair is a slider mapping, which `slider_step` already reads with `plain=True`, so no persisted transform in the bundled dataset is wrong.

## Expected behavior

A codec xmap lambda containing any invocation other than boxing and unboxing (`BOXING_CALLS`) or any branch is left unresolved (`xmap_unresolved`), exactly like the slider path.

## Impact

A release that moves such a pair onto the persisted codec would publish a wrong `value_to_storage` transform at high confidence.

## Locations

- `tools/minecraft-options/analyze_options.py` `analyse_option_window` (codec `xmap` branch), `xmap_transform`, `lambda_arithmetic`, `is_plain_arithmetic`, `arithmetic_chain`

## Validation and limitations

Read from the current code; the slider pair was checked against the cached 1.19, 1.21.4 and 26.2 JARs. A regression test can use a synthetic javap listing with the helpers in `tools/minecraft-options/test_option_analysis.py`.
issues.title: A persisted codec xmap whose lambdas call methods is read as plain linear arithmetic

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-options` (generated data) and `tools/minecraft-options`

**Commit:** `f844b107`

## Behavior

The bundled dataset has a `cloudStatus` codec for 1.12.2 through 1.16.5 (unquoted `enum_token` `true`/`fast`/`false`) and from 1.20.2 (quoted `enum_token`), but none for 1.17 through 1.20.1. The setting is neither supported nor unsupported there, so it stays unknown.

- 1.17 through 1.18.2 (field access persistence): the analyzer records `renderClouds` as `custom_codec` with `file_encoding` "enum, codec unresolved".
- 1.19 through 1.20.1 (OptionInstance definition): the codec xmap is reported with `transform_resolved: false`.

The JARs still prove the token set statically. In 1.17 (root class `dvs`, enum `dvc`) the visitor call for `renderClouds` binds two synthetic lambdas through `invokedynamic`: a string switch comparing `true`, `fast` and `false` to the enum constants, and an ordinal switch returning `true`, `fast` or `false`. This is the same raw token set proven for 1.12.2 through 1.16.5.

## Expected behavior

The analyzer follows the `invokedynamic` bootstrap to these synthetic methods, requires that the reader accepts every token the writer returns, and emits an `enum_token` codec for 1.17 through 1.20.1, with the quoting each release actually writes (to be checked for the OptionInstance releases 1.19 through 1.20.1). Without that proof the setting stays unknown.

## Impact

Cloud status cannot be managed for 1.17 through 1.20.1. This is safe, but leaves a gap between 1.16.5 and 1.20.2.

## Locations

- `tools/minecraft-options/analyze_options.py` custom codec visitor path, `enum_string_lambda`, `token_bindings`
- `tools/minecraft-options/dataset.py` `_enum_codec`

## Validation and limitations

Checked against the committed `minecraft-options.json`: `cloudStatus` is absent from the supported settings of exactly 1.17 through 1.20.1. Related: #582 (1.12.2 through 1.13.2 token codec) and #607 (enum extraction).
issues.title: Cloud status has no codec for Minecraft 1.17 through 1.20.1

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-options` (generated data) and `tools/minecraft-options`

**Commit:** `f844b107`

## Behavior

`validate()` documents that it refuses exactly what the application's loader refuses. It now checks codecs, keys, representation positions, the unsupported lists, revision and `data_version`, but not the other field types `crates/options/src/dataset.rs` requires through serde:

- `RegistrySetting.key` and `type` must be strings, `category` and `translation_key` optional strings, `manageable` a bool;
- `canonical_minecraft_version`, `ReleaseMapping.minecraft_version`, `ReleaseMapping.schema` and `SchemaFamily.id` must be strings;
- `SchemaFamily.supported` must be a string-keyed object.

A hand-edited or corrupted previous dataset with `manageable: null` or a numeric `category` passes `validate()` and is published, then refused wholesale by the application as malformed. A non-object schema, release or registry entry, or a non-hashable schema id, makes `validate()` raise `TypeError`, `KeyError` or `AttributeError` instead of `DatasetError`, which `update.py main` does not catch.

## Expected behavior

`validate()` refuses these shapes with `DatasetError`.

## Impact

A dataset the application cannot load can still pass the publication gate, and clients silently keep their old data.

## Locations

- `tools/minecraft-options/dataset.py` `validate`
- `crates/options/src/dataset.rs` (serde field types)

## Validation and limitations

Read from the current `validate()`; `schema["supported"].items()` and `release["schema"] not in families` are reached without a type check. Follows #601, whose fix covers codecs, keys, positions and the unsupported lists but not these field types.
issues.title: Dataset validation does not check the registry, release and schema field types the application deserializes

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `tools/minecraft-options`

**Commit:** `f844b107`

## Behavior

The options analyzer reads string constants from the comments in `javap -c` output, and javap does not print them verbatim:

- It escapes control characters. A constant `"x\n"` prints as the comment `String x\n` and `"t\t"` as `String t\t`, so `Insn.string()` returns the literal backslash sequences instead of the real value.
- It prints U+2028 and similar line-separator characters raw. `parse_members` splits the text with `str.splitlines()`, which also breaks on those characters, so the `ldc` line is cut there and a constant such as `"a<U+2028> "` is read as `a`.

`with_trailing_spaces` already rewrites `ldc` String lines from the class constant pool, but only appends the trailing spaces javap drops.

## Expected behavior

`Insn.string()` returns the exact constant. The exact values are already available from `string_constants` (class bytes, by constant pool index) and can replace the comment text for `ldc` String operands, and the listing is split on `\n` only.

## Impact

Low for current Minecraft option defaults. A default or token containing such a character would be recorded with the wrong value.

## Locations

- `tools/minecraft-options/analyze_options.py` `with_trailing_spaces`, `Insn.string`, `parse_members`, `Disassembler.get`

## Validation and limitations

Reproduced with javac and javap 25 on a class holding these constants: javap prints `// String x\n`, `// String t\t` and a raw U+2028. Follows #604, whose fix restores empty and padded constants but not escaped or line-separator ones.
issues.title: javap-escaped and line-separator string constants are not read as their exact values

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-options` (generated data) and `tools/minecraft-options`

**Commit:** `f844b107`

## Behavior

`crates/options/data/minecraft-options.json` lists the `version` setting (key `version`) in the `unsupported` array of the schemas for 1.12.2 through 1.13.2 and every release from 1.17 on (37 releases in revision 56), while the 1.14 through 1.16.5 schemas list it as supported. `SchemaFamily::unsupported` means settings that provably did not exist in a release, but every one of those releases writes a `version:<data version>` line to options.txt and has a `data_version` in its release mapping for exactly that marker (for example 1.12.2 = 1343, 1.20.1 = 3465, 26.1 = 4786).

Suspected cause: `dataset.py` `schema_for()` records every canonical setting missing from an `extraction_complete` record as unsupported, while `analyze_options.py` extracts the schema marker separately rather than as a setting.

## Expected behavior

The version marker is supported (integer codec) wherever the release writes it, or is excluded from the unsupported derivation, and the dataset is regenerated.

## Impact

Anything that trusts `unsupported` as proof of absence gets the wrong answer for `version`. `every_fixture_line_is_a_key_and_value_its_release_writes` in `crates/options/tests/era_fixtures.rs` has to skip `VERSION_KEY` to avoid a false failure.

## Acceptance

- No schema lists `version` as unsupported for a release that has a `data_version`.
- A regression test covers it.
- The era fixture test no longer special-cases the marker.

## Locations

- `tools/minecraft-options/analyze_options.py` (schema marker extraction)
- `crates/options/data/minecraft-options.json`

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `tools/minecraft-options`

**Commit:** `f844b107`

## Behavior

`analyse_option_window` records `enum_default_constant` from the last `getstatic` of an enum-typed field in the window tail. It does not check whether that `getstatic` is a jump target or inside a branch (`Insn.join` / `Insn.conditional`, set by `mark_control_flow`). A definition such as `new OptionInstance<>(..., cond ? Mode.A : Mode.B, ...)` gets the else-arm constant as a high-confidence default, either through the enum default resolution in `analyse_option_window` or through the later string-token pass in `analyze_jar` (`record.get('default') is None and constant`).

The `valueOf`, `Boolean.valueOf`, boolean factory and constructor field-initializer sites already refuse conditional constants (#581); the enum site does not.

## Expected behavior

An enum default constant is accepted only when its `getstatic` runs unconditionally (`runs_unconditionally` on the `getstatic` and its consumer). Otherwise the default stays unproven with the conditional-default note. A regression test covers a ternary enum constant.

## Impact

A scan of all 52 cached release JARs found no window where this happens today, so shipped data is unaffected, and the fix must not change either committed data file for those releases. A future release with a conditional enum default would get a wrong proven default.

## Locations

- `tools/minecraft-options/analyze_options.py` `analyse_option_window` (enum `getstatic` in the tail loop, enum default resolution), `analyze_jar` (string-token default pass)
issues.title: An OptionInstance enum default chosen by a condition is recorded as the else-arm constant

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-options`

**Commit:** `28fa50f6`

## Behavior

From 26.1 the client has a `graphicsPreset` option (`fast`, `fancy`, `fabulous`, `custom`). Right after it loads `options.txt`, the client calls `Options.applyGraphicsPreset(graphicsPreset)` on every launch. For `fast`, `fancy` and `fabulous` this writes a fixed value to every option the preset controls; `custom` leaves them alone. A file without `graphicsPreset` gets the default, `fancy`, so the preset runs and replaces whatever the file said for those options.

Ephervex does not know about this coupling. It writes a managed value such as `renderClouds:"false"` without `graphicsPreset`, and the client discards it at startup and saves `graphicsPreset:"fancy"` and `renderClouds:"true"`.

Verified by starting unstarted 26.1.2 (data version 4790) and 26.3 (5023) instances whose `options.txt` held only Ephervex-written entries. Every entry survived unchanged except `renderClouds`, which went from `"false"` to `"true"` in both. 1.12.2 and 1.20.1 instances kept every entry, since those releases have no preset.

The options the preset sets (from `GraphicsPreset.apply` in 26.3): `ambientOcclusion`, `biomeBlendRadius`, `cloudRange`, `cloudStatus` (`renderClouds`), `cutoutLeaves`, `entityDistanceScaling`, `entityShadows`, `improvedTransparency`, `maxAnisotropyBit`, `menuBackgroundBlurriness`, `mipmapLevels`, `particles`, `prioritizeChunkUpdates`, `renderDistance`, `simulationDistance`, `textureFiltering` and `weatherRadius`.

## Expected behavior

When a managed preference is one of the options the release's graphics preset controls, and the release has `graphicsPreset`, the written file also stores `graphicsPreset:"custom"`, so the managed value is what the game runs with. The set of preset-controlled options should be derived from the release's own `GraphicsPreset` bytecode by the analyzer and recorded in the compatibility data, not hard-coded per release. A user who manages `graphicsPreset` themselves keeps their choice. Releases without the preset are unaffected.

## Impact

Any managed value for the options above is silently reverted on the next launch of 26.1 and later, so the instance does not run with the configuration the user selected. Add a regression test that writes a preset-controlled preference for a release with `graphicsPreset` and asserts `graphicsPreset:"custom"` is present.
issues.title: Managed graphics settings are reverted by the game's graphics preset from 26.1

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-options` (generated data) and `tools/minecraft-options`

**Commit:** `28fa50f6`

## Behavior

In the 26.2 data, the defaults of `key.smoothCamera` and `key.spectatorOutlines` are proven unbound (`key.keyboard.unknown`). In the 26.3 analysis both key mappings have `code: null` and `unbound: false`, so their catalog descriptors carry no default (`keybind_smooth_camera` and `keybind_spectator_outlines`). **Commit:** `4614552d`

## Behavior

`default_change()` in `tools/minecraft-options/analyze_options.py` returns `None` for every key binding whenever the previous and current releases have different `keybinding_code_space` values. The `glfw` and `hid` code spaces both serialize bindings as the same `key.keyboard.*` and `key.mouse.*` names, so a real default-key change between 26.2 (`glfw`) and 26.3 (`hid`) is comparable by its serialized name, but the generated change history never reports it. issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-options` (generated catalog), `tools/minecraft-options`

## Behavior

The bundled preference catalog offers 185 Minecraft settings as global defaults, including every key binding, every graphics option and dozens of release-specific toggles. Each one needs a proven storage form for every supported release, and several have release-specific behavior outside `options.txt` itself: key bindings use three numbering schemes, the graphics preset replaces a group of settings at startup, and the game's data fixers rewrite entries of older files. Most of that surface is rarely wanted as a global default and has produced most of the compatibility defects found so far.

## Expected behavior

The catalog offers a short, curated set whose storage has been stable across the supported releases: GUI scale, language, fullscreen, window size, field of view, render distance, simulation distance, gamma, auto-jump, cloud status, the dark loading screen, the sound volumes, the two key bindings in common use (sprint and swap offhand), and the onboarding and multiplayer-warning flags. Every other current setting is excluded with one stated reason instead of being offered. The compatibility dataset keeps its full per-release proofs, so a setting can be offered again later by adding it to the curated set. A configuration entry for a setting that is no longer offered stays in the configuration file untouched and is not applied.

## Impact

Smaller defaults screen, fewer per-release failure modes, and less to verify for every new Minecraft release.
issues.title: Offer a short curated set of Minecraft settings as global defaults

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crates:** `ephervex-options`, `ephervex-storage`, `ephervex-core`, `ephervex-gui`

## Behavior

The global Minecraft defaults offer a curated set of settings (#629). Anything outside that set, such as a setting added in a new release, a mod's option or a rarely used key binding, cannot be put into the `options.txt` of a new instance.

## Expected behavior

The Minecraft defaults screen has a free-text area for raw `options.txt` lines. The text is stored in the configuration, and when an instance's `options.txt` is written, each line is applied after the managed preferences: a line whose key already exists in the file replaces that line, and any other line is appended. Lines are written as given, with no check against any release's settings, codecs or data version; the user is responsible for their correctness, and the screen says so.

The only requirements are those of the file format: a line is `key:value` with a non-empty key, a line that cannot be one (no separator, a control character in the key or value) is reported to the user and not written, and the data-version marker line (`version`) is never taken from the text because it belongs to the release being written. Blank lines are ignored. Because raw lines are applied last, they win over any managed preference and over the line Ephervex adds for the graphics preset. A raw line is applied only to instances created or imported afterwards, like every other default, and never to an existing instance.

## Impact

Any setting can be set as a default without waiting for the catalog to offer it, while the catalog itself stays small and fully verified.

## Validation

Tests cover replacing an existing key, appending a new one, ignoring blank lines, refusing a malformed line and the `version` line, and precedence over a managed preference. The configuration field defaults to empty so existing configuration files load unchanged.
issues.title: Let the user add raw options.txt lines to the global Minecraft defaults

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
Signing in with Microsoft uses the device-code flow, and the code and verification address are shown only in a short-lived toast (`AuthEvent::DeviceCode` in `crates/gui/src/backend.rs`). The toast can disappear before the code is typed, and the code cannot be copied from it.

The dialog closes when the sign-in finishes or fails, and a failure keeps its actionable message.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-options`

## Behavior

The bundled preference catalog `crates/options/data/minecraft-preferences.json` is out of step with the compatibility dataset it is generated from. The descriptor `simulation_distance` has category `gameplay`, while `crates/options/data/minecraft-options.json` records `simulationDistance` with category `Video`, and the 26.3 analysis gives `Video` too. The Minecraft defaults screen therefore shows Simulation distance under Gameplay instead of next to Render distance under Video.

`python3 tools/minecraft-options/preferences.py --from-analysis <analysis of the cached releases> --check` fails with "the bundled catalog does not match what these inputs regenerate". Regenerating changes only this one category.

## Expected behavior

The committed catalog is exactly what `preferences.py` regenerates from the committed dataset, so `simulation_distance` is in `video` and `--check` passes.

## Reproduce

1. Analyze the cached releases with `tools/minecraft-options/analyze_options.py`.
2. Run `preferences.py --from-analysis <that output> --check`.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
**Crate:** `ephervex-cli`

## Behavior

When a client instance is created or imported, the raw `options.txt` lines from the Minecraft defaults (`minecraft_raw_options` in the configuration, #630) are applied after the managed preferences. A line that cannot be an `options.txt` line (no `:` separator, an empty key, a control character, or the `version` data-version line) is not written and is listed in `PreferenceApplication::raw_lines_rejected`, with `raw_lines_applied` counting the lines that were written.

The CLI creation report ignores both. The human output after `print_instance` in `crates/cli/src/main.rs` prints unsupported, unknown and skipped managed preferences, and `preferences_applied_json` serializes the same fields, but neither mentions rejected raw lines or the applied count. Core only logs a warning. The GUI shows rejected lines while the user types, but a user who edited `config.toml` by hand or who scripts the CLI gets no feedback that a line was dropped, although #630 requires a malformed line to be reported to the user.

The messages `preferences-raw-line-missing-separator`, `-empty-key`, `-control-character` and `-data-version` already exist in `crates/i18n/locales/en-US/main.ftl`.

## Expected behavior

- Human output prints one line per rejected raw line using `RawLineProblem::message_id()` with its line number.
- JSON output includes the rejected lines (line number and problem) and `raw_lines_applied`.

Verified at `8ce3ae9a`.
issues.title: CLI instance creation does not report raw options.txt lines that were not written

issues.bodyMarkdown:
Settings > Minecraft shows each option (`MinecraftPreferenceRowCard` in `crates/gui/ui/settings/minecraft-defaults.slint`) as a stack that only widens its controls when the page is not narrow. The Workbench reference (`workbench-settings-minecraft.png`) lays each row out as two columns on a wide page: the text on the left (option name, "Not overridden | default ...", and the compatibility line such as "Supported" or "Unavailable: Minecraft 1.12.2 does not have this setting"), and the control with its Reset button on the right, vertically centered, so the controls line up down the page.

Scope:

- From a width the page can hold both columns, the text column and the control column sit side by side with the controls aligned to one edge across rows. Below that width the rows stack as they do now. The breakpoint is a named measurement in `Theme`, not a literal in markup.
- Every editor kind keeps working in the control column: toggle, slider with its readout, dropdown, window size with the keep-ratio box, text, and key binding.
- Unavailable and unverified rows keep their hatched, disabled look and their reason text; nothing moves out of keyboard order, and the Override/Reset buttons keep their tooltips and accessible names.
- Text at 90% to 125% and the CI font (DejaVu) must not overlap or clip the two columns; add a layout test at those scales for the widest editor (window size).

No change to the draft, validation, or save behavior.

issues.author: MelanX
issues.bodyMarkdown:
`organization::tests::concurrent_updates_do_not_lose_each_other` (`crates/storage/src/organization.rs`) fails with `update: Busy { path: ".../data/organization.lock" }` when the machine is heavily loaded.

The test starts eight threads that each call `Organization::update`. Each update takes the organization lock through `FileGuard::take` with `ORGANIZATION_LOCK_PATIENCE` (five seconds). Under enough load a waiting thread does not get the lock in that time and gets `Busy`, so the test panics.

Seen while `cargo test --workspace` ran next to a CI run and other builds (load average above 200): it failed once in the workspace run, and once in 15 repeated runs of the test alone. It passes in the normal case, including in an earlier full workspace run on the same code, so this is not a regression of the code under test.

Expected: the test does not depend on the lock being granted within five seconds on a machine under load, for example by giving the guard more patience in tests, or by the test tolerating `Busy` and retrying. Check whether a real caller can hit the same five-second limit before choosing, because the lock is also taken by the interface and the CLI.
issues.title: The organization concurrency test fails with Busy when the machine is heavily loaded

pulls.author: MelanX
pulls.bodyMarkdown:
## Summary

Adds a durable, dependency-aware mod isolation workflow for narrowing Minecraft mod issues to a one-minimal reproducing configuration.

Isolation is available through both the CLI and GUI for client instances and local servers. It reuses the existing dependency graph, mod mutation APIs, and snapshot system.

## Behavior

- Treats every enabled mod outside the pinned closure as an isolation candidate, including mods required by other candidates.
- Merges only required dependency cycles that cannot be separated by any valid configuration.
- Keeps every tested configuration valid by closing it over required dependencies.
- Keeps pinned mods and their required transitive dependencies enabled throughout the search.
- Preserves shared dependencies whenever a remaining candidate requires them.
- Runs deterministic dependency-aware subset/complement ddmin with durable round history and granularity progression.
- Produces a one-minimal result when exhaustive removal testing establishes one; zero/one-candidate cases are reported as the smallest testable set reached.
- Persists version-1 session state in `.launcher/isolation.json`.
- Reconciles the exact pending round after restarting Ephervex or detecting mod-state drift.
- Supports undo, contradiction detection, finish, and cancel.
- Refuses isolation mutations while the target host is running.
- Allows the host to be launched while waiting for a round answer.
- Never mutates a linked server during client isolation.
- Requires an explicit reduced-confidence acknowledgement when required dependencies are missing.
- Requires a separate explicit reduced-confidence acknowledgement for refreshable but unrecorded dependency information.
- Treats unidentifiable jars as independent candidates and marks the result unproven.
- Invalidates an unstarted setup when the host's mod state changes, while preserving it when nothing actually changed.

## Snapshot integration

A pre-isolation safety snapshot is created before the first mutation.

Cancel restores the exact pre-isolation state through the existing snapshot API. Finish leaves the minimized reproducing configuration enabled and retains the safety snapshot for later restoration.

## CLI

Adds:

- `mod isolate start`
- `mod isolate status`
- `mod isolate resume`
- `mod isolate answer`
- `mod isolate undo`
- `mod isolate finish`
- `mod isolate cancel`

Text and JSON output follow the existing CLI conventions.

## GUI

Adds:

- A dedicated Isolation surface for client instances and local servers.
- Isolation setup and pinned-mod selection.
- Dependency-knowledge warnings and separate reduced-confidence acknowledgements.
- A visible explanation whenever `Start isolation` is unavailable.
- Exact enabled/disabled round configuration.
- Issue-present and issue-gone answers.
- Undo and contradiction views.
- Persistent active-session workflow state.
- Automatic restart/interruption reconciliation and recovery.
- Busy/progress feedback while isolation mutates the host.
- Result, finish, and cancel workflows.
- English localization for the complete workflow.

## Documentation

- Adds ADR 0036.
- Adds the mod-isolation user guide.
- Documents persistence format and compatibility policy.
- Updates architecture, ADR index, and README documentation.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace`
- `git diff --check`

Focused core, CLI, and GUI isolation tests also pass.

pulls.author: MelanX
pulls.bodyMarkdown:
Adds a constrained split workspace: two to four panes, each showing one installed client or local server on one of its surfaces. A pane chooses where a host's feature is displayed; it never owns that feature's state.

Closes #4

## Layouts

- Single, `1:1`, `2:1`, `1:2`, `2:2`, as a typed `WorkspaceLayout` whose only representable values are those shapes.
- Split beside from a single pane; split below from a full-height pane of a split; close from any pane of a split. Closing settles deterministically on the next smaller shape in reading order, down to the single pane.
- Equal columns and rows. Below `Theme.workspace-pane-min-width/height` (360x260) the pane area scrolls instead of letting panes overlap.
- No persistence: the workspace opens as a single pane, and opening a host from a list replaces the layout.

## Pane UI

- The single-pane workspace looks as before, with a split icon in its header.
- A split pane has a compact header: the host (a button that opens a card picker), its state, Restart and the primary action on one row; the surface tabs, split below, and close on the next.
- The host picker shows clients and servers as cards. A client's linked servers are offered on its card. Clients rank by what runs on their card (client and linked server, client, linked server, nothing); servers list running ones first.
- Surface tabs that do not fit wait under **More**, and the selected surface always keeps a tab.
- One Back above a split, leaving for the page the split was opened from.
- Accessible pane labels name position, host, and surface ("Top right pane: Repro Server, Console").

## State ownership

- One host view per shown host, however many panes show it. Every feature writes by host: snapshots, runtime settings, server properties, mod lists and catalog searches, isolation, Diagnostics and bundle choices, workflow status.
- Pane-local: each Logs or Console pane's viewer (mode, file, filters, search, wrap, Following, selection).
- Single-flight guards stay global: the isolation change, the verification or repair, one restart per host, and the host-change claim. Two panes on one host cannot start the same work twice.
- A workflow's banner is left to the pane showing the workflow's own surface, so an Isolation round is not repeated above the host's other panes.
- A deleted host keeps its pane, which says "No longer installed" and can be retargeted or closed.

## Fixes found along the way

- Late mod metadata no longer restores a stale list: the enriched list is reconciled with the host's current mods, and metadata is kept only for the same artifact (file, origin, exact identity, hashes, size).
- Starting isolation announces the safety snapshot it takes.
- Host overviews fit narrow panes instead of scrolling sideways.

## Tests

- `workspace_layout` unit tests for every shape, transition, and close position.
- Controller tests: shape transitions and labels, host choice and ordering, restart from two panes is one restart, isolation surviving another pane's changes, per-host isolation, Diagnostics, mods, and log viewers.
- Headless Slint tests (`tests/split_workspace.rs`): geometry of every shape at 1480x900 and 980x680 (no overlap, minimum size), header inside its pane, split and close controls, host picker, tabs and More, shared host state, header actions on the pane's own host, workflow banner placement.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` (108 suites, 2770 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored).

## Related, not closed

- #16: per-pane viewer state and closing a source only when its last viewer leaves are done; sharing one tail between viewers, stale-tail rejection, and drawing new lines while Following is off are not. Details in the issue.
- #13 / #7: the Split Workspace consistency parts (lifecycle state and host-owned state shared across panes, actions targeting the pane's host) are covered; the rest is not.

## Manual acceptance

- [ ] Single-pane workspace looks and works as before.
- [ ] Enter each layout; close every pane position and check normalization.
- [ ] Client in one pane and server in another; the same client in two panes on different surfaces.
- [ ] Change a surface in one pane; the other pane keeps its own.
- [ ] Start or restart a host in one pane; the other pane on it follows. A second Restart is refused.
- [ ] Active Isolation in one pane, Logs or Mods for the same host in another: one session, mods update when a round applies, banner only on the Isolation pane.
- [ ] Diagnostics in one pane with another surface for the same host.
- [ ] Switch a pane from a client on Settings to a server: it lands on Overview.
- [ ] Delete a host shown in one pane: it says so and can be retargeted or closed.
- [ ] Host picker order with running clients, running linked servers, and stopped hosts.
- [ ] Tabs and More at a small window size; no clipping or overlap at 980x680.
- [ ] Settings > Disk Usage unchanged; no pairing behavior from a client and server side by side.

## Non-goals

Linked client/server pairing (#5), launch supervision, docking, recursive splits, floating or detached panes, presets, draggable dividers, layout persistence, Disk Usage changes.

pulls.bodyMarkdown:
Moves the desktop interface out of the `slint!` macro in `crates/gui/src/ui.rs` into standalone `.slint` modules under `crates/gui/ui`, compiled by `slint-build` from `build.rs`. This is the same UI moved, not a redesign: no behavior, layout, or visual changes are intended.

Closes #8

## Structure

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `app.slint` | `AppWindow` only: its Rust-facing properties and callbacks, navigation shell, pages, and modals. Re-exports everything Rust uses |
| `theme.slint` | The `Theme` global |
| `globals.slint` | `GuiI18n`, `PropertyRules` |
| `models.slint` | The 35 row/view structs |
| `components/` | `text.slint`, `controls.slint`, `artwork.slint` |
| `workspace/` | `host-workspace`, `mods`, `logs`, `isolation`, `diagnostics`, `snapshots`, `host-settings` |
| `home/` | `host-cards`, `activity-cards` |
| `settings/` | `application`, `minecraft-defaults` (including `WindowSizePreview`) |

`crates/gui/src/ui.rs` is now a doc comment and `slint::include_modules!();`. `docs/architecture.md` has a short section on the layout and build.

## Compatibility

- All 40 previously generated types (3 globals, 35 structs, `AppWindow`, `WindowSizePreview`) are still generated under the same names. No controller, backend, or integration-test code changed.
- Every moved declaration was checked by script to be byte-identical to the single-file original, apart from the added `export` keyword and asset path depth. The one intended edit: four `rgb(...)` theme colors are written as their identical hex values, since the macro lexer workaround they existed for is gone.
- `build.rs` keeps the `fluent` style and keeps Slint debug info for every profile except release, as before.
- Workspace lints now apply to the `include!`d generated code, so five lints are allowed on the `ui` module only, next to the existing `unsafe_code` exception.
- The markup-reading controller tests read the `.slint` sources through `test_support::UI_SOURCES`. Assertions are unchanged; only boundary detection moved from macro indentation to top-level declarations. A new test fails if a `.slint` file is missing from that list.

## Costs

Measured with the `.deb` built in fresh `ephervex-baseline:22.04` containers, no caches, one run each:

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Build time (download + build + package) | 274.6 s | 289.9 s (+5.6%) |
| Peak process memory | 9.01 GiB | 8.90 GiB |
| `.deb` | 27.59 MiB | 27.74 MiB (+0.5%) |
| `ephervex-gui` binary | 82.9 MB | 85.6 MB (+3.2%) |
| Target directory | 2.14 GB | 2.69 GB |

- `slint-build` 1.17.1 adds 58 build-only crates (mostly `image` codecs). They come from compiler features `slint-build` always enables (`software-renderer`, `bundle-translations`) and cannot be turned off from here. Nothing new ships: the license inventory is unchanged, and `deny.toml` gains one Slint license exception for `slint-build`.
- GUI binary growth: `.rodata` is identical, and both binaries contain the same 564 generated UI types, so the module split duplicated nothing. The generated UI code is about 1.5% larger across every component, mostly because about 6,000 small binding-initialization closures stay out of line. That points at the compiler inlining the build-script output differently from the macro output. This is not proven further.
- After a `.slint` edit, Cargo rebuilds the crate once more than needed because of timestamp rounding. It then settles.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` (2777 passed, 0 failed), `git diff --check main...HEAD`
- `cargo deny check licenses` and `tools/licenses/generate.sh --check`
- Clean and release builds. The release binary embeds the SVG icons and contains no source-tree paths.
- `.deb` built and smoke-tested with `packaging/build-deb.sh` in the baseline container.

Not yet checked:

- [x] Launch the app and confirm it looks and behaves as before
- [x] RustRover's Slint plugin recognizes the modules (its preview may need the `fluent` style set)

## Left for later

`AppWindow` is still one ~2,480-line component, because its pages and modals read the window's own properties directly. Splitting it further changes structure rather than moving it, so it belongs in separate changes.

pulls.author: MelanX
pulls.bodyMarkdown:
Adds a linked client/server workflow on top of the split workspace: a client is paired with one of its linked servers, the pair can be shown side by side without touching the panes already open, and either side can start both as one operation.

Closes #5

## Pairing

- A pair names one of the servers already linked to the client (`linked_client_id`). Pairing never creates, changes, or removes a link, so linked mod sync and Launch & Connect are unaffected by unpairing.
- A client's oldest linked server is its pair by default, however it was created (by hand or by a pack import). Choosing another linked server replaces it. Unpairing keeps the client unpaired while the server it declined stays its first; once that one is deleted, the next first linked server is paired again. A chosen server that disappears falls back to the first.
- Only a choice is stored: `config.toml` under `[linked_pairs.<client id>]` with the chosen server, `start_together`, and the server that was unpaired from. The default needs no entry. Pairs survive a restart of Ephervex.
- Not on the server record: host records are mirrored column by column into the SQLite index, which stays at its initial migration until 1.0.0 (ADR 0033).
- ADR 0040 records the decision.

## UI

- Pane header (single and split): a **Paired** badge beside the host's state badge, on every surface. It is left out of a split pane narrower than 420px so the header actions keep their room.
- Client Overview: the Reproduction Environment card says **Paired with <server>** and offers **Show beside**. Each linked server card shows **Paired** beside its state badge, **Unpair** (or **Pair with client**) next to Delete, and a compact **Start together** switch.
- Server Overview: a **Paired with** row in its details card, **Show beside** after Launch Client & Connect, **Unpair** (or **Pair with its client**) next to Delete, and the same switch.
- Narrow cards use three rows: Start/Stop with Launch Client & Connect, Open Server Workspace with Open Folder, then Unpair with Delete.
- No client- or server-specific pane components; either host keeps all of its normal surfaces.

## Show beside (additive only)

Built on a new `WorkspaceLayout::reveal`:

- a pane already showing the counterpart (once or more) is reused, and the layout is left exactly as it is;
- otherwise one pane is added: Single to 1:1, 1:1 stacks in the column the asking pane is not in, 2:1 fills its right column, 1:2 fills its left one;
- every existing pane keeps its host, surface, column, and row;
- 2:2 is never changed: the button is disabled with a hint, and an automatic reveal reports that no pane is replaced.

**Launch & Connect** and a **Start together** start show both sides the same way: the workspace opens on the client when it is closed, and a missing side is added beside the other, the server on its Console. Starting a paired server never moves the client's pane off the client.

## Starting together

- With **Start together** on, Launch or Start on either side is one Launch & Connect run: the server is started or reused, then the client launches connected to it. If the client is already running, only the server starts.
- Nothing reacts to a host having started by starting another, so neither side's start can lead back to the other's.
- The controller tracks one pair start per pair by operation number. While it runs, another Launch or Start on either side, and Restart, are refused, and both hosts show **Starting the pair...** in every pane. A running side can still be stopped.
- The worker settles the start exactly once through a drop guard: when the client is running, or on failure, refusal, cancellation, or panic. A late settle of an earlier start is ignored.
- A failure names the side that failed (from whether the server became ready). A server that started is left running, and the pair is kept.

## Restart

- Restart never consults the pair.
- A client started by Launch & Connect, including a pair start, is restartable once its server is ready. Restart relaunches only the client, as the same account, joining the same server target. It never starts or restarts the server.

## Fix

- A launched client no longer stays **Starting** while its game runs. Starting is announced before the game's process exists, so the refresh it triggered could read the lock before the game was recorded; the rows are now read again once the game runs.

## Tests

- Storage: pair round trip with unknown keys; credential-shaped keys dropped.
- Core: default pair; choosing, replacing, and unpairing from either side; unpairing surviving a reopen and a new server, and re-pairing once the declined server is gone; fallback when a chosen server is deleted; unlinked, standalone, deleted, and malformed entries; the start decision for each side and a running client.
- Layout: reveal for Single, 1:1 (both sides and no asking pane), 2:1, 1:2 with every existing pane unchanged; 2:2 unchanged; counterpart already shown, or shown twice, adds nothing; revealing twice adds one pane.
- Controller: Show beside in single, full, and already-shown workspaces; Launch & Connect from the client, from the server, with no workspace, and in a full workspace; a pair start from either side shows both, the server on Console; two panes read one host view; closing panes and leaving the workspace never unpair; a pair start is one command with nothing after it; either side waits while its pair starts; settle and stale settle; Restart never starts the pair.
- Backend: the settle guard fires exactly once on drop, early take, and unwind; failure attribution per side; restart keeps the joined server target; a running game refreshes the rows.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`: 2823 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored
- `git diff --check main...HEAD`
- Visual check of both overviews, the pane headers, and the split at several widths with a software-rendered harness.

## Known limitations and follow-ups

- **Open Server Workspace** still points the pane it was clicked in at the server; a server started alone from a single-pane workspace still follows to its console. Both are existing navigation, not the pair action.
- Only the plain Launch and Start buttons start the pair; **Launch as** does not.
- The server always starts first; if it fails, the client is not launched.
- A restarted client whose server has since stopped relaunches alone and fails to connect in game.
- The full-width host header overflows below about 900px window width (also on `main`).
- Not included: CLI pair commands, pair restart, pair-aware isolation, showing the counterpart's running state.

Closes #21.

## What changes

- **Complete palettes behind semantic tokens.** `Theme`'s color tokens now read the active `ThemePalette`. The built-in Dark and Light palettes live in `palettes.slint`, the only place a color is written. Components are unchanged and never learn which palette is active. `crates/gui/src/palette.rs` is the one place that turns the preference into a palette. Text sizes, the monospace family and layout measurements stay outside the palette (ADR 0041).
- **User themes.** TOML files in `~/.config/ephervex/themes/` appear in Settings > General > Interface theme. A theme sets `name`, a built-in `parent` (`dark` or `light`) and any subset of colors; every color it leaves out comes from the parent. Files are bounded in count and size and parsed strictly. Problems are listed under the setting, one line per file, and a bad file never affects the others (ADR 0042, format in `docs/themes.md`).
- **Example.** `docs/themes/modrinth.toml` is a complete Modrinth-style dark theme. A test keeps it valid and complete, and another keeps the token table in `docs/themes.md` in step with the palette.
- **Config compatibility.** `[display] color_scheme` keeps its existing `dark` / `light` values, and a user theme is recorded as `user:<file-stem>`. An unrecognized value no longer makes the whole config fail to load: it paints the default palette and is written back unchanged until another theme is chosen.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` (2849 passed, 2 ignored).
- Dark and Light match `main` exactly. All 34 color tokens resolve to the same values, and headless renders of 24 states (lists, overviews, split workspace, logs and console, mods, isolation, diagnostics, settings, dialogs, toasts) at two widths in both schemes are byte-identical to `main`, except the theme setting card, whose text changed.
- Every state was also rendered in the Modrinth example and checked by eye.

Real-window acceptance across pages, dialogs, popovers and the split workspace under Dark, Light and a user theme.

pulls.author: MelanX
pulls.bodyMarkdown:
Diagnostics now answers whether a host is configured correctly for what it runs, and why a launch or crash failed, instead of only verifying files.

## What changes

- **Problem vs. Valid, customized.** Findings are classified. A custom Java that runs the release, custom JVM arguments, memory overrides, and hand-placed jars are customizations, not errors. A host with only customizations is healthy.
- **Findings from stated evidence only:** Java plan and its override layers (incompatible major/update/architecture, unusable path, detection or download off), turned-off or missing required mods with the chain that needs them, declared conflicts, the mandatory dependencies Forge/NeoForge refused in the last start's log, a crash report written after the last start, and missing/damaged recorded files and shared launch files.
- **Cross-catalog requirements.** A requirement names a project in its requirer's catalog, so absence is only reported once proven. Diagnose asks that catalog to identify the other jars by SHA-1 (Modrinth) or fingerprint (CurseForge), and names a missing project known only by id.
- **Preview, then Apply.** Enabling turned-off requirements, removing a host's Java override when automatic selection leads somewhere that works, and restoring recorded files are previewed; Apply does exactly that, reports partial success, and diagnoses again. Ambiguous changes (which version of a missing mod) route to the owning surface instead.
- **Manual by default.** Opening Diagnostics runs nothing. After a failed run a quick pass (no hashing, no network) shows a notice on the client Overview with the likely cause and Open Diagnostics / crash report / log. Nothing navigates on its own.
- **Copy technical report** (home paths as `~`, JVM argument values left out); the verbatim bundle is now the secondary step behind its own disclosure.
- Host-keyed state and one diagnosis or fix at a time, per ADR 0039; a fix claims the host like repair did.

Decision recorded in ADR 0043.

## Left out

- Server Overview crash notice actions (#6 owns that surface); servers get the quick diagnosis and the Diagnostics context.
- Installing a missing dependency from a preview; Fabric/Quilt log parsing; version ranges only a jar's own metadata declares; a CLI `diagnose` command.
- The Mods page relation panel still matches requirements by project id only, so it can call a jar from another catalog "not installed here".

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` (2880 passed), `git diff --check main...HEAD`.
- New core tests (dependency chains, loader log, offline diagnosis with a fake JVM and seeded metadata, cross-catalog confirmation against loopback catalogs), controller flow tests, and markup tests including two panes at the minimum window width at 1x and 1.5x text.
- Visual QA of every state in Dark and Light, split and 1.5x. Final visual acceptance is pending.

Closes #2

pulls.bodyMarkdown:
Local servers get the everyday development operations: a clear lifecycle state, a working console, and direct routes to the server's files and logs. Arbitrary file editing stays in the desktop's own tools.

## What changes

- **Lifecycle state.** Starting, Running, Stopping, Restarting, Stopped, and Failed come from one per-server state, so every pane showing a server agrees. Starting covers preparation; Running means the Java child was spawned, not that Minecraft accepts connections.
- **Host header actions.** Kill..., Restart, and Stop sit in the header of every server pane, in that order. Kill still asks for confirmation and stays available during a restart.
- **Console.** Commands go through the existing supervisor control channel (ADR 0014), no RCON. Delivery is reported only after a confirmed stdin write and names the server. A delivered command clears the submitting pane's field; a refused or failed one stays for correction, and drafts in other panes are untouched. A pending submission disables input in every view of that server. A failed input channel stays disabled until a new child starts, and the Console says why input is unavailable. Output takes the remaining height.
- **Files.** Overview has Open Server Folder (the directory with `server.properties`), a Properties shortcut, and a folder selector for config, Minecraft logs, crash reports, captured output, mods, and the server root. Logs and crash folders that were never written are reported unavailable instead of being created.
- **Logs.** Logs separates Ephervex's captured stdout/stderr ("Captured output") from files Minecraft writes, and its Folder action follows the selected mode. Overview links to Console and Crash reports.
- **Failure handling.** An intentional Stop or Kill never requests Diagnostics, whichever of the control reply and the exit arrives first. A real failure uses the existing quick diagnosis, and a late result for an old run is ignored after a new start. Stop, kill, and console requests run off the GUI worker loop, so other hosts stay usable while a server responds.

## Left out

- The server Overview still uses `CrashNotice`, not `RunFailureNotice` with Open Diagnostics / crash report / log.
- Dedicated controls for individual `server.properties` settings beyond the existing Properties form (#12).
- Showing whether a linked counterpart is currently running (#7, #13).

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` (2912 passed, 2 ignored), `git diff --check main...HEAD`.
- New tests cover console outcomes (delivered, rejected, unavailable) staying server-wide across panes, a disconnected worker refusing a submission and releasing the guard, intentional stops not triggering diagnosis, folder shortcuts resolving to the selected server and reporting unwritten folders as unavailable, and the Console layout giving each lifecycle action once per pane with output filling the height in single and split views.
- Manual desktop acceptance is pending.

Closes #6

pulls.author: MelanX
pulls.bodyMarkdown:
Bug fixes found while testing the release with a real Forge server and its linked client, before v0.10.0.

## What changes

- **A server that fails during startup is a failed run.** Minecraft's server catches a startup exception, logs it, and exits with code 0, so a Forge loading error looked like a clean stop: no notice, no quick diagnosis, Diagnostics empty. The supervisor now records whether each child logged vanilla's `Done (...)! For help, type "help"` line, and whether a Stop or Kill through the control channel ended it. A clean exit before the ready line counts as a failure unless the user asked for it. The run's result and its Activity entry use the same classification, so a Stop during startup is never reported as failed.
- **The failed-run notice is shown above every surface** of the host except Diagnostics, which already leads with the failure. It never navigates on its own, and any of its actions dismisses it.
- **Crash notices clear when the host starts again** ("This server failed to start" on Overview and Mods). A crash review now only describes the last run: a report older than the last start is not reviewed again.
- **Linked servers leave client-only mods alone.** A server's recipe also records what only the client takes (`server: unsupported`, client overrides). The server's mod list, verification and repair, and dependency checks read the client's side of it, so those mods showed as missing, a restore put them back, and a client-only mod such as Lighty then crashed the server. The server now reads its own side. Only content unsupported on a side is absent on purpose there; a deselected optional entry that an installed mod requires is still reported missing, on clients and servers.
- **One loader finding per missing mod id.** The loader names one line per asking mod. Those lines are grouped by the exact mod id they lack, with the narrowest range every requester accepts. Ranges follow Maven's range rules and version order and are only combined when that is certain (numeric bounds that are dotted, or have `.` and `-` in the same places); otherwise each distinct range is listed with the mods that asked for it. Loader refusals lead the findings, so the failed-run notice's likely cause names the refusal rather than the crash report.
- **Evidence stays separate.** A loader mod id is not a catalog project, display name, or jar name, so a loader refusal, a recorded relation, and a crash report are separate findings however alike their names are. Only a finding backed by a recorded or proven catalog identity offers an action.
- **Each missing mod has its own action.** A mod the host records whose jar is gone offers "Restore <name>" at the recorded release, and a restore touches exactly the files its preview listed. A mod nothing records, whose catalog project is known, offers "Install latest compatible version" on a client; its plan, exact release included, is always shown in the install confirmation before anything installs.
- **Logs:** an open crash report scrolls inside its view instead of pushing the tab down; Log Files has the same header search and Find as Crash Reports; the redundant "These files are written by Minecraft or the server software." line is gone.
- **#27:** desktop tools (`xdg-mime`, `update-desktop-database`) run against explicit roots get `HOME` and the XDG variables inside those roots, so a test run no longer rewrites the developer's `~/.config/mimeapps.list`. The user's own session is unchanged.

Docs: `docs/architecture.md` (what a failed server run is, the server side of a linked recipe) and ADR 0043 (loader grouping, separate evidence, restore and install actions, notice placement).

## Left out

- Installing a missing mod on a server: servers have no catalog install path yet (#28). A recorded one is restored; an unrecorded one keeps the Mods page advice.
- A `stop` typed into Ephervex's console before the server finished starting counts as a failed start; only a Stop or Kill through Ephervex's controls is known to be intentional.
- `last_started_at` does not advance for a restart's replacement child. That limitation predates this PR and is kept separate from it.
- Jars that an earlier restore put onto a linked server (for example JustEnoughResources, oauth, Lighty) stay on disk and now show as hand-placed mods to delete.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` (2948 passed, 2 ignored), `git diff --check`.
- Every commit on the branch passes `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` on its own.
- `~/.config/mimeapps.list` is untouched by a full workspace test run.
- Manual acceptance with a real server is outstanding: start without a required library and see Failed and the notice on every tab; Diagnostics shows the loader refusal with `[1.20.1-5.0.14,)` and, separately, the recorded LibX with a Restore action; a Stop during startup is not reported as failed; starting again clears every notice; a linked server created from a pack with client overrides reports and restores no client-only mod; "Install latest compatible version" on a client opens the confirmation before installing.

closes #27

Loader installation now rejects conflicting declarations before downloading libraries or replacing shared-cache files. Declarations from the install profile, loader version metadata, and (for client installs) vanilla parent metadata must agree on SHA-1 and size whenever they resolve to the same cache path.

Comparison uses the entries installation actually selects, honoring platform rules and the first stored entry. Distinct Maven coordinates that resolve to one path are compared as the same file, and server downloads use the same path-based duplicate selection. Conflict diagnostics identify the library, metadata source, hashes, and sizes.

Regression coverage includes size-only conflicts, downloaded and installer-carried libraries, parent metadata conflicts, cache-path aliases, excluded and duplicate entries, and preservation of cached files without network requests on failure.

Capture the real Slint UI with synthetic fixtures in every theme, publish the captures through a Docusaurus documentation site under `web/`, and serve the Minecraft options feed from that site.

## Screenshot tool (`tools/auto-screenshot-tool`)
- Headless capture of the real `AppWindow`, fixed `en-US` locale, mocked time, no controller, no storage or network access. About 100 states, including the Workbench shell, Home, quick view, the Case tab and the Add Mods dialog.
- Rows come from data recorded from real packs, mods and servers in an isolated launcher home (`data/`, documented in `SOURCES.md`).
- Rendered with Skia, which draws item transforms and rounded clips that Slint's software renderer ignores. Skia is the `skia` feature of the tool, off by default and turned on by `generate.sh`, so it stays out of the license inventory and `cargo deny`. A build without it refuses to generate.
- Six themes: Light, Dark, Halloween, Christmas, Pride and April Fools. The default run writes 1920x1080 only; `--size 2560x1440` is still available.
- Original PNGs and contact sheets are gitignored.

## Website (`web/`)
- Guides for every feature, an interface tour, a generated CLI reference, an install page, a screenshots page with a viewer, and local search.
- `ThemeScreenshot` loads only the active theme's image. Lossless WebP assets are generated from the PNGs, and their manifest is committed. The site follows the color mode and the four seasonal themes.
- Road to v1 archive: an export of the Forgejo issues and pull requests (615 issues, 22 PRs), a read-only exporter, and a browser at `/road-to-v1/`. The data was replaced in every commit of this branch by a fresh export.
- Minecraft options coverage page at `/minecraft-options/`, built from `crates/options/data/minecraft-options.json`.

## Options feed (refs #575)
- `pages.yml` publishes the committed dataset byte for byte at `/assets/minecraft-options.json`. It takes the file from `main`, not the release tag, and a push that changes only the dataset rebuilds the site.
- The application's default feed is now that document. The Gist source is removed from `ephervex-options`. The feed host allowlist is derived from the URL, and the existing validate-then-cache logic is unchanged: an unreachable site, an error page or a bad document leaves the cached or bundled dataset in use. New tests cover a site answering 404, 500 and 503.
- `tools/minecraft-options/update.py` no longer writes a separate feed file. Merging the dataset is the publish step.
- Applications released before this one read the Gist and keep their cached data. There is no mirror.

## Licenses
- The third-party inventory, `about.toml` and `deny.toml` cover `i-slint-backend-testing` under the royalty-free terms of the other Slint crates. `tools/licenses/generate.sh --check` passes.

## Verification
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p ephervex-options`, `cargo test -p ephervex-screenshots`, `cargo test -p ephervex-core --test offline_operation`, and the `tools/minecraft-options` Python tests
- In `web/`: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run screenshots:check`, `npm run archive:test`, `npm run archive:check`, `npm run options:test`
- The full `cargo test --workspace` runs in CI.

## Not verified yet
- The first Pages deploy: the feed URL answering, the `jq` check and copy step in `pages.yml`, and Skia's prebuilt binary download on the GitHub runner. Pages still deploys only after the first release, and the domain setup is open in `web/TODO.md`.

Replaces #380, which was opened through the AGit flow.

A local server can now search Modrinth and CurseForge and install mods directly, without a linked client and without touching one.

- **Search** uses the server's exact Minecraft version and loader. Mods declared client-only are left out: Modrinth is asked to drop projects with no server support, and both catalogs drop hits whose newest fitting release is declared client-only. A hit whose server side is not stated stays and is marked with "?". "Show incompatible mods" lists client-only mods marked "Client only", with Install disabled.
- **Install** works against the server's own recipe and `mods/` only; a server with no recipe gets one. Exact selections are refused rather than substituted. A client-only root is refused. Installing a mod whose server support is not stated, or one that needs such a mod, requires a confirmation that names each of them. A client-only required dependency is installed with a warning and recorded as installed on the server while keeping the catalog's declaration (new additive recipe field `installed_despite_unsupported`). Restricted CurseForge files go through the existing manual acquisition with the catalog's sides. A running server receives the change for its next start.
- **CLI**: `mod search|show|plan|install` take `--instance` or `--server` (the positional instance is gone), and `--accept-unknown-server-support` is the confirmation for a server install.
- **GUI**: the server Mods surface has the same catalog browser as a client (hidden for Vanilla and for a server without its base installation), and Diagnostics offers "Install latest compatible version" for an unrecorded missing dependency on a server.
- **Also included**: the selected release's own side declarations are now recorded for identified and re-recorded mods. ADR 0021 now describes the running-server rule the code follows. ADR 0045 records the direct-install decisions.

pulls.bodyMarkdown:
Closes #9

Makes a large instance collection easier to find your way around: search, combinable filters, a remembered sort order, favorites, groups and icons. None of it touches an instance's identity, paths, links, snapshots or timestamps.

## Desktop

- **Instances toolbar:**
  - All / Temporary / Persistent, plus a Favorites toggle.
  - Live search over name, Minecraft version, loader, source and group.
  - **Filters** opens a captioned panel: Minecraft version, loader, running state, linked servers, group, and sort order (favorites first, name, Minecraft version, loader). The order is remembered.
  - **Groups** opens group management. **Clear filters** appears while anything narrows the list, and the header shows "N of M instances". A filter that hides everything says "No instances match".
- **Cards and inspector:**
  - Favorite star, and a group badge beside the name in that group's own color.
  - A custom icon in place of the loader symbol.
  - The inspector's Organization section has the group choice, a Remove from group button, Manage groups..., and Choose / Remove icon.
- **Groups:** create, rename and delete, each with a toast. A group keeps its color through renames. Group lists show only real groups, so leaving a group is its own action and a group can be named anything, even "No group".
- **Elsewhere:** icons show on the Running page and in the split workspace. The workspace host picker gains search and ranks favorites first; it always offers every host, whatever the Instances filters hide.
- Selection follows the instance by id, so re-sorting or filtering never moves it to another one.

## Command line

- `instances list` gains `--search`, `--favorite`, `--group` / `--ungrouped`, `--minecraft`, `--loader`, `--running` / `--stopped`, `--linking paired|servers|none` and `--sort`.
- New commands: `instance favorite|unfavorite|group|icon`, `server favorite|unfavorite|icon` and `groups list|create|rename|delete`.
- JSON records carry `favorite`, `linking`, `group` and `icon`.

## Storage and safety

- Favorites, groups and icon references live in one launcher-level `organization.json` (its own format version 1, written compactly, changed under a file lock). It is never part of host metadata, so no restore, promotion, move or reconciliation rolls it back, and no diagnostic bundle carries it.
- Changes take no host claim and do not bump `updated_at`, so they work while a host runs.
- Every change first keeps the previous state as `organization.old.json`. A damaged file is copied aside, reported and never overwritten, and the previous copy takes its place. It starts empty only when both are unusable.
- Icons are untrusted input:
  - The file is capped at 16 MiB, and the decode is bounded at 8192 px on a side and 16 MP, so ordinary photos work.
  - The image is scaled to 256 px, re-encoded as PNG and stored by content hash.
  - An icon is removed once neither the file nor its previous copy names it.

## For reviewers

- **Search, filters and sorting:** these are pure core functions shared by the CLI and the GUI. The name sort is natural ("test 2" before "test 10"). The Minecraft version sort uses the cached manifest and never the network.
- **Theme:** six new palette tokens, `group-tone-1` to `group-tone-6`, are set in both built-in palettes and documented in `docs/themes.md` and the example theme.
- **Docs:** ADR 0048, a new architecture section, the format-version table and the README.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` all pass on the rebased head.
- Every round passed an independent review, the rebase included.
- Manually checked in a sandbox with a release AppImage, including every CLI command above.

pulls.bodyMarkdown:
## Problem

A theme could only change colors. Themes that ship their own logo and window icon (#378) need theme folders, plus a way to load images from them without letting a theme read files outside its own folder.

## Change

- **Theme folders.** `themes/<id>/theme.toml` is read beside standalone `<id>.toml` files. A usable folder takes priority over a same-named file. A folder that is a symbolic link, or that cannot be used, is reported and never hides the file.
- **`[branding]`.** `logo` and `icon` name files inside the theme's own `branding/` folder. A reference is refused before anything is opened if it is absolute, uses `.` or `..`, or contains a backslash, a colon (drive letters, URLs, URI schemes), a control character or a doubled `/`. It is also refused if it is too long, nested too deeply, or not `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg` or `.webp`. Each refusal reason gets its own message.
- **Confined loading in `ephervex-core` (`theme_package`).** Every path component below the themes folder is opened with `openat(O_NOFOLLOW)` relative to the directory opened before it. A symbolic link at any level is refused, and replacing a folder after it was opened cannot redirect the read. The final file is opened with `O_NONBLOCK` and checked to be a regular file using `fstat` on the open descriptor. It is read up to 4 MiB, and its contents must be the format its extension names. It must be at most 1024x1024 pixels, and the decoder's allocation is capped at 16 MiB from the moment it reads the header. Icons are centered on a transparent square, and logos keep their shape.
- **UI.** Only the chosen theme's images are decoded, on the backend thread. The Slint `theme-logo` and `theme-icon` properties fall back to the embedded default logo whenever one is empty, and logo and icon fall back independently. The themed window icon is also handed straight to winit, because Slint only re-sends the icon when the image's cache key changes, and every image decoded at runtime has the same empty key.
- **Built-in themes.** Built-in themes can declare compiled-in branding that goes through the same bounded decoder and never reads from disk. Dark and Light declare none.
- **Docs.** `docs/themes.md` (layout, format, image types, security rules, platform icon limits), `docs/architecture.md`, a new ADR 0046, and an amendment note on ADR 0042.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace` all pass (4884 tests).
- New tests cover:
  - valid PNG, JPEG and WebP files;
  - missing, malformed and mislabeled files;
  - oversized files, a header claiming huge dimensions, and a compressed color-profile chunk that inflates past the cap;
  - every refused reference form;
  - symbolic links at the file, intermediate-folder, `branding/` and package level;
  - FIFOs;
  - a folder replaced after it was opened, and a concurrent link-swap race;
  - shadowing, fallback, compiled-in branding, and switching between two themed icons and back to the default.

## Limitations

- On Wayland the compositor takes the window icon from the desktop entry, so only the logo inside the window follows the theme there.
- On X11 the window icon changes, but docks that match the window to the desktop entry, such as GNOME Shell, keep showing the installed icon.
- A hard link inside `branding/` is read like any other file. Creating one needs the user's own permissions.

Follow-ups to #523 (#28), from two rounds of manual testing of the server Mods surface.

## Fixed

- **A result stayed "Queued" after installing, and a deleted mod stayed in the list until a tab switch.** A host view row was rewritten even when unchanged, and Slint 1.17's repeater then dropped the in-place change. Rows are now rewritten only when they changed. Clients were affected too.
- **Server-support badges** sit above the Install button, like a managed mod's badges above its bin. The "?" badge explains itself inside the row, because a Slint tooltip at the window's right edge runs off it.
- **The server's mod list matches the client's:** same panel, title, card, width and description placement, and both descriptions start level with the browser's.
- **Open Providers & APIs** from a mod browser's CurseForge key notice now opens Settings (closing the workspace dropped the pane mid-handler). Clients were affected too.
- **Unstated server support is asked about once:** a mod already on the server is not confirmed again, alone or as a dependency (core, GUI and CLI).
- **Diagnostics no longer offers to install a client-only dependency on a server**; it says the dependent most likely belongs only on a client.
- **Wording:** "Vanilla cannot load mods" instead of "Vanilla instances cannot install mods"; the Manage Mod release list and the pack-owned notices no longer say "instance".
- **CLI:** the unconfirmed-install refusal prints its next step on its own line instead of a literal `\u{a}`; `mod show --server` marks client-only and unstated mods; search prints and returns where the next page starts.

## Added

- **A server's own mods can be changed and removed** (version change, update, removal through the same Manage Mod dialog a client uses). A server made in Ephervex treats its mods as the user's (ADR 0032, ADR 0045); its bin removes the mod and the dependencies nothing else needs. A version change that would add a mod with unstated server support is refused until that mod is installed from the catalog.
- **Servers have a Settings tab** like clients: memory and JVM arguments (`App::set_server_jvm_settings` keeps the Java pin), the Java runtime section (moved there from Properties; the Overview's Java pill opens Settings for both kinds), and **Independent mod changes**, so a server built from a pack can let its mods be changed. The setting lives in the server's metadata only, because ADR 0033 reserves the next index migration for after 1.0.0. Diagnostics findings about a server's own runtime open its Settings tab.

## Notes

- `server runtime` in the CLI comes from #527.
- Pre-existing problems found while testing are tracked separately (server-files server recorded as Vanilla, put-aside jars without a source, inspector name elision, Import Modpack overlap, cross-catalog dependency conflict, tooltips at the window edge, other pane buttons that leave for Settings, CLI wording, opening a project page from the AppImage).
