pulls.author: MelanX
pulls.bodyMarkdown:
## Problem

Before a launch, Ephervex did not show which Java a host would run or whether that runtime fits the host's Minecraft version and loader. A runtime problem usually surfaced only as a failed launch with the raw JVM error. Choosing another runtime meant editing a path by hand, with no indication of which runtimes were compatible.

## Change

- **One rule evaluation.** `ephervex-java` judges a runtime against a host in one function: the required major, the loader's update bounds, and the architecture. Automatic selection, the pinned-runtime check, the picker, the host status and Diagnostics all use it, so they cannot disagree for the same inventory.
- **Runtime visibility.** Each client and server shows:
  - its runtime's path, version, vendor and architecture;
  - how the runtime was chosen (automatically, pinned by the host, or pinned by the launcher preference), and whether Ephervex manages it;
  - what the host expects, e.g. "Java 8, update 320 or older (Forge)".

  The status reads Healthy, Valid, customized, or Problem, in the same language as Diagnostics. It appears in the workspace header, in the host's Settings/Properties, in Diagnostics, and in `ephervex instance runtime` / `ephervex server runtime`.
- **Picker and previewed changes.** The runtime section lists every known runtime with the host's verdict. The runtime the default entry already uses is not listed twice. Compatible runtimes come first; incompatible ones are disabled with what the host requires. It also accepts a custom path, which is probed before use. Any choice, and Diagnostics' Java fix, opens the same review. The review shows the runtime before and after and changes nothing until Apply. Valid custom runtimes stay untouched.
- **Install.** "Install Java N" installs the managed runtime a host expects, within its loader's update ceiling. It works even with automatic downloads off. It never pins the runtime; when the host would not pick it up on its own, a previewed pin is offered. The CLI equivalent is `ephervex java install --instance/--server`.
- **Failure explanations.** A launch or start refused before the JVM runs names the runtime it tried, how that runtime was chosen (automatically, pinned by the host, pinned by the launcher preference, or given for this run), what the host expected, and the mismatch or probe failure. A JVM that exits with `UnsupportedClassVersionError` is explained with the class, the Java it needs, and the runtime. Both the GUI and the CLI show this.
- **Settings > Java** shows each runtime's architecture and every instance, server and launcher preference that pins it. Removing a pinned managed runtime lists those settings before you confirm.
- **Freshness.** The cached inventory catches up with the managed store when a launch, a start or another process installs or removes a runtime there, probing only the managed store. Shown hosts read their Java again after a launch, start, creation, import or loader change.
- **Server parity.** The CLI gains `server runtime`, `java select --server` and `java install --server`. Server diagnosis reads committed server metadata.
- **Docs.** ADR 0046 records the decisions. There is a new "Java runtime selection" section in `docs/architecture.md` and a README feature bullet.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` pass on the tip (4957 passed, 0 failed).

pulls.bodyMarkdown:
## What changes

Ephervex now dresses up for Halloween. From **October 25 through October 31**, by the computer's local date, a Halloween theme replaces Dark or Light. It uses near-black and deep purple with pumpkin orange and gold, and the pumpkin-ghost mascot as the logo and window icon.

- The Halloween theme is an easter egg. It is not in the theme list, cannot be chosen or recorded, and a theme file cannot name it as its `parent`.
- One Halloween palette stands in for both Dark and Light. A user's own theme is never replaced.
- A new **Settings > General > Seasonal themes** switch, on by default, turns it off. The chosen Dark or Light then shows straight away. The switch's description names no dates. While the season is on, the card says which theme is shown and which one comes back.
- The recorded theme is never changed. The theme the season shows is worked out again from the recorded theme, the switch and the local date each time the settings are read. Dark or Light therefore comes back on November 1, also after a restart.
- While Ephervex stays open, the local date is checked once a minute. Settings are read again only when the new date changes the theme that should be shown, at most once per date, so the theme changes once at each boundary and does not flicker.
- The seasons live in one table in `ephervex_core::seasonal_theme` (ADR 0049). Adding another season is a `SeasonalTheme` value, its days, a palette, its branding and its name. Nothing else checks dates.
- The Interface theme card now only says "The colors Ephervex paints itself in. Minecraft is unaffected."; the themes folder path is still named in the theme problems dialog.

## Colors

The palette follows the website's dark Halloween look on `feature/web-docs` (#381): background `#1b1221`, surface `#281b2f`, raised surface `#322239`, border `#604258`, bars `#1d1124`, accent `#ffb86e`, buttons `#ffae60` / `#ffc47d` with `#2b172c` captions, and text `#f3e8e3` / `#d3bfc9`.

Where the site has no matching color, new ones were added:

- warning `#f5cf5b` (golden yellow)
- danger `#f46c82`, slightly lighter so it stays readable on a selected card
- success `#79cf8e` and server `#c39bf0`
- six group tones

The Modrinth, CurseForge, vanilla, Forge and NeoForge marks are Dark's.

## Mascot

The mascot is `upscaled_logos_x4/allay_halloween_5016x5016.png`, scaled down to 620 x 620 (the size of the default logo) and compiled in at `assets/themes/halloween.png`. It goes through the same bounded decoder as theme-folder branding, and nothing is read from disk for it.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace`
- New tests cover:
  - the October 24/25 and October 31/November 1 boundaries over several years
  - Dark and Light both being replaced, and user themes being kept
  - turning the switch off, in season and after a restart
  - the recorded theme never being written by a season
  - the once-per-date check at midnight
  - readable text, captions and switches on every Halloween surface
  - the mascot shown as logo and icon, with a theme folder of the same name ignored
  - the Halloween theme missing from the theme list and refused as a `parent`
- Checked by hand in the desktop app with the date set to October 28: Light was replaced by the Halloween theme and logo, the switch brought Light back, and the setting was saved.

## Limitations

- The window icon changes on X11. On Wayland, and in docks that match Ephervex to its desktop entry, the installed icon stays, as for every theme.
- Someone who chose Dark or Light sees the season unless they turn Seasonal themes off.

pulls.bodyMarkdown:
## Problem

#12 still needed two things:
- marking server settings that only take effect after a restart;
- showing a server's address and port next to its identity.

The Properties tab also covered only a handful of `server.properties` keys, and there was no way to give new servers the same settings.

## Changes

Three commits:

1. **Save while running** (#12).
   - Gameplay properties can be saved while the server runs under Ephervex. The server keeps running, and nothing restarts it.
   - Changed values are written to `server.properties` straight away and kept in `.launcher/server-properties-pending.json`. The supervisor writes them again right before every start or restart, so a server that writes its own copy back (for example on `/whitelist on`) cannot lose them.
   - "Restart required" shows in the header, on the Overview and in Properties until a new process has read the values.
   - Network settings stay stopped-only, because they are the linked client's connection target.
   - The header shows the address and port next to the name.
   - The CLI reports restart-required in `server properties set` and in `server status`.
   - ADR 0050.
2. **Properties tab rework.**
   - A typed catalog of most `server.properties` keys lives in `ephervex-server`. It records each key's group, type, accepted range or choices, and vanilla default.
   - Core validates catalog values from both the GUI and the CLI. Keys outside the catalog keep what the file holds, and remote admin (RCON, query, JMX) is not offered.
   - The tab shows grouped cards (World, Gameplay, Players, Performance, and Advanced behind a toggle), each row with a short description.
   - Rows show changed values, an inline validation error, and a per-row restart tag. A bottom bar counts unsaved changes and offers Discard and Save.
   - `level-type` is free text.
   - Once a server's file lists every key its release writes, keys that release does not read are hidden.
   - Choices are written as their position, which every release reads.
3. **Global defaults.**
   - A new Settings > Server Properties page with the same cards.
   - Defaults are a sparse set of catalog values, written into a new server's `server.properties` for keys it does not hold, at creation or first install.
   - Values from a pack's server files stay, and existing servers are never changed.
   - Stored defaults this build cannot interpret are kept and skipped rather than failing creation.
   - ADR 0051.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` pass on the pushed head.
- New tests cover:
  - kept values and the supervisor re-applying them on restart;
  - core saves while running and while stopped;
  - catalog validation;
  - the form's drafts, rows and version filtering;
  - the defaults form and its save;
  - the defaults fill at creation;
  - GUI wiring for both pages.
- Layout checked with headless screenshots, including DejaVu-only fonts at narrow width.
- Every commit went through independent review rounds until it passed.
- A manual review AppImage was tested. The Properties tab and the Settings page look right.

## Limitations

- An edit made to `server.properties` outside Ephervex, while saved values are kept, is overwritten for those keys at the next start.
- A setting the server changes itself after the user saved that same setting is set back to the saved value at the next start.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Closes #12

## Problem

#13 had three gaps left:

- A pane of a split workspace had no way to open its host's folder. Only the single-pane header had Open Folder.
- The crash notice on a server's Overview offered only "Review mods". It had no way to the crash report, the log, or Diagnostics once the failed-run notice was dismissed, or after Ephervex restarted.
- The same host state was drawn in a different color depending on where it was shown. A failed server was gray in the pane header but amber on the Servers list, and an orphaned client was gray in one place and amber in another.

## Change

- **Split pane folder:** the compact header's tab row has a folder button, labeled Open Instance Folder or Open Server Folder for the pane's own host. On hover it and the split and close buttons name only their action; screen readers still hear which pane they belong to. To fit it at the smallest window, the tabs shrink toward a new `Theme.workspace-tab-min-width` token when two full-width tabs do not fit, and tab labels elide.
- **Crash notice routes:** on the server Overview the notice now also offers Open Diagnostics, Open crash report (opens that report in Logs), and Open log, on one row or two depending on width. Beside the mods it adds Open crash report. While the failed-run notice above it already offers these, the crash notice leaves them out, so each route appears once. A start refused for missing EULA consent offers only the EULA, so the crash notice keeps its routes then.
- **One state tone:** a new `StateTone` global and `StatePill` component carry the mapping every host state pill now uses: running green, failed red, starting, stopping, restarting, orphaned, unknown and needs recovery amber, and anything else quiet. The pair badge keeps its accent for a settled counterpart.
- `docs/architecture.md` describes the header folder, the state tone and the crash notice routes.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace` (5316 passed) all pass.
- New GUI tests:
  - each split pane's folder button opens its own host's folder
  - the tab row stays inside the pane at the smallest window
  - each crash notice route reaches the right surface, log mode and report
  - the routes are left to the failed-run notice when it is shown, and kept beside a refused start
  - a split pane's glyph buttons name only their action on hover
  - the notice stays inside its pane at the smallest split, at text scale 1.0 and 1.5

## What changes

**Shell and navigation**
- Three columns: instances and servers on the left, the page in the middle, a column of cards on the right. Narrow windows turn the side columns into drawers.
- Home with running, attention, resume and activity cards, plus a right column with storage counts, cache usage and tips.
- Host list cards with a state strip, a state square, problem badge, favorite star and a quick view button.
- Host pages with a header band, a status stamp (Running, Needs fix, ...), chips, an editable issue link and keyboard-reachable tabs. Split panes keep their model.

**Host pages**
- Run card, linked servers, report card (copyable summary), diagnostic bundle card and storage card in the side column.
- Case tab: steps, a note and the reproduced count. Stored in the organization file and available as `ephervex instance case`.
- Mods: one table with a filter, "Add jars" and an "Add mods" dialog that holds the catalog browser.
- Logs: a dark console with level chips and counts, search, a follow button and tinted error rows.
- Diagnostics: a result banner, problem cards with the likely cause called out, Java runtime cards, a "valid, customized" table and a checked list.
- Quick view: a slide-over (or fullscreen) of any host's surfaces, opened from a list card or the Run card, without changing the page underneath.
- "What happened": a bounded per-host history (ADR 0058) shown as a timeline in the Case tab and listed by `ephervex instance case <id> history`.

**Dialogs and Settings**
- New Instance and New Server follow the reference: segmented loader and storage choices, an optional linked server (port, accounts, server pack), delete with two cards.
- Settings has a category rail, grouped cards and a draft bar for unsaved changes. Includes a default server port and a default account mode for linked servers.

**Themes and icons**
- Workbench is the built-in look, in a light and a dark palette (ADR 0057). Light is the default, Dark is selectable, and `light` and `dark` stay valid in configuration files and as a theme file's `parent`.
- The seasonal themes (Halloween, Christmas, Pride Month, April Fools) are back on the new look and stand in for the chosen built-in theme during their season (ADR 0049). Settings > General > Seasonal themes turns them off and is offered only while a season is on. `SEASONS_THEME=<name>` previews one.
- The interface icons are redrawn in a whiteboard marker style: round, slightly bowed strokes in one theme color, 24-unit viewBox, stroke 2.4.
- Fonts: Pixelify Sans, Space Grotesk and IBM Plex Mono are bundled and listed in the licenses.

## Notes for review

- Quick view fullscreen shows the normal surfaces at full width, not the reference's two-column composition.
- A client run or server run that outlives the launcher's process records its start but not its end in the history (documented in ADR 0058).
- The Minecraft defaults rows build on #635: text and editor columns from about 780 px with the editor against a fixed Reset slot (disabled when nothing is overridden), and two columns of rows side by side on very wide pages. The Settings rebuild restyles the borders.
- `main` was merged in twice while this was in progress (sign-in code dialog, Minecraft split rows, server statistics); those features are mounted in the new shell.
- Not visually signed off yet; screenshots from the reference were compared during development.

## Checks

`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` pass locally.
